items.title: Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examined how machine learning is being applied to wastewater-based surveillance for detecting and monitoring emerging pathogens at the community level. The authors conducted a narrative review of the published literature, classifying methods into four tiers spanning classical statistical models through deep learning and hybrid mechanistic approaches, and evaluated evidence across five analytical tasks including forecasting, anomaly detection, and decision support. They found that the evidence base is heavily concentrated on a single pathogen, with most analytical work focused on SARS-CoV-2, and that the strongest early-warning evidence came from simpler classical statistical methods rather than more complex machine learning approaches. Reported performance was highly context-dependent, and most combinations of method and surveillance task remain prospective rather than validated in real-world settings. The authors conclude that broader application requires standardized collaborative frameworks, multimodal data integration, mechanistic modelling with uncertainty quantification, and improved governance structures to address data quality and public acceptability barriers.
items.citation: Song A, Jia P, Luo J et al.. Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects.. Emerging microbes & infections. 2026

items.title: Multimodal genomic surveillance for respiratory pathogens at four U.S. international airports: A comparison of air, wastewater, clinical, and national surveillance data.
items.summary: This study evaluated environmental and clinical surveillance methods for detecting respiratory pathogens at major international airports, which represent high-risk settings for pathogen introduction due to dense, enclosed populations and international traveler mixing. Air samples were collected at four U.S. international airports over approximately ten months and analyzed using PCR, targeted amplicon sequencing, and targeted enrichment sequencing, then compared against aviation wastewater data, traveler nasal swab results, and national clinical surveillance. SARS-CoV-2 was detected in the vast majority of air samples, while influenza A was detected in a smaller but substantial fraction, and sequencing approaches recovered high-quality genomes for multiple respiratory viruses including influenza, bocavirus, and seasonal coronaviruses. Influenza A positivity in air samples correlated well with wastewater, nasal swab, and national surveillance signals, whereas SARS-CoV-2 air measurements did not show significant concordance across these modalities. The findings demonstrate that air sampling can serve as a complementary tool to wastewater-based surveillance at ports of entry, though its utility varies by pathogen and warrants consideration alongside other surveillance streams.
items.citation: Gratalo D, Friedman CR, Morley VJ et al.. Multimodal genomic surveillance for respiratory pathogens at four U.S. international airports: A comparison of air, wastewater, clinical, and national surveillance data.. PLOS global public health. 2026

items.title: Progress and Expansion of the National Wastewater Surveillance System, United States, 2020-2024.
items.summary: The paper examines the development and growth of the National Wastewater Surveillance System in the United States from its origins as an emergency response measure through its first four years of operation. The authors describe how the system expanded its geographic coverage, broadened the range of pathogens monitored, improved analytical and visualization tools, and refined laboratory methods over this period. Collaborations across public, private, and academic sectors were central to standardizing practices and translating wastewater signals into actionable public health responses. The paper argues that wastewater surveillance has matured from a crisis-driven initiative into an established component of public health infrastructure, demonstrating adaptability and scalability in supporting community-level threat detection and data-driven decision-making.
items.citation: Mark-Carew M, Bias M, Reckling S et al.. Progress and Expansion of the National Wastewater Surveillance System, United States, 2020-2024.. Emerging infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Cyclospora cayetanensis in Wastewater: Expanding Pathogen Targets for Regulatory Public Health Surveillance
items.citation: Lin C, Gonzalez DS, Poretsky RS. Laboratory Evaluation of Cyclospora cayetanensis in Wastewater: Expanding Pathogen Targets for Regulatory Public Health Surveillance. 2026

items.title: Wastewater metagenomic sequencing enables broad pathogen and resistome monitoring in Lagos, Nigeria
items.summary: This study investigated pathogen diversity and antimicrobial resistance in Lagos, Nigeria, using wastewater-based epidemiology to overcome the limitations of clinical surveillance systems in resource-constrained settings. The researchers performed virus-enriched metagenomic and metatranscriptomic sequencing on untreated wastewater collected from open drainage canals over a two-month period in 2024. They detected a broad and diverse human-associated virome dominated by enteric adenoviruses, astroviruses, and caliciviruses, and recovered partial and near-complete genomes from pathogens of public health concern including noroviruses, enteroviruses, and sapoviruses. Despite targeting viruses, the sequencing also revealed diverse bacterial pathogens such as Vibrio cholerae and zoonotic species like Streptococcus suis, as well as clinically important antimicrobial resistance genes including those conferring resistance to aminoglycosides, beta-lactams, and fluoroquinolones. The findings establish a regional baseline of pathogen diversity for Lagos and demonstrate that virus-enriched wastewater sequencing can serve as an integrated surveillance tool capable of simultaneously monitoring viral, bacterial, and resistance threats at the population scale.
items.citation: Parker E, Oladipo F, Levy JI et al.. Wastewater metagenomic sequencing enables broad pathogen and resistome monitoring in Lagos, Nigeria. 2026

items.title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls.
items.summary: This review examines wastewater-based surveillance as a population-level tool for monitoring viral pathogens, focusing on the sequencing strategies and bioinformatic challenges involved. The authors outline two primary sequencing approaches: targeted methods such as amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, which offer sensitive detection of known viruses but cannot identify novel pathogens, and untargeted shotgun metagenomic sequencing, which provides a broader view of the wastewater virome but is hampered by low viral abundance, complex background signals, and genome assembly difficulties. The review further identifies key bioinformatic obstacles including gaps in human viral sequence databases, co-circulating viral lineages, viral dark matter, reference database limitations, and methodological biases. The authors also highlight emerging computational approaches aimed at improving the analysis and interpretation of wastewater sequencing data, positioning the field as moving beyond simple pathogen detection toward detailed genomic characterization of circulating viruses.
items.citation: De Smedt M, Cuypers WL, Hudda NU et al.. Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls.. iScience. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the transmission rates of different SARS-CoV-2 variants co-circulating in a population. The researchers developed a statistical method that jointly combines confirmed case counts and genetic sequencing data to estimate variant-specific effective reproduction numbers and variant frequencies simultaneously, rather than relying on sequence frequency data alone. The approach also allows for inferring structured relationships between reproduction numbers over time, enabling estimation of fixed growth advantages for specific variants across different locations. Applying this method to data from United States states spanning early 2021 through early 2022, they estimated effective reproduction numbers for multiple variants of concern and interest and identified consistent growth advantages of particular variants across geographic locations. The work demonstrates that integrating case data with sequencing data captures richer epidemiological dynamics than sequence frequency data alone can provide.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: Mobile Genetic Elements as Central Drivers of Antimicrobial Resistance: Molecular Mechanisms, Evolutionary Ecology, One Health Implications and Control Strategies
items.summary: This review examines the role of mobile genetic elements in driving the global spread of antimicrobial resistance across bacterial species and ecosystems. The authors synthesized current genomic, epidemiological, and ecological research, including case studies of clinically significant resistance outbreaks, to evaluate how different classes of mobile genetic elements facilitate horizontal gene transfer of antibiotic resistance genes. The review finds that these elements act as hubs for resistance gene capture, recombination, and stabilization, enabling the emergence of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant pathogens, while ecological pressures such as heavy metals and biocides further amplify their spread through One Health transmission pathways. The authors connect these molecular mechanisms to applied intervention strategies, including genomic surveillance, mobile genetic element-targeted inhibitors, phage therapy, and CRISPR-based approaches, arguing that a mechanistic understanding of these elements is essential for designing effective antimicrobial resistance mitigation strategies.
items.citation: Hemayet Hossain, Md. Hasan Ali, Tanvir Ahmad et al.. Mobile Genetic Elements as Central Drivers of Antimicrobial Resistance: Molecular Mechanisms, Evolutionary Ecology, One Health Implications and Control Strategies. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory
items.summary: This paper examines how diverse microbial communities in soil regulate critical ecosystem processes, including nutrient cycling, carbon storage, and ecosystem resilience, while acknowledging that the links between microbial diversity and function are not yet fully understood. The authors synthesize existing soil microbiome research across ecological, agricultural, and environmental contexts using a function-centred framework. They identify four conserved functional axes — secondary metabolism, nutrient cycling, community interactions, and stress tolerance — that collectively shape ecosystem outcomes such as plant productivity, climate regulation, and pollutant transformation, though they note these functions are strongly context dependent. The authors propose that soil operates as a self-organizing system in which microbial interactions produce emergent ecosystem-level behaviour. This conceptual framework is offered as a foundation for developing predictive, ecology-informed strategies to manage soils for sustainable agriculture, environmental remediation, and climate mitigation.
items.citation: Suzanne Hassan-Dalléac, Wafa Guiga, Antonia Suau. Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory. Communications Earth & Environment. 2026

items.title: The dual role of azoles: lifesaving antifungals and drivers of resistance – a One Health perspective
items.summary: This review examines the paradoxical role of azole antifungals as both indispensable treatments for fungal diseases and contributors to the emergence of resistant pathogens. The authors analyze azole use across human medicine, veterinary care, and agriculture, exploring the mechanisms by which these compounds act against fungi and how environmental and evolutionary pressures drive resistance development. By integrating perspectives from microbiology, agriculture, and public health, the review highlights how widespread cross-sector deployment of azoles threatens human health, food security, and ecosystem stability. The authors argue that the convergence of these pressures demands a coordinated One Health stewardship approach, combining surveillance and sustainable antifungal strategies to preserve the long-term efficacy of this critical class of compounds.
items.citation: Behrad Roohi, Joel D. A. Tyndall, Thomas Svoboda et al.. The dual role of azoles: lifesaving antifungals and drivers of resistance – a One Health perspective. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Beyond the visible: metal-ion-doped inorganic UV phosphors for advanced photonics
items.summary: This review examines inorganic ultraviolet luminescent materials doped with metal ions, including rare-earth and heavy main-group metal ions, which display distinctive electronic transitions, tunable emission, and strong photostability. The authors systematically survey three principal luminescence modes—persistent luminescence, upconversion luminescence, and mechanoluminescence—organizing their analysis by dominant emission mechanism and supplementing it with spectral classifications. The review covers underlying luminescence mechanisms, recent advances in material design, and optimization strategies for each mode. Applications spanning optoelectronics, environmental remediation, and biomedicine are analyzed under the principle that material performance should guide application selection. The paper concludes by identifying key challenges and outlining future research directions to advance the broader field of inorganic ultraviolet phosphors.
items.citation: Yu Zhang, Yanjie Liang, Feng Liu et al.. Beyond the visible: metal-ion-doped inorganic UV phosphors for advanced photonics. Light Science & Applications. 2026

items.title: Pharmaceuticals in Water: Fate, Health Risks, Treatment and Governance for Sustainable Management
items.summary: This review examines the presence, behavior, and management of pharmaceutical compounds as emerging contaminants in aquatic environments, addressing their journey from production and consumption through to environmental persistence. The authors synthesize current evidence on the occurrence, fate, transport, and removal of major drug classes—including antibiotics, anti-inflammatory drugs, antidepressants, hormones, and beta-blockers—across freshwater and related aquatic systems. Despite occurring at trace concentrations, these substances are shown to pose potential ecological and human health risks through diverse biological mechanisms even at low exposure levels. Current and emerging water treatment technologies are critically assessed alongside existing regulatory and governance frameworks. The paper proposes an integrated management framework linking lifecycle thinking, advanced treatment approaches, and adaptive regulatory governance to guide future research, policy, and sustainable protection of drinking-water resources.
items.citation: Asvinidevi Arumugam, Khai Ern Lee, Pei Yuen Ng et al.. Pharmaceuticals in Water: Fate, Health Risks, Treatment and Governance for Sustainable Management. Water Air & Soil Pollution. 2026

items.title: OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit
items.summary: This paper investigated a microlensing event exhibiting two short-lived brightness bumps separated by over eight years in survey data spanning more than a decade, seeking to determine whether such long-baseline signals could reveal extremely wide-orbit binary lens systems. The researchers cross-matched microlensing event catalogs from two major surveys and evaluated three competing physical interpretations for the light curve morphology: a binary-lens single-source model, a single-lens binary-source model, and two entirely unrelated microlensing events. After ruling out the latter two scenarios on statistical and photometric grounds, the binary-lens interpretation was favored, revealing a mass ratio consistent with a low-mass brown dwarf or super-Jupiter companion orbiting a primary M dwarf host. The inferred projected separation of the companion makes it the widest low-mass object discovered through microlensing to date, demonstrating that current wide-field surveys can detect companions at hundreds of astronomical units. The authors note that while future space-based observatories will improve sensitivity to such systems, distinguishing genuine wide-orbit binaries from confounding variable phenomena will remain a critical challenge for statistical studies of this population.
items.citation: Hongjing Yang, Weicheng Zang, Yoon-Hyun Ryu et al.. OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale census of emission-line galaxies using JWST's NIRCam wide-field slitless spectroscopy from the COSMOS-3D program, covering a substantial contiguous sky area with grism spectroscopy spanning a specific infrared wavelength range. The study combined slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging to build a homogeneous spectroscopic catalog of over twelve thousand galaxies spanning redshifts from essentially the present day out to the early universe, reaching very faint emission-line flux limits. To overcome the source confusion that is inherent to slitless spectroscopy, the team developed a multi-step identification framework that incorporated convolutional neural networks and large language models to emulate and accelerate the human identification process. The resulting catalog captures a wide variety of emission lines—including oxygen, hydrogen recombination series, helium, sulfur, iron, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon features—enabling continuous tracing of star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across cosmic time. Composite spectra constructed in multiple redshift bins also revealed faint spectral features such as higher-order hydrogen lines, CO absorption bands, and iron lines that are undetectable in individual spectra, demonstrating the broad utility of wide-field slitless spectroscopy for large, unbiased galaxy surveys.
items.citation: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al.. A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations
items.summary: This paper investigates the fundamental limits of covert communication within a queueing framework, where an operator attempts to serve hidden jobs alongside legitimate traffic without detection by the legitimate user. The system is modeled as an M/M/1-type queue, with the legitimate user monitoring busy-period statistics—either the number of jobs served or the duration of each busy period—to detect anomalous activity. The authors prove that a square-root law governs the maximum number of covert jobs that can be served: over a given number of busy periods, the covert throughput can scale at most as the square root of that number, and any faster scaling allows the legitimate user to detect the covert traffic with vanishing error probability. Beyond establishing this square-root law for both statistics, the paper characterizes the precise scaling constant, termed the covert queueing constant, for each observational statistic. A comparison of the two statistics reveals that monitoring the number of jobs served is a more powerful detection tool than monitoring busy-period duration, as it affords the legitimate user a strictly tighter constraint on covert activity.
items.citation: Anumula Venkata Sai Sree Sahithi, Arti Yardi, Jithin Ravi. Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection
items.summary: This paper investigated how adverse weather, specifically snow, affects LiDAR-based object detection in autonomous driving systems. Using two benchmark datasets, the researchers conducted a granular evaluation and discovered a counter-intuitive result: detection accuracy tends to improve as snow intensity increases, rather than degrading as commonly assumed. Through ablation studies and meta-information analysis, they found that while falling snow does introduce atmospheric noise that harms performance, this effect is outweighed by a concurrent increase in the number of point cloud returns from detected objects. The authors hypothesize that snow accumulation on vehicle surfaces enlarges their effective geometric profile and shifts reflectance from specular to diffuse, both of which enhance detection. They conclude that evaluating perception systems using coarse weather-severity categories without controlling for correlated object-level factors can produce misleading assessments of detector robustness, and call for future work to formally decouple atmospheric noise from surface accumulation effects.
items.citation: Yiming Yang, Jeremy P. Bos. Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting wheel tracks on snow-covered roads, where following existing tracks provides traction, stability, and path predictability benefits that general traversability methods fail to capture. The authors developed a self-supervised approach that fuses RGB imagery with long-wave infrared (thermal) imaging, using synchronized GNSS data to automatically generate training labels by projecting future wheel trajectories without manual annotation. A neural network was trained on the resulting four-channel RGB-thermal images to identify wheel tracks on visually featureless, white-out road surfaces. The method was validated experimentally, demonstrating robust detection in adverse winter conditions, and the authors released a new dataset called ThermalTrack to support further research in this domain.
items.citation: Yiming Yang, Jeremy P. Bos. Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ask Your Advisor: Learning When to Consult Stronger Models in Agentic Systems
items.summary: This paper investigates how to optimally decide when a weaker AI agent should seek help from a stronger, more expensive model during complex task execution. The authors developed ARIA, a meta-controller that frames consultation decisions as a sequential resource-allocation problem, learning at workflow contact points whether to remain silent or request advice based on execution evidence mapped to a compact state representation. Action values are learned through Monte Carlo control using cost-penalized outcomes, allowing the system to balance task success against the computational expense of consulting the stronger model. Evaluated across three agentic benchmarks involving software engineering and terminal-based tasks, ARIA recovers a substantial portion of the performance gap between using only the weaker model versus always using the stronger model, at less than half the advisor model's cost. ARIA outperforms a range of alternative strategies including routing, cascading, fixed consultation schedules, and random advice placement, while remaining interpretable and controllable through a single consultation-price parameter that adjusts the success-cost trade-off without retraining either underlying model.
items.citation: Pascal Sowietzki, Steffen Holter, Yannick Metz et al.. Ask Your Advisor: Learning When to Consult Stronger Models in Agentic Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid – based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing beyond conventional laboratory settings. The authors systematically surveyed the field across three operational stages: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. Extraction strategies reviewed include magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic approaches, with emphasis on simplicity, portability, and equipment-free operation. Amplification methods such as PCR, NASBA, RPA, and LAMP were assessed for their adaptation to low-power and portable conditions, while detection platforms ranged from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensors employing CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch principles. The review concludes that these combined innovations are advancing point-of-care nucleic acid diagnostics toward highly sensitive, selective, programmable, and economically viable tools for infectious disease identification.
items.citation: Hossam Hatem, Mohamed Mysara, Raghda Ramadan. Trends of nucleic acid – based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases. Journal of Biological Engineering. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The study addressed the need for improved diagnostic tools to detect *Schistosoma mansoni* infection in its intermediate snail hosts, which is critical for controlling and eliminating schistosomiasis. Researchers developed a novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of *S. mansoni*, optimized under simple isothermal conditions, and evaluated its performance against conventional parasitological and molecular methods using both laboratory-infected snails and field-collected samples from two African countries. The new assay achieved complete specificity and high sensitivity in laboratory settings, outperforming microscopy and performing comparably to real-time PCR, while in field surveys it detected a higher proportion of infected snails than conventional PCR and identified infections entirely missed by parasitological examination. These results indicate that the assay is a sensitive, specific, and practically deployable tool suitable for routine surveillance of snail infection and early detection of changes in schistosomiasis transmission.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Development of a rapid LAMP assay toward point-of-care detection of dermatophyte infections and antifungal resistance.
items.summary: The paper addressed the need for rapid, accessible diagnostics for dermatophyte fungal infections and the antifungal resistance that increasingly complicates their treatment. The researchers developed and validated a suite of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assays targeting taxonomic identification at multiple levels—pan-dermatophyte, genus, and species complex—as well as competitive SNP-based LAMP assays designed to detect single-nucleotide polymorphisms associated with terbinafine resistance, using unmodified self-stabilizing primers to improve specificity. The taxonomic assays achieved detection within minutes at a single temperature with low limits of detection and were compatible with simple colorimetric readout, while the resistance assays successfully differentiated wild-type from mutant alleles in clinical isolates. Together, the assays constitute a proof-of-concept point-of-care diagnostic platform that could enable rapid species identification and resistance profiling without laboratory infrastructure. The authors propose that this platform could support targeted antifungal treatment and stewardship efforts, particularly in resource-limited settings where dermatophyte infections are prevalent but diagnostics are scarce.
items.citation: Wunderlich G, Butterly S, Johnson M et al.. Development of a rapid LAMP assay toward point-of-care detection of dermatophyte infections and antifungal resistance.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize, as it contains only a report citation reference and a note about corrections, with no scientific content described.
items.citation: V. Kotov. Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package. Dokumentenrepositorium der RUB (Ruhr University Bochum). 2026

items.title: The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods
items.summary: This study investigated whether Raman spectroscopy could reliably distinguish natural gemstones from their laboratory-grown synthetic counterparts, focusing on ruby, sapphire, emerald, and spinel. The researchers evaluated both a laboratory Raman spectrometer equipped with two different lasers and a portable Raman system, testing their ability to identify gem origin and differentiate between stones produced by various manufacturing methods. The laboratory instrument successfully determined the geographic or synthetic origin of gemstones and could differentiate natural from synthetic specimens, with the dual-laser configuration proving essential since emerald analysis required the shorter wavelength laser. The portable system could distinguish between different stone types but lacked the sensitivity needed to separate natural from synthetic gems. Measurements were confirmed as reliable through repetitive testing, with Raman band positions falling within an acceptable margin of the reference values reported in the literature.
items.citation: Raabell Shah. The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods. Research Output (Edinburgh Napier University). 2026

items.title: Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses
items.summary: This study investigated the viral diversity carried by synanthropic urban bats in Brazil as a strategy for identifying potential zoonotic threats. The researchers developed a framework that integrates existing rabies passive surveillance infrastructure with nanopore metagenomic sequencing, applying a selection algorithm to choose representative bat specimens from a large collection across São Paulo state and sequencing paired lung and intestine samples. The approach detected viral contigs spanning multiple families of public health concern, including coronaviruses, arenaviruses, and paramyxoviruses, and notably uncovered a previously unknown filovirus in bats from the Americas. These results demonstrate that substantial undetected viral diversity circulates in bat populations and that repurposing existing animal surveillance systems can serve as an efficient and cost-effective tool for pathogen monitoring. A multisectoral One Health workshop validated the framework as a scalable model suitable for national expansion and applicable to low- and middle-income countries.
items.citation: Juliana Amorim Conselheiro, Filipe Romero Rebello Moreira, Gisely Toledo Barone et al.. Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses. One Health. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review paper examines hantaviruses as emerging rodent-borne pathogens responsible for two serious disease syndromes — hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome — in the context of a rapidly changing global environment. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and surveillance, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and land-use transformation drive shifts in rodent reservoir populations and increase spillover risk to humans. Special focus is given to surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is thought to be underrecognized. The review also discusses advances in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, vaccine development, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems as tools for improving outbreak response. The authors conclude that integrated One Health surveillance combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring — alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration — is essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and preparing for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV): Advances in Diagnosis, Molecular Epidemiology, and Clinical Impact of an Underrecognized Respiratory Virus
items.summary: This review examines human metapneumovirus, a respiratory pathogen first identified in the early 2000s that causes illness ranging from mild upper respiratory infections to severe pneumonia. The paper synthesizes recent literature on the virus's epidemiology, molecular virology, and clinical characteristics, with particular attention to vulnerable populations including immunocompromised individuals, the elderly, and young infants, while also addressing evidence that healthy adults face greater risk than previously assumed. The authors highlight that children appear disproportionately susceptible to infection compared to adults. The review emphasizes that HMPV represents an underrecognized contributor to respiratory morbidity and calls for improved diagnostic tools and stronger public health measures to address the burden of this pathogen.
items.citation: ‏Helal F. Hetta, Rehab Ahmed, Abdul Haseeb et al.. Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV): Advances in Diagnosis, Molecular Epidemiology, and Clinical Impact of an Underrecognized Respiratory Virus. Diagnostics. 2026

items.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale spectroscopic survey of emission-line galaxies using JWST's NIRCam wide-field slitless spectroscopy mode as part of the COSMOS-3D program, covering a substantial contiguous sky area with grism spectroscopy spanning a specific mid-infrared wavelength range. The study constructed a homogeneous sample of over twelve thousand galaxies spanning redshifts from zero to nine by combining slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging, and developed a novel multi-step source identification framework that incorporates convolutional neural networks and large language models to address the source confusion inherent to slitless spectroscopy. The survey detects a wide range of emission lines—including oxygen, hydrogen recombination, helium, sulfur, iron, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon features—enabling continuous galaxy census across cosmic time. Stacked composite spectra in multiple redshift bins revealed faint spectral features such as higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and iron emission lines that are undetectable in individual spectra. The resulting catalog, providing spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties, is presented as a key reference dataset for studying galaxy evolution, star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across a wide redshift baseline.
items.citation: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al.. A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates sub-volume sampling strategies in self-supervised learning for three-dimensional medical images, arguing that the conventional practice of random cropping is a previously overlooked bottleneck. The authors first demonstrate through controlled experiments that crop quality directly influences downstream transfer performance, motivating a reframing of sub-volume selection as a "where-to-look" problem. They propose a plug-and-play framework that replaces random cropping with an offline coarse-to-fine probe bank designed to balance anatomy-awareness, informativeness, and diversity, instantiated in both a lightweight variant using geometric and image-statistical cues and a diagnostic variant using frozen visual features. Extensive experiments across multiple backbone architectures and downstream tasks show that the lightweight variant consistently outperforms random sampling. Mechanistic analyses attribute the gains to more anatomically plausible and informative crops, reduced spatial redundancy, improved learning dynamics, and more structured learned representations.
items.citation: Junkai Liu, Le Zhang. Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: How Social Reinforcement Shapes Word-of-Mouth: A Conviction-Based Model for Marketing Diffusion and Network Targeting
items.summary: This paper examines how the strength of social reinforcement experienced at the moment of product adoption shapes consumers' subsequent willingness to advocate for that product, a mechanism largely ignored in existing diffusion models. The authors introduce the Pressure Threshold model, a conviction-based diffusion framework in which an individual's persuasive influence on others increases with the cumulative social pressure they experienced when adopting. Using this framework, they analyze optimal marketing targeting and seeding strategies, finding that accounting for conviction formation shifts focus toward consumers embedded in cohesive, densely connected network regions where repeated social exposure can amplify downstream word-of-mouth. They demonstrate that scalable heuristics remain effective for the resulting optimization problem and that social reinforcement substantially boosts the effectiveness of seeding interventions, especially in clustered network environments. Validation against real-world time-stamped social media cascades confirms that the model improves predictive accuracy over standard diffusion approaches, supporting the empirical relevance of conviction-driven amplification.
items.citation: Abhishek K. Umrawal, Curt Stutsman, Camille Woods et al.. How Social Reinforcement Shapes Word-of-Mouth: A Conviction-Based Model for Marketing Diffusion and Network Targeting. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Physical-state supervision for design-only Gaussian process surrogates of implosion simulations
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of building accurate surrogate models for inertial confinement fusion implosion simulations, where physical diagnostics recorded during simulation can organize a highly variable response but are unavailable at prediction time without running a new calculation. The authors developed a Gaussian process surrogate that learns to predict these physical-state diagnostics from design variables alone, using cross-fitted state estimates to augment design representations for both a global predictor and an optional mixture-of-experts model. Testing on a large database of paired one-dimensional implosion simulations, they found that incorporating learned burn-weighted physical states substantially reduced prediction error for both random holdout and design-space extrapolation compared to baselines using random projections or shuffled states. The benefits of expert specialization were found to depend on training set size and the specific design space, with experts helping at smaller budgets but adding little or even degrading accuracy at larger ones, suggesting validation-based selection is necessary. The work concludes that physical-state supervision is a valuable representation strategy for data-limited surrogates, and the authors release an open implementation along with the data and results to support reproducibility.
items.citation: Chang Liu, Hao Shen, Chuanying Li. Physical-state supervision for design-only Gaussian process surrogates of implosion simulations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language models can generate reliable unit tests for quantum software, a domain that poses unique challenges due to probabilistic outputs, numerical tolerances, and domain-specific correctness criteria. The authors developed QTestBench, a framework that evaluates LLM-generated test suites by comparing their verdicts against independent benchmark checkers rather than treating the generated tests themselves as ground truth. The framework prompts models to produce syntactic, semantic, and behavioral tests, injects candidate solutions at runtime, and assesses discrimination ability across multiple validation cohorts designed to answer distinct diagnostic questions. Testing five large language models on quantum programming challenges from two frameworks, the study found that while generated test suites almost always execute successfully, their ability to distinguish correct from faulty implementations is substantially weaker, with the best-performing model reaching a test quality score well below ceiling on one benchmark and considerably lower on the other. The work also demonstrates that oracle-verified synthetic mutants can stabilize bug-detection estimates when naturally occurring faulty solutions are scarce, offering a reproducible benchmark for assessing the trustworthiness of LLM-generated quantum tests.
items.citation: Meriem Terki, Nouhaila Innan, Minghao Shao et al.. QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
items.summary: This paper addresses a limitation of Gaussian process solvers for linear partial differential equations: while these solvers produce posterior distributions conditioned on equality information such as residuals and boundary data, they cannot enforce inequality constraints like nonnegativity, monotonicity, or no-arbitrage conditions. The authors prove that jointly conditioning a Gaussian process prior on linear equality observations and a finite-dimensional inequality event is mathematically equivalent to sequential conditioning, establishing that the physics-informed posterior serves as a valid prior for a subsequent inequality update. The resulting combined distribution is non-Gaussian but remains tractable through truncated-Gaussian moment calculations, requiring no modification to either the PDE conditioning or inequality update steps. The approach was evaluated on a Poisson equation benchmark, financial option-price surfaces, and air-quality fields, demonstrating substantial error reductions and improved constraint satisfaction across varied data regimes. The framework reframes admissibility constraints as genuine conditioning information rather than a post-processing correction, integrating physical and structural prior knowledge directly into probabilistic PDE solvers.
items.citation: Boyuan Deng, Kshitiz Upadhyay, Michael Shields. Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints. arXiv. 2026
