items.citation: Hou W, Li X, Li J et al.. Paper-Based Biosensor Using Dual-Recognition Molecules for Detection of <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> in Milk.. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities
items.summary: This study investigated peptide-based low-molecular-weight hydrogels incorporating DNA nucleobases, known as nucleopeptides, to understand how combining electrostatic and nucleobase-pairing interactions influences hydrogel properties. The researchers synthesized six nucleopeptides derived from two complementary peptide sequences — one negatively charged and one positively charged at physiological pH — each functionalized with one of the four DNA nucleobases introduced via a peptide nucleic acid moiety. Using a systematic multiscale approach, they examined how charge complementarity and nucleobase-pair complementarity, individually and in combination, affect mechanical and physicochemical properties including gelation time, stiffness, sol-gel transition temperature, stress resistance, and fibrillar network morphology. The findings demonstrate that careful selection of complementary components allows fine-tuning of hydrogel properties, while also revealing unexpected behaviors that highlight the complexity of these bioinspired multicomponent systems. Overall, the work underscores the potential of nucleopeptide-based multicomponent hydrogels as versatile, high-performance supramolecular materials for biomedical and biotechnological applications.
items.citation: Tristan Giraud, Marine Koch, Paul Hoschtettler et al.. Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities. ACS Materials Au. 2026

items.title: Self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) and circular RNA (circRNA) vaccines: Progress, evidence gaps, and translational pathways for durable and scalable immunization
items.summary: This review examines two next-generation RNA vaccine platforms — self-amplifying RNA and circular RNA — as alternatives to conventional non-replicating mRNA vaccines. Self-amplifying RNA uses an encoded replicase to amplify intracellular RNA, achieving high antigen expression at lower doses, while circular RNA's covalently closed structure resists enzymatic degradation and enables sustained, cap-independent translation. The authors integrate clinical, animal, and mechanistic evidence across both platforms, noting a substantial asymmetry in maturity: self-amplifying RNA has advanced through human trials including late-phase evaluation of COVID-19 vaccines and has received regulatory authorization in some jurisdictions, whereas circular RNA vaccines remain predominantly preclinical. To guide cross-platform development, the review proposes a "3D" framework organized around durability, dose-sparing, and deployability, and identifies critical barriers including delivery system design, innate immune sensing, and manufacturing and chemistry controls. The authors conclude by mapping translational pathways needed to enable robust comparison and broader deployment of these modalities for durable and scalable immunization.
items.citation: Ugwu Okechukwu Paul-Chima, Michael Ben Okon, Ogenyi Fabian C. et al.. Self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) and circular RNA (circRNA) vaccines: Progress, evidence gaps, and translational pathways for durable and scalable immunization. Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined CRISPR-Cas systems as potential alternatives to conventional antibiotics in the context of rising multidrug-resistant bacterial infections. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental evidence on how different CRISPR effectors, primarily Cas9 alongside Cas12 and Cas13, can be deployed to kill resistant bacteria or restore antibiotic sensitivity through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid curing, and RNA-targeted cleavage. Delivery platforms evaluated included bacteriophages, conjugative plasmids, and nanoparticles, with phage-mediated delivery showing the most reliable efficacy across complex environments and animal models. The review found broad support for CRISPR-Cas antimicrobials as a precision approach to combating resistance, and noted that one CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has progressed to clinical evaluation. Nevertheless, significant translational barriers persist, including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient long-term safety data, with the authors concluding that optimized delivery systems, multiplex targeting, and standardized regulatory frameworks will be essential before clinical adoption.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Advancing Fruit Quality Monitoring with Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Non-Destructive Technologies
items.summary: This review paper examines how artificial intelligence can be integrated with non-destructive sensing technologies to improve fruit quality monitoring across pre- and postharvest stages. The authors surveyed a broad range of sensing modalities, including spectroscopic, imaging, and sensor-based systems, and evaluated how traditional machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid models have been applied to tasks such as ripeness classification and bruise detection. The review also assessed deployment considerations including real-time processing, edge AI, and multimodal data fusion. AI-driven approaches were found to achieve high accuracy in quality assessment tasks while substantially reducing postharvest losses, though persistent challenges include sensor costs, model fragility under real-world field conditions, and the absence of standardized protocols. The authors identify explainable AI, IoT-enabled digital twins, and autonomous agri-robotics as key future directions, emphasizing that realizing AI's transformative potential in this domain will require interdisciplinary collaboration and scalable implementation strategies.
items.citation: Ying Fu, Da‐Wen Sun. Advancing Fruit Quality Monitoring with Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Non-Destructive Technologies. Food Engineering Reviews. 2026

items.title: Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation
items.summary: This review examined the microbial ecosystems underlying traditional fermented foods, focusing on the challenge that spontaneous fermentation introduces variability in quality and safety that hinders industrial standardization. The authors surveyed how multi-omics approaches can be integrated to comprehensively characterize microbial community composition, dynamics, metabolite production, microbial interactions, and phage activity. They also summarized strategies for artificially regulating these ecosystems, including the use of functional starter strains, synthetic microbial communities, bacteriophage manipulation, and physicochemical environmental controls. The review concludes by outlining future directions and outstanding challenges in transitioning traditional fermentation from empirical, artisanal practice toward predictable and scalable industrial production.
items.citation: M T Wu, Yi-Xiang Wang, Yu Wang et al.. Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation. npj Science of Food. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning as a privacy-preserving approach to training artificial intelligence models across diverse healthcare data modalities, including biomedical imaging, electronic health records, wearable sensor outputs, and clinical decision support systems. The authors conducted a broad literature review spanning multiple healthcare domains to assess how federated learning enables multi-institutional AI model training without transferring raw patient data, instead sharing only model updates between collaborating sites. The paper finds that while federated learning substantially reduces direct exposure of sensitive clinical data and improves alignment with privacy regulations, confidentiality is not guaranteed and requires additional protections against threats such as gradient leakage, model inversion, and membership inference attacks. The review also identifies significant practical barriers to deployment, including system heterogeneity across institutions, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and fairness concerns. Drawing on both research findings and practical experience, the authors offer actionable guidance for regulators, developers, and healthcare systems aimed at advancing safe, equitable, and geographically distributed federated learning in medicine.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit
items.summary: This paper investigated a microlensing event, OGLE-2016-BLG-0523, identified through cross-matching survey data spanning over a decade as a candidate for hosting a very wide-orbit binary lens. The researchers analyzed a light curve exhibiting two short-lived brightness bumps separated by more than eight years, evaluating three possible interpretations: a binary-lens single-source, a single-lens binary-source, and two entirely unrelated microlensing events. After ruling out the latter two scenarios based on poorer data fits, implausible source fluxes, and low event rates, the binary-lens interpretation was favored, revealing a mass ratio between the two lensing bodies consistent with a low-mass M dwarf primary hosting a brown dwarf or super-Jupiter companion. Bayesian analysis placed the projected separation of the companion at roughly several hundred astronomical units, making it the widest low-mass object discovered through microlensing to date. The authors note that while future space-based observatories will improve sensitivity to such wide-orbit systems, distinguishing genuine binary-lens events from variable star contaminants and other degeneracies remains a critical challenge for statistical studies of wide-orbit companions.
items.citation: Hongjing Yang, Weicheng Zang, Yoon-Hyun Ryu et al.. OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale census of emission-line galaxies using JWST's near-infrared wide-field slitless spectroscopy as part of the COSMOS-3D program, covering a substantial contiguous sky area with grism spectroscopy across a mid-infrared wavelength range. The study combined slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging to build a homogeneous spectroscopic catalog spanning redshifts from zero to nine, and introduced a novel multi-step source identification framework that incorporates convolutional neural networks and large language models to handle the source confusion inherent to slitless spectroscopy. The resulting catalog provides spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties for tens of thousands of sources, detecting numerous emission lines that enable a continuous census of galaxies across cosmic time. Composite spectra constructed in multiple redshift bins reveal faint spectral features — including higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and iron lines — that are undetectable in individual spectra. The work demonstrates the power of wide-field slitless spectroscopy for assembling large, unbiased samples suited to studying galaxy evolution, star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across most of cosmic history.
items.citation: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al.. A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations
items.summary: This paper investigates the fundamental limits of covert communication within a queueing framework, where an operator attempts to secretly serve unauthorized jobs alongside legitimate traffic without detection. The setting involves a Markovian queueing system in which the legitimate user monitors summary statistics from each busy period, specifically either the number of jobs served or the busy period duration. Using hypothesis testing as the detection framework, the authors derive that the maximum number of covert jobs that can be served follows a square-root law with respect to the number of observed busy periods, consistent with square-root laws found in other covert communication settings. They further characterize the precise scaling constant of this square-root law, termed the covert queueing constant, for each of the two monitoring statistics. Comparing the two cases, they establish that observing the number of jobs served is a strictly more powerful detection statistic than observing busy period duration, as it yields a smaller covert queueing constant for the operator.
items.citation: Anumula Venkata Sai Sree Sahithi, Arti Yardi, Jithin Ravi. Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection
items.summary: This paper investigated how adverse weather, specifically snowfall, affects LiDAR-based object detection in autonomous vehicles. Using two datasets and ablation studies, the researchers analyzed detection performance across varying snow intensities while examining correlated metadata. Counter-intuitively, they found that detection accuracy improves as snow intensity increases, which they explain not as a benefit of snow itself but as a consequence of a confounding factor: snow accumulation on vehicle surfaces increases point cloud density by expanding effective surface area and shifting reflectance from specular to diffuse. The authors argue that existing evaluation frameworks conflate atmospheric noise effects with surface accumulation effects, leading to misleading conclusions about detector robustness in adverse weather. They conclude that meaningful evaluation of perception systems requires disentangling these two physically distinct phenomena rather than grouping data by broad weather-severity categories alone.
items.citation: Yiming Yang, Jeremy P. Bos. Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting wheel tracks on snow-covered roads for autonomous driving, arguing that following existing tracks provides traction and stability benefits that general traversability methods fail to exploit. The authors developed a self-supervised approach that fuses standard RGB imagery with long-wave infrared thermal imaging, using synchronized GNSS recordings to automatically generate training labels by projecting future wheel trajectories onto the image plane. A neural network was trained on the resulting four-channel RGB-thermal images to identify wheel tracks on visually featureless, white-out road surfaces without requiring manual annotation. The method was validated experimentally in adverse winter conditions, demonstrating robustness where conventional vision-based approaches struggle, and the authors also released a new dataset called ThermalTrack to support further research in this area.
items.citation: Yiming Yang, Jeremy P. Bos. Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ask Your Advisor: Learning When to Consult Stronger Models in Agentic Systems
items.summary: This paper investigates how agentic AI systems can balance task performance against computational cost by selectively consulting a stronger "advisor" model rather than relying on it throughout execution. The challenge is that the weaker "executor" model must decide when its own reasoning is insufficient, a task current language models handle poorly through self-assessment alone. The authors introduce ARIA, a meta-controller that learns consultation timing by framing the problem as a sequential resource-allocation task, mapping execution evidence to a compact state representation and choosing between remaining silent or seeking advice, with action values learned via Monte Carlo control from cost-penalized outcomes. Evaluated across several agentic benchmarks, ARIA recovers a substantial portion of the performance gap between using only the weak model and always using the strong model, while spending less than half the cost of the stronger model. ARIA outperforms a range of alternative strategies including routing, cascading, fixed consultation schedules, and random advice placement, and its policies remain compact, inspectable, and adjustable through a single cost parameter without retraining the underlying models.
items.citation: Pascal Sowietzki, Steffen Holter, Yannick Metz et al.. Ask Your Advisor: Learning When to Consult Stronger Models in Agentic Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid – based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing beyond conventional laboratory settings. The authors systematically surveyed the three core operational stages of such diagnostics: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they describe approaches including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods designed to be simple, rugged, and equipment-free. They then outline key amplification strategies—including both thermal cycling and isothermal methods—that have been adapted for portable, low-power conditions, before cataloguing detection platforms ranging from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensors employing CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch principles, which offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition.
items.citation: Hossam Hatem, Mohamed Mysara, Raghda Ramadan. Trends of nucleic acid – based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases. Journal of Biological Engineering. 2026

items.title: Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.
items.summary: This study developed and validated a multiplex real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial and mycoplasmal pathogens responsible for respiratory disease in goats. Two triplex TaqMan panels were designed, one targeting three Mycoplasma species and another targeting two Pasteurellaceae species and a Streptococcus subspecies, and the assay was evaluated for specificity, sensitivity, and reproducibility using plasmid standards and nucleic acids from both target and non-target organisms. The assay demonstrated high specificity with no cross-reactivity against non-target pathogens, low detection limits, and excellent reproducibility with low coefficients of variation both within and between runs. When applied to field-collected goat nasal swab samples, the assay detected at least one target pathogen in the majority of samples and identified co-infections involving two or more pathogens in nearly a quarter of samples. The authors conclude that this multiplex qPCR tool offers a rapid and reliable approach for clinical diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance of caprine respiratory disease.
items.citation: Fu M, Liu Y, Zhang Z et al.. Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of rapid integrated molecular testing for major respiratory viral infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.citation: Liu C, Yu D. Diagnostic accuracy of rapid integrated molecular testing for major respiratory viral infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Development and Initial Analytical Evaluation of a Multiplex PCR-Based Targeted NGS Assay for Expanded Viral Detection in Clinical Respiratory Specimens.
items.summary: This study developed and evaluated an in-house multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing method designed to expand the simultaneous detection of viral pathogens in clinical respiratory specimens beyond the limitations of conventional PCR assays. The panel targeted a broad range of viruses and was paired with dedicated bioinformatics pipelines, with analytical sensitivity assessed using positive control samples and performance explored across hundreds of nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swab specimens stratified by prior PCR results. The method achieved detection limits within a clinically relevant range for the majority of targets tested experimentally, and demonstrated concordance with conventional PCR results while additionally identifying co-infections and viruses missed by prior testing in a meaningful proportion of specimens. Among the supplementary detections, Epstein-Barr virus and cytomegalovirus featured prominently, which the authors caution requires careful clinical interpretation given the complexity of latent infections. The authors conclude that the approach holds promise as an adjunctive diagnostic tool for respiratory infections but requires further optimization, validation, and standardization before broader clinical implementation.
items.citation: Nadtoka MI, Bukharina AY, Roev GV et al.. Development and Initial Analytical Evaluation of a Multiplex PCR-Based Targeted NGS Assay for Expanded Viral Detection in Clinical Respiratory Specimens.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Respiratory viral and bacterial co-infections in adults in acute care: A multiplex PCR-based study.
items.summary: This study investigated how frequently respiratory viruses and bacteria are simultaneously detected by molecular methods in acutely ill adults presenting to the emergency department, and whether such co-detection leads to worse clinical outcomes than detection of either pathogen alone. Nearly one thousand adult patients with respiratory infection symptoms were prospectively enrolled, with nasal swabs analysed by multiplex PCR for a broad panel of viral and bacterial pathogens, and clinical records reviewed for outcomes including pneumonia, antibiotic use, ICU admission, and death. Co-detection of a virus and bacterium was uncommon, with rhinovirus and Streptococcus pneumoniae being the most frequent co-detected pathogens. While co-detection was associated with the greatest risk of antibiotic treatment during follow-up, it was not associated with the highest risk of pneumonia nor with death or ICU admission, with the sole bacterial detection group actually carrying a higher pneumonia risk. The authors conclude that routine multiplex PCR testing for both viral and bacterial respiratory pathogens is unlikely to add meaningful clinical value in this population, and that larger studies with real-time result reporting are needed to determine whether such testing can usefully guide management.
items.citation: Saarela E, Renko M, Uhari M et al.. Respiratory viral and bacterial co-infections in adults in acute care: A multiplex PCR-based study.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Utility of multiplex PCR panels for optimum management of lower respiratory Infections Employing FilmArray Pneumonia Plus Testing-results of the UPLIFT study.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic utility of multiplex PCR testing using the FilmArray Pneumonia Plus Panel (FAPP) in hospitalized patients with lower respiratory tract infections, with a focus on its ability to guide antimicrobial therapy. Patients were enrolled and tested with both FAPP and conventional culture, with outcomes including pathogen detection rates, turnaround time, antibiotic modification, duration of antibiotic therapy, and length of hospital stay compared between methods. FAPP detected at least one pathogen in the vast majority of specimens, far exceeding the detection rate of conventional culture, and enabled antimicrobial modification in a substantially higher proportion of patients. Patients in whom FAPP identified a pathogen also had shorter courses of antibiotic therapy and briefer hospital stays compared to those who tested negative, with turnaround time markedly faster than culture. The authors conclude that FAPP offers superior diagnostic sensitivity, resistance gene detection, and clinical utility compared to conventional culture for managing lower respiratory tract infections in hospitalized patients.
items.venue: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
items.citation: Venkitakrishnan R, Basheer BA, Cleetus M et al.. Utility of multiplex PCR panels for optimum management of lower respiratory Infections Employing FilmArray Pneumonia Plus Testing-results of the UPLIFT study.. Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society. 2026

items.title: B lymphocyte protein factories produced by hematopoietic stem cell gene editing
items.summary: This study investigated whether hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells could be gene-edited to produce long-term, high-level therapeutic proteins in vivo. The researchers edited small numbers of these stem cells and transplanted them into mice, where the resulting B lymphocytes were activated by cognate antigen, underwent clonal expansion, and differentiated into plasma cells capable of synthesizing either antibodies or cargo proteins. The engineered cells produced durable, therapeutic serum levels of antibodies targeting HIV-1, malaria, and influenza, with the anti-influenza broadly neutralizing antibody conferring universal protection against lethal heterologous viral challenge. The findings establish a proof-of-concept framework for self-amplifying B cell protein factories as a platform for both the prevention and treatment of disease.
items.citation: Harald Hartweger, Chiara Ruprecht, Kai-Hui Yao et al.. B lymphocyte protein factories produced by hematopoietic stem cell gene editing. Science. 2026

items.title: Small extracellular vesicle signaling and mitochondrial transfer reprogram T helper cell function in human asthma
items.summary: This paper investigated how small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) derived from airway myeloid-derived regulatory cells contribute to the dysregulated T cell responses characteristic of asthma. The researchers examined whether these sEVs carry mitochondria that can be transferred to CD4+ T cells and whether such transfer influences T cell activation and polarization toward pro-inflammatory Th17 and Th2 phenotypes. They found that sEVs from asthmatic airway cells engage the T cell receptor and deliver mitochondria primarily through membrane fusion, with reactive oxygen species signaling from the transferred mitochondria driving antigen-specific T cell activation. A Drp1-dependent mitochondrial fission mechanism was identified as responsible for packaging mitochondria into sEVs in pro-inflammatory cells, and blocking this oxidant signaling reduced T cell activation. Intranasal delivery of mitochondria-containing sEVs in a mouse asthma model enhanced airway inflammation in vivo, suggesting that sEV-mediated mitochondrial transfer represents a previously unrecognized mechanism of chronic airway inflammation and a potential therapeutic target.
items.citation: Kenneth P. Hough, Jennifer L. Trevor, Shaheer Ahmad et al.. Small extracellular vesicle signaling and mitochondrial transfer reprogram T helper cell function in human asthma. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025
items.summary: This report investigated whether highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus spread from infected domestic cats to humans during an outbreak in Los Angeles County linked to consumption of raw animal products. Health authorities monitored all individuals exposed to the infected cats, tested a subset for antibodies against H5N1, and reviewed their symptom histories and protective behaviors. Among those who underwent serological testing, one asymptomatic veterinary professional who had not worn respiratory or eye protection showed antibodies specific to the H5N1 clade responsible for the cat infections, with no other identifiable risk factors for infection. Notably, none of the exposed individuals, including those who reported influenza-like illness, tested positive by standard molecular testing, underscoring that RT-PCR alone may miss cases. The findings provide serological evidence of possible cat-to-human transmission of H5N1 and highlight the importance of infection control practices in veterinary settings.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Aisling Vaughan, Allison Joyce, Elizabeth Traub et al.. Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: These guidelines address the prevention, diagnosis, and management of infections in people with inflammatory bowel disease, a population at elevated risk for opportunistic infections due to immunosuppressive therapies. The work was undertaken because the therapeutic landscape for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis has expanded rapidly, with newer small molecules, advanced biologics, and evolving vaccination strategies introducing distinct infection risk profiles not fully covered by prior guidance. The guidelines provide structured, evidence-based recommendations spanning risk stratification and the full spectrum of viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable infections. A key emphasis is placed on preventative strategies tailored to contemporary treatment regimens, recognising that potent immune modulation demands proactive clinical management. This update supersedes earlier consensus statements and reflects the most current data to support clinicians in balancing effective disease control with minimising infection-related morbidity and mortality.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: mRNA-based influenza vaccine expands the B cell response breadth in humans
items.summary: This study compared human immune responses to conventional split-virion influenza vaccines versus investigational mRNA-based quadrivalent influenza vaccines across two consecutive seasonal vaccination periods. Researchers assessed B cell responses in healthy young adults, examining antibody titers, memory B cell frequencies, germinal center reactions in draining lymph nodes, and serum immunoglobulin repertoires using proteomic and B cell lineage analyses. The mRNA-based vaccine induced higher antibody titers and greater memory B cell frequencies compared to the conventional vaccine, and uniquely stimulated sustained germinal center reactions persisting for at least half a year after vaccination in a subset of participants. Proteomic analysis revealed that mRNA vaccination increased the diversity of vaccine-elicited serum antibody clonotypes and promoted expansion within pre-existing clonotypes, with lineage tracing linking these expanded clonotypes to germinal center-associated B cell branches. Crucially, this remodeling of the antibody repertoire was accompanied by broader binding activity against antigenically divergent influenza viruses, highlighting persistent germinal center responses as a key mechanism for expanding vaccine-induced antibody breadth.
items.citation: Hanover C. Matz, Tae-Geun Yu, Kritika Dixit et al.. mRNA-based influenza vaccine expands the B cell response breadth in humans. Nature Immunology. 2026

items.title: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga
items.summary: This paper argues that artificial intelligence can enable large-scale computational study of comics, a visually rich historical medium that has largely been examined only one work at a time. The researchers developed PAGE, a framework that segments comic book scans into panels and text, applies vision-language models to annotate visual content according to a structured codebook, validates those annotations against human coding, and uses statistical modeling to explain changes across an archive while controlling for publisher and genre. The framework was demonstrated on a large corpus of mid-twentieth-century American comic books and Japanese manga volumes through three studies examining political representation, visual style and individual artistic signatures, and patterns of who speaks across the two traditions. The work shows that AI tools can systematically recover historical patterns in how mass media depicted power, war, and social roles at a scale impossible through conventional close reading. Beyond scholarship, the authors argue the same methods could make comics archives searchable by visual content, improve accessibility for blind and low-vision readers, and aid in preservation and attribution of uncredited artists.
items.citation: Emilio Ferrara. Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga. arXiv. 2026

items.title: How far is Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness from Martin-Löf randomness?
items.summary: This paper investigates the relationship between Kolmogorov-Loveland (KL) randomness and Martin-Löf randomness (MLR) by asking how close these two notions are in a precise, constructive sense. The authors introduce the concept of a computable encoding—a measure-preserving, disjointedness-respecting map from basic to clopen sets of binary sequences—and study whether such encodings can transfer randomness tests between different notions. They show that no such computable encoding exists for partial computable randomness relative to MLR, but that one does exist for KL randomness. Specifically, they construct a total computable encoding together with a pair of total computable non-monotonic betting strategies such that at least one strategy wins on every encoded sequence whenever the original sequence is non-MLR, thereby effectively reducing MLR testing to KL randomness testing. This result provides a concrete sense in which KL randomness is closer to Martin-Löf randomness than partial computable randomness is.
items.citation: Tomislav Petrović. How far is Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness from Martin-Löf randomness?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Hybrid and Hierarchical Ray Tracing Method for Efficient 3D Gaussian Rendering
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational inefficiencies of ray-traced three-dimensional Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), which, despite enabling advanced rendering effects like secondary lighting and depth-of-field, suffers from load imbalance, redundant ray traversal, and heterogeneous intersection workloads compared to rasterization-based approaches. The authors developed H2-Ray, a hybrid and hierarchical ray tracing architecture incorporating three innovations: a density-aware spatial bounding volume hierarchy for balanced workload distribution, a proxy-ray mechanism that shares traversal state among neighboring rays to reduce redundant computation, and a unified intersection engine with a multiplexed datapath capable of handling both Gaussian and triangle primitives efficiently. Evaluation across multiple scenes demonstrated substantial speedups over an existing ray-traced Gaussian splatting baseline on a professional GPU, with a geometric-mean speedup exceeding three-fold and peak speedups approaching an order of magnitude.
items.citation: Tiancheng Zhao, Sixu Li, Yuzhou Chen et al.. A Hybrid and Hierarchical Ray Tracing Method for Efficient 3D Gaussian Rendering. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Blocking of bistable front propagation: Application to Wolbachia population replacement
items.summary: This paper investigates the spatial spread of Wolbachia bacteria within mosquito populations as a strategy to block transmission of mosquito-borne diseases like dengue, for which no vaccine exists. The authors developed a mathematical framework based on a reaction-diffusion system, reducing a two-equation model to a single closed equation to simplify analysis of propagation dynamics. They specifically examined how spatial heterogeneity in environmental carrying capacity can block the bistable travelling front that drives population replacement. Through theoretical analysis and supporting numerical simulations, the study demonstrates that sufficiently large variations in carrying capacity across different regions of the spatial domain can halt the propagation of Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes, preventing complete population replacement.
items.citation: Saoussen Latrach, Nicolas Vauchelet, Hatem Zaag. Blocking of bistable front propagation: Application to Wolbachia population replacement. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Who Can Say No? Control, Accountability and the Pace of Frontier AI
items.summary: This paper examines the institutional and human dimensions of controlling frontier AI systems, arguing that loss of control arises not from AI acting autonomously but from organizational structures that systematically eliminate the possibility of anyone saying no. The authors define meaningful control as requiring a named individual who can detect a serious problem, challenge a decision, halt a system, and reverse it, while bearing personal accountability for failing to do so. To operationalize this, they propose three diagnostic questions any organization involved in AI development or deployment should be able to answer publicly, concerning internal accountability, external oversight authority, and the pace of AI-building relative to the pace of checking. They evaluate fifty existing governance mechanisms against these criteria, finding that nearly all originated as single rules adopted unilaterally by individual actors rather than through coordinated frameworks. The paper frames itself explicitly as a starting point rather than a solution, contending that transparent publication of accountability structures is an action any single laboratory can take immediately, with contracts, independent bodies, and legal frameworks to follow.
items.citation: Rikard Rosenbacke, Carl Rosenbacke, Victor Rosenbacke et al.. Who Can Say No? Control, Accountability and the Pace of Frontier AI. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Agreement Without Alignment: Label-Free Rubric Clarification Increases LLM-Judge Consensus but Not Agreement with Humans
items.summary: This paper investigated whether LLM judge panels can be made more consistent through automated rubric clarification, and whether such consistency improvements translate into better alignment with human judgments. The researchers developed a label-free procedure that identifies the most contested sub-criteria within a rubric by measuring cross-judge disagreement, then uses an editor model to rewrite only those disputed clauses, without ever using human labels to guide the editing process. The approach was evaluated across three datasets using a panel of five judges from three providers, testing preregistered hypotheses about inter-judge agreement and human alignment. The procedure successfully increased consensus among LLM judges compared to both original rubrics and a control condition that edited randomly selected clauses, demonstrating that targeting contested criteria specifically drives the improvement. However, the increased inter-judge agreement did not produce any detectable improvement in alignment with human expert ratings, and secondary analyses suggested that editing contested clauses may even yield slightly lower human agreement than editing arbitrary ones, revealing a troubling dissociation between judge consensus and actual validity.
items.citation: Sangdo Han, Moonsoo Kim. Agreement Without Alignment: Label-Free Rubric Clarification Increases LLM-Judge Consensus but Not Agreement with Humans. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.
items.summary: The paper developed and evaluated two pentaplex real-time fluorescent PCR assays designed to simultaneously detect ten important pathogens affecting sheep, covering five respiratory and five reproductive disease agents. Each panel was validated using reference materials and plasmids, with detection limits established across all targets and assessments of reproducibility and specificity. The assays demonstrated very low limits of detection, excellent reproducibility with minimal variation between and within runs, and high specificity with no cross-reactivity among the targeted pathogens. Clinical validation using a large collection of field samples from multiple regions showed strong agreement with established reference methods. The resulting multiplex platform offers a rapid and reliable approach for differential diagnosis and broad surveillance of major ovine respiratory and reproductive pathogens.
items.citation: Wang S, Bai Z, Wan B et al.. Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Nanobodies: A Promising Toolkit for Diagnostic Applications
items.summary: This paper reviews nanobodies — single-domain antigen-binding fragments derived from camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies — as tools for diagnostic applications. The authors examine how their distinctive biochemical properties, including small size, high solubility, and favorable stability, make them advantageous for recognizing otherwise inaccessible epitopes and performing well under conditions that challenge conventional antibodies. The review covers the integration of nanobodies into a range of detection platforms, including ELISA, lateral flow immunoassays, biosensors, and in vivo imaging modalities such as PET and SPECT. The authors also highlight technical advances such as multivalent designs, site-specific conjugation, and optimized expression systems that have improved nanobody performance in clinical diagnostics. The paper additionally surveys ongoing clinical trials and emerging strategies aimed at developing scalable and sensitive nanobody-based diagnostic platforms.
items.citation: Wei Wu, Abid Ali, Li Sun et al.. Nanobodies: A Promising Toolkit for Diagnostic Applications. SmartMat. 2026

items.title: Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.
items.citation: Atta S, Thorsen TL, Vasse T et al.. Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.. ACS applied materials & interfaces. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.
items.summary: This review paper examines lateral flow immunoassay technology as a diagnostic tool for viral infectious diseases, reconceptualizing it beyond its conventional role as a point-of-care test toward a broader point-of-need self-testing platform capable of supporting large-scale epidemic surveillance and pandemic preparedness. The authors systematically survey recent advances across three main areas: signal generation and transduction strategies employing diverse nanomaterials such as colorimetric, fluorescent, magnetic, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and photothermal systems; multimodal and multiplex detection approaches aimed at improving sensitivity, accuracy, and throughput; and the integration of machine learning for signal interpretation and system optimization. The review also comprehensively covers applications in detecting viral antigens, antibodies, and nucleic acids. The authors critically assess current limitations including sensitivity constraints, target specificity issues, and practical challenges related to cost, usability, and stability, while proposing future directions centered on advanced nanomaterials, intelligent data processing, and multi-target detection. Overall, the review argues that lateral flow immunoassay, particularly in its colorimetric form, holds transformative potential as an emergency pandemic screening tool and for routine decentralized diagnostics that could strengthen global public health infrastructure.
items.citation: Li L, Liu F, He X et al.. Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Beyond lateral flow: vertical flow immunoassays as thermodynamically assisted rapid diagnostics.
items.summary: Lateral flow immunoassays dominate point-of-care testing but suffer from fundamental architectural constraints—including poor analyte capture kinetics, high non-specific background, limited multiplexing capacity, and the hook effect at elevated analyte concentrations—that cap their diagnostic performance. This review examines vertical flow immunoassays as a structural alternative, wherein a stacked-membrane design separates convective fluid delivery from immunoreaction kinetics, enabling selective thermodynamic washing, two-dimensional multiplexing arrays, and sequential surface chemistry that eliminates the hook effect. The authors survey the physical-chemical principles underlying vertical flow performance and document substantial sensitivity gains over matched lateral flow formats, with improvements extending into the sub-picogram-per-milliliter range when coupled with surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical transduction, nanoparticle amplification, or deep-learning inference. Applications across clinical diagnostics, food safety, and environmental monitoring are mapped alongside an analysis of the engineering and commercialization barriers that have prevented wider adoption despite the demonstrated sensitivity advantage. The review concludes by outlining a realistic pathway toward practical deployment and sustained clinical and industrial impact for this platform.
items.citation: Nainar SNS, Chu YY, Lin HC et al.. Beyond lateral flow: vertical flow immunoassays as thermodynamically assisted rapid diagnostics.. Chemical communications (Cambridge, England). 2026

items.title: Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.
items.citation: Liu T, Sun J, Huang J et al.. Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of point-of-care testing technologies for SARS-CoV-2, motivated by the diagnostic demands exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors conducted a structured literature search across major databases to evaluate molecular assays, antigen and antibody tests, biosensor platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostic approaches. Molecular methods such as rapid RT-PCR, LAMP, and CRISPR-based technologies were found to offer high sensitivity and specificity suited to decentralized settings, while antigen tests provide rapid and affordable screening despite variable performance influenced by viral load and circulating variants. Antibody-based testing was found most appropriate for seroprevalence and retrospective applications rather than acute diagnosis, and emerging biosensor and AI systems showed promise but largely remain at prototype or early-validation stages. The review concludes that no single modality is universally optimal, and that complementary use of these approaches, alongside advances in multiplexing, digital connectivity, and variant-resilient design, will strengthen future infectious disease preparedness.
items.citation: Hetta HF, Ahmed R, Haseeb A et al.. SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.
items.summary: This study evaluated a field-deployable serological assay for detecting arbovirus antibodies in wild birds, focusing on Usutu virus, which is enzootically maintained between mosquitoes and avian hosts. The researchers tested a species-independent Lateral Flow Microarray ImmunoAssay capable of simultaneously detecting antibodies against both Usutu virus and West Nile virus non-structural proteins in wild birds captured at ringing sites in the Netherlands. Field-collected blood samples were tested on-site, and a subset of birds was additionally analyzed using gold-standard neutralization tests to validate the assay's performance. The assay demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for Usutu virus detection compared to the gold-standard method, and also successfully identified a seroconversion event in a Eurasian blackbird. Evaluation against the WHO REASSURED framework confirmed the assay's suitability for point-of-capture testing, supporting its potential use in wildlife surveillance programs operating in field or resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Godarzi B, Holicki CM, Chandler FD et al.. On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.. Journal of virological methods. 2026

items.title: Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities
items.summary: This study investigated how combining DNA-base pairing and electrostatic complementarity influences the properties of peptide-based hydrogels, using a class of hybrid molecules called nucleopeptides. The researchers synthesized six nucleopeptides derived from two tetrapeptide sequences carrying opposite charges at physiological pH, each functionalized with one of the four DNA nucleobases introduced through a peptide nucleic acid moiety. By systematically combining these components in a multicomponent approach, they examined how charge complementarity and nucleobase-pair complementarity together shape the mechanical and physicochemical properties of the resulting hydrogels, including stiffness, gelation time, thermal stability, and fibrillar network morphology. Their findings demonstrate that carefully selecting complementary components allows fine-tuning of hydrogel properties, while also revealing unexpected behaviors that highlight the underlying complexity of these bioinspired systems. Overall, the work establishes nucleopeptide-based multicomponent hydrogels as a promising platform for developing high-performance supramolecular materials with tunable characteristics for biomedical and biotechnological applications.
items.citation: Tristan Giraud, Marine Koch, Paul Hoschtettler et al.. Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities. ACS Materials Au. 2026

items.title: Microneedle array platforms for drug delivery and biomarker sensing: From skin mechanics guided design to scalable manufacture for clinical utility
items.summary: This review examines the current state and translational challenges of microneedle array patch technology for drug delivery and biomarker sensing through the skin. The authors survey the design considerations governing microneedle geometry, noting the fundamental tension between needles being slender enough to penetrate skin painlessly yet large enough to carry therapeutically meaningful doses of active pharmaceutical ingredients. The review integrates analysis of skin anatomy and mechanical behavior with fabrication approaches, comparing manufacturing methods for their scalability, cost efficiency, and throughput suitability for commercial production. Applicator designs, biocompatibility, dissolution behavior in dermal tissue, and the regulatory science landscape are also examined. The authors conclude that despite substantial laboratory-level progress, no microneedle patch product has achieved regulatory approval for commercial use, and they identify the technical, manufacturing, and regulatory gaps that must be addressed to enable patient-directed, self-applied transdermal therapy.
items.citation: Jiachi Zhou, Lei Wu, Minna Wyttenbach et al.. Microneedle array platforms for drug delivery and biomarker sensing: From skin mechanics guided design to scalable manufacture for clinical utility. Journal of Controlled Release. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies
items.summary: This review paper examines the current state of Alzheimer's disease research, focusing on both the molecular mechanisms underlying the disease and emerging therapeutic approaches. The authors synthesize recent advances across several areas, including the roles of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, apolipoprotein E biology, neuroimmunology, and biomarker discovery. They also assess early clinical experience with new disease-modifying therapies that can slow cognitive decline by clearing amyloid plaques from the brain. While these treatments represent meaningful progress, the review acknowledges that interventions capable of stopping or preventing cognitive impairment altogether remain an unmet goal. The authors conclude that recent discoveries are transforming how Alzheimer's disease is diagnosed and treated, raising optimism for future strategies that could render the disease both treatable and preventable.
items.citation: Michelle Diane Rudman, Jason D. Ulrich, David M. Holtzman. Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies. Cell. 2026

items.title: The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review
items.summary: This narrative review examines the biological connections between periodontal disease, gut health, and brain function, proposing an integrated "oral–gut–brain axis" as a unifying framework for understanding comorbidities among periodontal, cardiometabolic, and neurodegenerative conditions. The authors conducted a structured literature search across major databases to synthesize evidence on the molecular mechanisms by which oral dysbiosis may propagate inflammation through the gut to the central nervous system. Key findings indicate that periodontal pathogens such as Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum can be detected ectopically in the gut, where they are associated with disrupted intestinal barrier integrity and altered microbial composition, changes that are in turn linked to increased blood–brain barrier permeability, microglial activation, and amyloid-beta accumulation in preclinical and observational studies. Salivary and intestinal biomarkers, including matrix metalloproteinases, interleukins, short-chain fatty acids, and calprotectin, are identified as potentially useful non-invasive tools for monitoring inflammatory burden across the entire axis. The authors conclude that while the framework is biologically plausible, existing evidence remains largely associative, and causal directionality in humans requires validation through longitudinal studies before pharmacological interventions targeting this tripartite pathway can be clinically implemented.
items.citation: Caterina Nela Dumitru, Alina Oana Dumitru, Gabriel Valeriu Popa et al.. The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review. Dentistry Journal. 2026

items.title: Quantum dot biosensors for highly sensitive and multiplex detection in biomedical diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines quantum dot-based biosensors as platforms for biomedical diagnostics, addressing limitations of conventional immunoassays such as low sensitivity, photobleaching, and poor optical penetration in biological tissues. The authors survey recent advances across fluorescent, photoelectrochemical, and electrochemiluminescent sensing formats, connecting quantum dot surface engineering strategies—including attachment of antibodies, aptamers, peptides, and nucleic acids—to their underlying detection mechanisms. Near-infrared-emitting quantum dots are highlighted for their ability to reduce tissue autofluorescence and improve imaging depth for real-time in vivo molecular tracking. The review covers analytical performance in detecting pathogens, cancer biomarkers, and metabolites, while also addressing challenges of toxicity and biocompatibility alongside emerging mitigation strategies such as cadmium-free compositions and surface passivation. The authors position their contribution as a mechanistically integrated framework linking surface chemistry to sensing performance and clinical translation, distinguishing it from prior reviews in the field.
items.citation: Soumendu Patra, Harshita Shand. Quantum dot biosensors for highly sensitive and multiplex detection in biomedical diagnostics. Discover Sensors. 2026

items.title: InstantFusion: A Shared Latent Interface for Heterogeneous Image Generators
items.summary: InstantFusion investigates whether independently trained image generation models based on diffusion and flow paradigms share compatible latent representations despite their architectural heterogeneity. The authors first demonstrate that such models exhibit similar spatial organization in their latent spaces and that passing intermediate denoising states between unaligned models can preserve coarse visual content. Building on this observation, they propose a lightweight shared latent interface that uses model-specific Latent AutoEncoders to project intermediate denoising states from different generators into a common space and decode them into a target generator's latent space, with training objectives that align states from the same image at matched noise levels and synchronize local denoising velocities. Once trained, the interface allows denoising trajectories to transition across frozen, heterogeneous generators without requiring pairwise mappings for every model combination. The approach is shown to be effective across several applications including generation acceleration, multi-preference composition, cross-architecture distillation, and cross-model composition.
items.citation: Xuanlang Dai, Jiazi Bu, Yujie Zhou et al.. InstantFusion: A Shared Latent Interface for Heterogeneous Image Generators. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Noise Space Learning for VLA Adaptation
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of adapting pretrained vision-language-action models to specific robot manipulation tasks under constraints on interaction data, computation, and safety. The proposed approach, noise space learning, works by learning a context-conditioned distribution over the noise inputs of flow-matching-based generative models while leaving the pretrained model weights frozen. The method is formulated as a general interface compatible with multiple reinforcement and imitation learning algorithms, which are instantiated with proximal policy optimization, soft actor-critic, and advantage-weighted regression. The authors provide both an information-theoretic analysis supporting the efficiency of this adaptation strategy and empirical evaluations across simulated and real-robot benchmarks. Their findings yield a suite of noise space learning variants along with practical guidelines for selecting among them depending on available resources and deployment conditions.
items.citation: Junjie Lu, Chuheng Zhang, Yucen Wang et al.. Noise Space Learning for VLA Adaptation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of managing communications in deep-space networks, where intermittent contact windows, long propagation delays, and limited relay storage make scheduling decisions critical. The authors developed a closed-loop reinforcement learning framework for a relay node forwarding data from both lunar and Martian sources to Earth, using the Bundle Protocol's store-carry-forward paradigm. They introduced a metric called excess age to capture information freshness relative to source-dependent delay baselines, and defined a goal-oriented loss function that supports nonlinear, mission-relevant penalties for staleness. The relay scheduling problem was formulated as a constrained semi-Markov decision process and solved using a masked Lagrangian Proximal Policy Optimization approach, where feasibility-aware action masking prevents scheduling bundles that cannot complete transmission within an available contact window. Simulations in DTNSim demonstrated that the proposed method outperforms conventional schedulers such as FIFO in terms of age-based utility and fairness across heterogeneous data sources.
items.citation: Sajjad Baghaeea, Aimin Lib, Shanmugarajan Balasubramanian et al.. Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale census of emission-line galaxies using JWST's near-infrared wide-field slitless spectroscopy mode as part of the COSMOS-3D program, covering a substantial contiguous sky area with grism spectroscopy spanning roughly 3.9 to 5.1 micrometers. The researchers combined slitless spectroscopic data with deep multi-band imaging to build a homogeneous sample of over twelve thousand objects spanning redshifts from zero to nine, developing a novel multi-step identification framework to address the source confusion inherent to slitless spectroscopy that incorporated convolutional neural networks and large language models to emulate human identification. The survey detected a broad suite of emission lines—including oxygen, hydrogen recombination, helium, sulfur, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon features—enabling a nearly continuous census of galaxies across cosmic time and yielding spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties for all sources. By constructing composite spectra in multiple redshift bins, the team also recovered faint spectral features such as higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and iron emission lines that are undetectable in individual spectra. The resulting catalog is presented as a key reference dataset for studies of star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity, and as a demonstration of the power of wide-field slitless spectroscopy for assembling large, unbiased spectroscopic samples.
items.citation: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al.. A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates the role of sub-volume sampling strategies in self-supervised learning for three-dimensional medical images, challenging the common assumption that random cropping treats all spatial regions equally. The authors first demonstrate through controlled crop-quality experiments that the choice of which sub-volumes to sample during pretraining acts as an underappreciated bottleneck, with higher-quality crops leading to better downstream task performance. To address this, they reframe sub-volume sampling as a "where-to-look" problem and propose a plug-and-play framework that replaces random cropping with an offline coarse-to-fine probe bank guided by principles of anatomy-awareness, informativeness, and diversity. The framework is instantiated in two variants—a lightweight version using geometric and image-statistical cues, and a diagnostically richer version using frozen visual features—to assess whether simple volume-intrinsic priors are sufficient or whether semantic cues provide additional benefit. Extensive experiments across multiple backbones and downstream tasks show that the lightweight variant consistently improves transfer performance over random sampling, with analyses attributing the gains to more anatomically meaningful observations, reduced spatial redundancy, and more structured learned representations.
items.citation: Junkai Liu, Le Zhang. Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Lean Formalization of the Hamilton--Perelman Proof of Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize meaningfully, as it provides almost no detail about the methods, intermediate results, or findings beyond announcing a Lean formalization of the Hamilton–Perelman Ricci-flow proof of Thurston's geometrization conjecture.
items.citation: Yuan Liao, Ziyang Qin, Jui-Hui Chung et al.. A Lean Formalization of the Hamilton--Perelman Proof of Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.
items.summary: This study evaluated the Xpert HIV-1 Viral Load XC assay as a candidate for primary nucleic acid testing within HIV-1 diagnostic workflows, with the goal of enabling both diagnosis and viral load measurement in a single clinical encounter at the point of care. The assay was assessed for analytical range, precision, reproducibility, and agreement against standard-of-care methods including the Roche cobas HIV-1 quantitative assay and four other HIV assays. The Xpert VL XC demonstrated a strong analytical range with complete detection across tested concentrations, full agreement with the comparator assay on known positive and negative samples, and a substantially faster turnaround time than conventional batch testing. However, positive agreement with other assays was moderate, with most discrepancies occurring at viral loads below the assay's lower limit of quantification, and the assay produced a small proportion of invalid results. The findings underscore both the potential utility and current limitations of rapid quantitative molecular diagnostics for HIV-1, particularly regarding sensitivity at low viral loads in point-of-care settings.
items.citation: Uhteg K, Bayan MH, Boudreau A et al.. Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.
items.summary: This study examined patient perspectives on point-of-care nucleic acid testing for HIV viral load monitoring, addressing the limitation that standard laboratory tests take days to return results. Participants enrolled in a clinical study received a semi-quantitative point-of-care test using fingerstick whole blood samples and were asked to complete surveys and in-depth interviews about the experience. Participants broadly found the point-of-care approach acceptable and preferred its faster turnaround time and clinic-based fingerstick sampling compared to conventional viral load testing. However, participants expressed a preference for an even shorter turnaround time than the roughly two hours the test required and desired a lower limit of detection than the current threshold, which would be important for monitoring patients with well-suppressed viral loads. The authors conclude that point-of-care nucleic acid testing holds promise for improving HIV care, particularly for patients with incomplete engagement in care, but that technical improvements would enhance its feasibility for implementation in United States clinical settings.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Murphy M, Violette LR et al.. Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.. AIDS care. 2026

items.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.
items.summary: This study examined the feasibility, acceptability, and diagnostic performance of point-of-care nucleic acid tests for both HIV detection and viral load monitoring in clinical and community settings in the United States. The researchers enrolled participants across two sites — a hospital-based clinic and an LGBTQ+ community center — where individuals seeking HIV testing, post-exposure prophylaxis, or pre-exposure prophylaxis received a qualitative point-of-care nucleic acid test alongside standard laboratory testing, while people already living with HIV received a semiquantitative point-of-care test compared against standard viral load monitoring in a randomized clinical trial. The study used a prospective longitudinal mixed-methods design incorporating demographic surveys, electronic medical records, acceptability surveys, in-depth interviews, and time-and-motion observations to capture both quantitative and qualitative outcomes. Enrollment was completed with hundreds of participants contributing research visits across the study period, but the abstract notes that test performance, clinical, and qualitative analyses are not yet complete and results are anticipated in future publications. As a protocol and feasibility paper, the abstract does not report findings on diagnostic accuracy or clinical impact, making full summary of outcomes premature.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Violette LR, Cornelius-Hudson A et al.. Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.. JMIR research protocols. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article addresses a longstanding question in exercise immunology: whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The authors examine evidence that while regular moderate-intensity exercise is broadly considered beneficial for immune defense, high-performance athletes and military personnel engaged in arduous exercise appear to experience elevated infection burdens. The debate explored whether this elevated infection risk can be attributed to exercise per se, or whether it is confounded by accompanying factors such as sleep disruption, anxiety, nutritional deficits, travel, and environmental extremes that independently alter immune pathways. Contested issues included whether athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, which biomarkers best reflect immune health under heavy training loads, and the quality of evidence used to support claims about exercise-induced immunosuppression. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial, but the question of whether exercise alone causally increases infection risk in athletes remains unresolved, with the authors calling for more rigorous empirical research.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review paper examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize how approaches such as genome-wide association studies, transcriptomic profiling, proteomic interaction mapping, and metabolomic sequencing generate deep molecular insights into disease mechanisms, while advanced deep learning architectures help decode these complex biological datasets. The review analyzes multiomics applications across the drug development pipeline, including target deconvolution, drug repositioning, and de novo compound discovery, alongside the role of AI in virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. The authors highlight demonstrated advantages in oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions, while acknowledging persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and mitigating algorithmic biases. They conclude that the convergence of multiomics and AI offers transformative potential for accelerating target identification, optimizing drug candidates, and enabling more precise clinical trial designs, heralding a new era in bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined CRISPR-Cas systems as potential next-generation antimicrobials for combating multidrug-resistant bacteria, motivated by the growing failure of conventional antibiotics. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental studies investigating CRISPR effectors—primarily Cas9, along with Cas12 and Cas13—across various bacterial targets, delivery platforms, and therapeutic outcomes. The reviewed evidence showed that CRISPR-Cas systems can effectively kill or resensitize resistant bacteria through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid elimination, integron disruption, and RNA-targeted cleavage. Among delivery strategies, phage-mediated delivery demonstrated the most consistent efficacy, and one CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has progressed to clinical evaluation. Despite promising results, the review identifies significant translational barriers including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient long-term safety data, highlighting the need for optimized delivery systems, multiplex targeting, and standardized regulatory frameworks.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients
items.summary: These two open-label randomized platform trials examined whether oral nirmatrelvir–ritonavir reduces hospitalization or death in higher-risk outpatients with COVID-19 who were predominantly vaccinated and/or had prior natural immunity. Conducted in the United Kingdom and Canada, the trials enrolled adults who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and had been symptomatic for five days or fewer, randomly assigning them to receive either usual care with nirmatrelvir–ritonavir or usual care alone. Hospitalization or death within 28 days was rare in both arms of both trials, and neither trial demonstrated a statistically meaningful reduction in this primary outcome with nirmatrelvir–ritonavir treatment. Although a substudy confirmed that the drug reduced viral load by the end of the treatment course, this virological effect did not translate into a clinical benefit for the hospitalization or mortality endpoint. The investigators concluded that, unlike findings in unvaccinated high-risk populations, nirmatrelvir–ritonavir does not reduce hospitalization or death among vaccinated higher-risk individuals with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
items.citation: Christopher C. Butler, Andrew Pinto, Victoria Harris et al.. Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: Trial design and end points in hepatocellular carcinoma: an EASL–AASLD–ILCA consensus statement
items.citation: Josep Maria Llovet, Ezequiel Mauro, Lorenza Rimassa et al.. Trial design and end points in hepatocellular carcinoma: an EASL–AASLD–ILCA consensus statement. Nature Reviews Clinical Oncology. 2026

items.title: Phase 3 Trial of Weekly Oral Islatravir–Lenacapavir for HIV-1 Treatment
items.summary: This phase 3 clinical trial investigated whether a once-weekly oral combination of islatravir and lenacapavir could maintain HIV-1 viral suppression as effectively as the standard once-daily single-tablet regimen of bictegravir-emtricitabine-tenofovir alafenamide in adults who were already virologically suppressed. The study was a double-blind, randomized, active-controlled noninferiority trial conducted across multiple countries, in which participants were assigned to switch to the weekly regimen or continue the daily regimen for up to 96 weeks, with noninferiority assessed at 48 weeks using viral load as the primary endpoint.
