At week 48, virologic failure was essentially absent in the weekly treatment group and occurred in only one participant in the daily treatment group, demonstrating that the once-weekly regimen was noninferior to the once-daily standard of care. CD4+ T-cell counts were maintained comparably between groups, and the safety profiles were similar, with low rates of treatment discontinuation due to adverse events in both arms. These findings suggest that once-weekly oral islatravir-lenacapavir represents a viable long-acting oral alternative that could help address adherence challenges associated with daily dosing.
items.citation: Jürgen Kurt Rockstroh, Moti N. Ramgopal, Adrià Curran Fábregas et al.. Phase 3 Trial of Weekly Oral Islatravir–Lenacapavir for HIV-1 Treatment. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: Monodromy of Tate-Linear varieties
items.summary: The paper addresses a question in algebraic geometry concerning the structure of special subvarieties within the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties in characteristic p. Specifically, it investigates whether the Tate-linear property of a smooth subvariety of a central leaf is a global or merely local condition. By carefully analyzing the p-adic monodromy groups of such varieties and building on recent foundational work, the authors prove that if a smooth subvariety of a central leaf is Tate-linear at a single point, then it is necessarily Tate-linear at every point. This rigidity result provides a positive answer to a question posed by Chai about the global nature of the Tate-linear condition.
items.citation: Livia Grammatica. Monodromy of Tate-Linear varieties. arXiv. 2026

items.title: One-Way Delay Model for 5G Low Latency, High Data Rate Communications
items.summary: This paper investigates one-way delay in 5G edge networks as a means to detect and manage queue buildup at wireless link bottlenecks, which are the typical congestion points in such systems. The authors developed a framework for modeling one-way delay by decomposing queueing delay into two measurable components: aggregation delay, which can be observed at the user equipment, and channel access time, which can be estimated from network conditions. The central finding is that queueing delay dominates one-way delay at high data rates, and that although queueing delay is difficult to measure directly at the base station, it can be closely approximated by combining these two sub-components. The model was validated through network simulations across varying load conditions and both single- and multi-user scenarios. The framework is intended to enable more efficient and fine-grained congestion control and bottleneck detection in 5G networks, addressing limitations of latency-based approaches that can lead to cellular network underutilization.
items.citation: Hamid Hassani, Sonia M. Heemstra de Groot, Ignas G. Niemegeers et al.. One-Way Delay Model for 5G Low Latency, High Data Rate Communications. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Adjoint-Based Stochastic Analysis for Fatigue of Aeroelastic and Frictional Systems
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of analyzing vibration behavior in engineering systems subject to both deterministic periodic forcing and stochastic noise, where existing methods are often limited to small models or ignore randomness in excitation. The authors expand a recent approach that computes a time-varying covariance matrix by linearizing around a periodic nonlinear response obtained via harmonic balance, improving numerical conditioning to handle models ranging from a few to hundreds of degrees of freedom. A key contribution is the development of a period-spanning covariance matrix, computed with model reduction for efficiency, which captures correlations across both space and time within a full vibration cycle. This framework enables rapid sampling of stochastic response cycles and estimation of fatigue-relevant statistics at a fraction of the cost of direct stochastic time integration. The methodology is demonstrated on two beam systems—one with unsteady aerodynamic forces and one with a frictional Bouc-Wen tip force—achieving accurate stochastic statistics for the aeroelastic case and useful, though somewhat less accurate, estimates for the frictional case due to linearization errors, while delivering very large reductions in computational time.
items.citation: Justin H. Porter. Adjoint-Based Stochastic Analysis for Fatigue of Aeroelastic and Frictional Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of serving long-context large language models efficiently when KV cache memory becomes the binding constraint before hardware throughput is saturated. The authors extend a prior system called HiSparse, which offloads KV cache history to host memory and fetches only selected entries, by introducing Adaptive DHiSparse, which adds two key capabilities: load-adaptive memory residency and support for speculative decoding frameworks. The system dynamically adjusts how much KV history remains on GPU depending on current load, protecting a required working set while retaining extra history when memory is available and recovering the remainder through fused sparse retrieval, and it integrates draft-model speculative decoding by sharing retrieval operations across queries, using a ring buffer for draft KV, and reusing verification staging across layer groups. Evaluated at very long contexts and high concurrency, the approach substantially outperforms both standard HiSparse and non-speculative adaptive serving in output throughput, and at matched latency targets it supports significantly higher concurrency and output volume. The adaptive residency mechanism also sharply reduces the fraction of rows that must be fetched from host memory under low-load conditions, demonstrating efficient use of available GPU memory across varying traffic levels.
items.citation: Naji Alazhar, Wassel Alazhar. Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Hybrid and Hierarchical Ray Tracing Method for Efficient 3D Gaussian Rendering
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of making ray-traced 3D Gaussian Splatting practical for real-time neural rendering, identifying three core problems: load imbalance from non-uniform Gaussian distributions, redundant ray traversal among neighboring pixels, and inefficient handling of mixed primitive types on current GPU hardware. The authors developed H2-Ray, a hybrid and hierarchical ray tracing architecture incorporating three novel techniques: a density-aware spatial bounding volume hierarchy for load balancing, a ray-cluster path reuse mechanism to share traversal state among similar rays, and a unified intersection engine with a mode-multiplexed datapath that handles both Gaussian and triangle primitives by sharing a substantial portion of floating-point units. The system was evaluated across multiple scenes using a cycle-accurate hardware model combined with measured GPU timings. H2-Ray achieves substantial geometric-mean and peak speedups over a baseline ray-traced Gaussian splatting system, demonstrating that targeted architectural innovations can make ray-traced Gaussian rendering significantly more efficient than prior approaches.
items.citation: Tiancheng Zhao, Sixu Li, Yuzhou Chen et al.. A Hybrid and Hierarchical Ray Tracing Method for Efficient 3D Gaussian Rendering. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Tri-Hybrid SWIPT with Reconfigurable Parasitic Antennas
items.summary: This paper proposes a tri-hybrid precoding architecture for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer systems that incorporates reconfigurable parasitic antennas as a third precoding layer. The authors integrate multiport network theory and information theory to explicitly account for mutual coupling and reactive energy storage within the antenna domain, which conventional hybrid precoding architectures ignore. To solve the resulting optimization problem efficiently, they develop a low-complexity algorithm combining coordinate descent for parasitic reactive load optimization, a singular value decomposition-based analog precoder, and a protective partial zero-forcing digital precoder. Their numerical results reveal that impedance mismatch at the transmit array reduces the real power accepted by the antenna array, and that deliberately exploiting coupling effects through the proposed architecture yields substantial improvements in both spectral efficiency and nonlinear harvested energy compared to standard hybrid precoding, while requiring only a fraction of the hardware cost.
items.citation: Thien Duc Hua, Mohammadali Mohammadi, Hien Quoc Ngo et al.. Tri-Hybrid SWIPT with Reconfigurable Parasitic Antennas. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Multistate Analysis of Longitudinal Care Outcomes Among People Newly Linked to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Care in Missouri.
items.summary: This study examined longitudinal patterns of HIV care engagement and viral suppression among people newly linked to HIV care in St. Louis, Missouri, a priority jurisdiction under the Ending the HIV Epidemic initiative. Using multistate analytic methods, researchers tracked individuals across nine mutually exclusive care states defined by clinic engagement and viral load status over three years following initial linkage to care. The analysis revealed that by one year post-linkage, roughly half of patients remained continuously retained, while substantial proportions had either disengaged or reengaged with care, with viral suppression rates being notably lower among reengaged compared to continuously retained individuals. Younger individuals and those from historically marginalized communities faced greater risk of disengagement, reengagement, and viremia. The authors conclude that conventional cross-sectional reporting obscures important cyclical patterns of care disruption, and that HIV care interventions should prioritize sustained long-term engagement rather than focusing narrowly on preventing isolated missed appointments.
items.citation: Ramakrishnan A, Vo D, Barrette EP et al.. A Multistate Analysis of Longitudinal Care Outcomes Among People Newly Linked to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Care in Missouri.. Open forum infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Association Between Housing Instability and HIV Care Outcomes Among People With HIV in the United States.
items.summary: This study examined how housing instability affects HIV clinical outcomes among people with HIV who are already engaged in care across the United States. Using clinical data and patient-reported measures from a large multi-site cohort collected between 2019 and 2025, researchers applied regression models to assess associations between self-reported housing status and outcomes including viral suppression, antiretroviral therapy use and adherence, and CD4 cell counts. Nearly one in ten individuals in active clinical care reported some form of housing instability, including unstable housing, homelessness, or uncertainty about their situation. Those experiencing homelessness or unstable housing had meaningfully lower rates of viral suppression, antiretroviral use, adherence, and CD4 counts compared to stably housed individuals, with findings consistent across subgroups defined by substance use and depression status. The authors conclude that lack of stable housing represents a structural barrier to HIV management even among those nominally engaged in care, with implications for efforts to end the HIV epidemic in the United States.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Fahey CA, Whitney BM, Drumright LN et al.. Association Between Housing Instability and HIV Care Outcomes Among People With HIV in the United States.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: Patterns of Workplace Absenteeism Across Levels of Virological Failure Among Employed Adults Co-Infected with HIV and Pulmonary Tuberculosis in the Govan Mbeki Sub-District, South Africa: A Retrospective Record Review.
items.summary: This study investigated whether the severity of virological failure is associated with workplace absenteeism among employed adults co-infected with HIV and pulmonary tuberculosis in a high-burden region of South Africa. Using a retrospective record review, researchers linked clinical and laboratory data to workplace sick-leave registers for mine workers who had documented virological failure after at least six months of antiretroviral therapy, categorizing participants by viral load level and classifying absenteeism as high or low based on sick-leave days over a three-month period. After adjusting for demographic and socioeconomic factors, viral load category was not independently associated with high absenteeism, and the overall regression model did not reach statistical significance. The findings indicate that while both high-level virological failure and elevated absenteeism were common in this cohort, the two were not detectably linked after adjustment, with the authors noting that healthy-worker selection bias, limited exposure contrast, and residual confounding restrict causal conclusions. The authors recommend integrated public health and workplace interventions to simultaneously address treatment outcomes and workforce participation in settings with a high burden of HIV and tuberculosis co-infection.
items.citation: Mabunda T, Singh T. Patterns of Workplace Absenteeism Across Levels of Virological Failure Among Employed Adults Co-Infected with HIV and Pulmonary Tuberculosis in the Govan Mbeki Sub-District, South Africa: A Retrospective Record Review.. Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *Plasmodium vivax* co-circulate, and where conventional HRP2-based tests are undermined by low parasite densities and gene deletions. Researchers enrolled febrile patients from health facilities during peak transmission season and compared the new Bioline Malaria multi-antigen RDT, which detects HRP2 and dual pLDH antigens for both species, against expert microscopy and quantitative PCR. The multi-antigen RDT performed well relative to microscopy, achieving high sensitivity and specificity with near-perfect agreement, but its sensitivity dropped notably when qPCR served as the reference standard. This decline reflects the test's inability to reliably detect submicroscopic, low-density infections that qPCR identified at the highest overall prevalence. The authors conclude that while the multi-antigen RDT is suitable for routine clinical diagnosis, more sensitive tools are needed for malaria surveillance and elimination efforts in co-endemic settings.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Dynamics and ecology of a multistage expansion of Oropouche virus in Brazil
items.summary: This paper investigated the unprecedented Oropouche virus outbreak that emerged in Brazil in 2024, driven by a reassortant viral lineage spreading beyond its historical Amazon Basin range. The researchers combined phylogeographic analyses with ecological niche modelling to characterize how the virus dispersed and what environmental conditions facilitated its expansion into new territories. Their findings revealed a multiscale dispersal process involving both short-range diffusion and long-distance jumps consistent with air travel-mediated spread. Key environmental drivers of range expansion included banana and cocoa cultivation, temperature, the predicted habitat suitability of the primary midge vector, and human population density, with the virus having circulated in ecologically suitable areas before its explosive epidemic emergence. The study raises concern about high ecological suitability for the virus along the Brazilian coast and underscores the likely role of human mobility in enabling the pathogen to colonize new regions.
items.citation: Houriiyah Tegally, Simon Dellicour, Jenicca Poongavanan et al.. Dynamics and ecology of a multistage expansion of Oropouche virus in Brazil. Nature Ecology & Evolution. 2026

items.title: Selecting nanocarrier platforms for drug delivery: a criteria-based, translational review integrating CQA/CMC and immune interactions
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of nanocarrier platforms used in drug delivery, assessing how different systems can be rationally selected for clinical translation rather than evaluated in isolation. The authors comparatively analyzed major platforms including liposomes, micelles, solid lipid nanoparticles, polymeric nanoparticles, dendrimers, carbon nanotubes, and metallic nanoparticles across dimensions such as cargo compatibility, targeting strategies, release mechanisms, and routes of administration. A central focus was placed on critical quality attributes and chemistry, manufacturing, and controls parameters—including particle size, surface chemistry, encapsulation efficiency, stability, and batch reproducibility—as essential determinants of clinical success alongside nanoscale properties. The review also highlighted key biological barriers to translation, particularly immune interactions such as protein corona formation, complement activation, and long-term biotransformation uncertainties, which can undermine safety and efficacy even when nanoscale design is optimized. The authors conclude that no single nanocarrier platform is universally superior, and instead advocate for a criteria-based selection framework that matches platform choice to the specific therapeutic indication, administration route, cargo type, and product development requirements.
items.citation: Reyhan Hocaoğlu, Kaan Zıkşahna, Murat Ihlamur. Selecting nanocarrier platforms for drug delivery: a criteria-based, translational review integrating CQA/CMC and immune interactions. Health Nanotechnology. 2026

items.title: The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles
items.summary: This study addressed the challenge that a large proportion of the *Plasmodium falciparum* proteome lacks known subcellular location or function, which limits understanding of malaria parasite biology. Using a spatial proteomics approach called hyperplexed Localisation of Organelle Proteins by Isotopic Tagging (hyperLOPIT), the researchers generated high-resolution maps of protein subcellular localization for the invasive erythrocytic schizont stage of *P. falciparum*. The approach resolved a large number of distinct cellular compartments, including sites within the host erythrocyte, and used supervised machine learning to assign thousands of proteins to specific niches. The resulting dataset substantially expands knowledge of where parasite proteins reside within the cell, including organelles critical for red blood cell invasion. By integrating these spatial data with comparative genomic analyses, the authors also illuminate the evolutionary trajectories that have shaped organelle composition across *Plasmodium* species and identify ongoing adaptive pressures relevant to disease management.
items.citation: Scott A. Chisholm, Victor Flores, Alison Kemp et al.. The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Real‐world comprehensive care of people living with schizophrenia: recommendations across different settings and clinical stages
items.summary: This paper addresses the global challenge of managing schizophrenia by developing the first comprehensive, real-world care recommendations spanning diverse clinical stages, treatment approaches, and resource settings. The recommendations were generated through a critical review of scientific literature combined with collaborative input from clinical academics treating people with schizophrenia across multiple countries, including those in the Global South, as well as individuals with lived experience of the disorder. The resulting framework identifies eleven key domains of care, ranging from early detection and pharmacological treatment to psychosocial interventions, community care, and population-level prevention. A central overarching recommendation is to implement evidence-based, culturally sensitive care that reduces disparities between high- and low-resource settings, utilizing task-sharing models that incorporate non-professional health workers and traditional healers. The paper also emphasizes that meaningful progress requires improved mental health funding, better access to care, attention to social determinants of health, and the future integration of scalable digital solutions.
items.citation: Paolo Fusar‐Poli, Toby Pillinger, Robert Ali McCutcheon et al.. Real‐world comprehensive care of people living with schizophrenia: recommendations across different settings and clinical stages. World Psychiatry. 2026

items.title: Malnutrition and double burden of disease: the African dilemma of non-communicable disease
items.summary: This review examined the double burden of malnutrition in Africa, where undernutrition and overnutrition coexist and together drive rising rates of non-communicable diseases. The authors conducted a narrative review of peer-reviewed literature, institutional datasets, and global health reports spanning a quarter century to synthesize evidence on the prevalence, biological mechanisms, and socio-environmental determinants of this dual burden. They found that undernutrition, reflected in high rates of stunting, wasting, and underweight among young children, persists alongside rapidly increasing overweight and obesity, particularly in urban settings. Biological pathways involving early-life nutritional deprivation, micronutrient deficiencies, and obesity-induced inflammation interact with food insecurity, urbanization, and socioeconomic inequality to elevate non-communicable disease risk. The authors conclude that addressing this challenge requires coordinated, context-specific, multisectoral strategies encompassing community nutrition programs, food fortification, fiscal policies, and integration of nutrition and disease prevention across health, agriculture, and social protection systems.
items.citation: Daniel Omeodisemi Omokpariola, Cecilia Agbanu-Kumordzi, Gloria Omoefe et al.. Malnutrition and double burden of disease: the African dilemma of non-communicable disease. Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems. 2026

items.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
items.summary: This paper investigated whether language models can effectively navigate large document networks by treating information retrieval as a graph traversal problem, using the Wikipedia Game as a testbed. The researchers compared sentence embedding models and large language models across multiple Wikipedia language editions and academic literature datasets, constructing large local graphs of Wikipedia pages and paper citation networks to enable evaluation without dependence on third-party APIs. Models were benchmarked against human players and a TF-IDF baseline, with performance assessed on the ability to reach a target article by following links. No model significantly surpassed human performance, though a small group of frontier reasoning and large language models achieved comparable success rates. Performance and model rankings varied meaningfully across languages and subject domains, with practical implications for deploying these techniques in real-world information retrieval contexts.
items.citation: Alexander Hickey, Joanna Knight, James Bishop. Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Can machines reason non-verbally?
items.summary: The paper investigates whether machines can perform visual, non-verbal reasoning — tasks such as completing abstract patterns or delineating ambiguous regions of interest — which remain difficult even for advanced AI systems that excel at language-based reasoning. The core challenge identified is that visual reasoning involves implicit intermediate steps that lack clear verification methods, unlike verbal reasoning where logic or automated tests can check correctness. To address this, the authors introduce GenVerOpt, a framework that integrates generation, verification, and iterative optimisation into a unified pipeline, enabling models to propose candidate solutions, assess their correctness, and refine them on a per-sample basis rather than relying on patterns learned during training. Tested across multiple domains, GenVerOpt surpassed human performance on abstract IQ puzzles, matched clinicians in prostate cancer segmentation, exceeded expert performance in liver vessel reconstruction, and outperformed leading approaches in tumour boundary delineation. The authors conclude that machine reasoning can meaningfully extend beyond language, positioning visual non-verbal reasoning as a key component of more flexible and generalisable artificial intelligence.
items.citation: Shaheer U. Saeed, Zion Tse, Gregory Slabaugh et al.. Can machines reason non-verbally?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale census of emission-line galaxies using JWST's near-infrared slitless spectroscopy mode to study star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across a wide range of cosmic epochs. The researchers used the COSMOS-3D program to conduct wide-field slitless spectroscopic observations over a large contiguous sky area, combining grism spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging to identify and characterize sources across redshifts from zero to nine. To overcome the source confusion problem inherent to slitless spectroscopy, they developed a multi-step identification framework that incorporates convolutional neural networks and large language models to automate and improve upon the human identification process. The resulting catalog contains over twelve thousand objects with spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties, detecting a broad suite of emission lines spanning from oxygen and hydrogen recombination lines to molecular features. Composite spectra constructed in multiple redshift bins additionally reveal faint spectral features—including higher-order hydrogen lines, CO absorption bands, and iron emission—that are undetectable in individual spectra, demonstrating the power of wide-field slitless spectroscopy for building large, unbiased samples for galaxy evolution studies.
items.citation: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al.. A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS. arXiv. 2026

items.title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
items.summary: This paper presents DyssomniaNN, a computational framework designed to model human sleep disorders and the disconnect between objective sleep duration and subjective feelings of restedness. The model integrates multiple levels of biological organization, combining classical sleep regulatory theories governing homeostatic and circadian drives with a hypothalamic flip-flop circuit and a recurrent corticothalamic spiking neural network. The framework was applied to simulate five clinical populations over a standardized multi-day photoperiod, and the resulting synthetic brain activity closely matched empirical electroencephalography recordings across standard frequency bands. A novel metric called the Well-Rested Index was introduced to quantify how restorative sleep actually is, revealing that total sleep time alone is a poor predictor of recovery. Notably, simulations reproduced clinically recognized phenomena such as normal sleep duration with low restoration in paradoxical insomnia due to persistent cortical beta-band activity, and severe nocturnal fragmentation with frequent sleep-onset rapid eye movement periods in narcolepsy, positioning the framework as a platform for mechanistic research and virtual drug testing.
items.citation: Daniel Szelogowski. DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates the role of sub-volume sampling strategies in self-supervised learning for three-dimensional medical images, challenging the common assumption that random cropping treats all spatial regions as equally informative. The authors first demonstrate through controlled crop-quality experiments that the quality of sampled sub-volumes directly influences downstream transfer performance, identifying the observation policy as a previously overlooked bottleneck. To address this, they propose a plug-and-play framework that reformulates sub-volume sampling as a "where-to-look" problem, replacing random cropping with an offline coarse-to-fine probe bank that selects crops guided by anatomy-awareness, informativeness, and diversity. The framework is instantiated in two variants—a lightweight version using geometric and image-statistical cues and a diagnostic version using frozen visual features—to assess whether simple volume-intrinsic priors are sufficient or whether richer semantic information provides additional benefit. Experiments across multiple backbones and downstream tasks show that the lightweight variant consistently outperforms random sampling, with mechanistic analyses attributing the gains to more anatomically plausible sampling, reduced spatial redundancy, more efficient learning dynamics, and more structured learned representations.
items.citation: Junkai Liu, Le Zhang. Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
items.summary: This paper introduces RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework for recursive self-improvement that uses predictive world models to guide both action selection and learning-data curation, allowing policies and workflows to improve iteratively from interaction experience. The framework incorporates observed feedback to drive policy updates and conditional world-model adaptation, with compatibility checks determining whether updated policy-model pairs should be retained. Evaluated across multiple computational and scientific domains—including code repair, graphical user interface navigation, laboratory planning, and chemical reaction optimization—the framework consistently outperformed static or baseline approaches. Notable results include more than doubling laboratory-planning scores across successive policy versions and achieving substantially higher reaction yields compared to Bayesian optimization under the same experimental budget. The authors conclude that combining predictive world models with principled retention of system updates enables robust recursive self-improvement across diverse and heterogeneous environments.
items.citation: Taoyong Cui, Pinxian Zeng, Wanghan Xu et al.. RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis Detection with MiniDock MTB Using Swab Samples
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and usability of a novel tuberculosis diagnostic tool called MiniDock MTB, designed for use in peripheral health settings where improved diagnostics are critically needed. Researchers conducted a prospective, cross-sectional study across seven countries, enrolling patients aged twelve and older with presumptive pulmonary tuberculosis and testing them using both sputum swabs and tongue swabs, with sputum culture serving as the reference standard. MiniDock MTB demonstrated high sensitivity with sputum swabs and somewhat lower but still substantial sensitivity with tongue swabs, while specificity exceeded the threshold for both sample types, meeting World Health Organization accuracy targets for near-point-of-care tuberculosis diagnostics. Its sensitivity was comparable to the Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay and markedly superior to sputum-smear microscopy for both sample types. The test also received good usability ratings from those who administered it, and no adverse events were reported, supporting its potential suitability for deployment in diverse clinical settings.
items.citation: Seda Yerlikaya, Masuzyo Chirwa, Bukola Ajide et al.. Pulmonary Tuberculosis Detection with MiniDock MTB Using Swab Samples. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether pooling sputum specimens for molecular tuberculosis testing could expand diagnostic access without requiring additional laboratory infrastructure. Conducted prospectively across seven countries using facility-based and community-based case finding, it compared pooled Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing of two, three, or four specimens against individual Xpert Ultra testing, using culture as the reference standard. Pooled testing demonstrated slightly higher specificity than individual testing but modestly lower sensitivity, with agreement between the two approaches remaining high for specimens with medium to high bacterial loads while declining notably for very low and trace grade results. Crucially, pooled testing reduced cartridge consumption by approximately half compared to individual testing. The authors conclude that pooled tuberculosis testing could meaningfully expand access to WHO-recommended molecular diagnostics in low-to-moderate prevalence settings without requiring new infrastructure.
items.citation: Garg T, Sander M, Byrne RL et al.. Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.. The Lancet. Global health. 2027

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This review synthesizes major advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research from 2020 to 2025, reflecting on how this evidence has shaped updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance into a single unified framework. Key developments include the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a frontline screening and triage tool, and the broadened deployment of decentralised molecular diagnostics such as low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests across diverse specimen types. Notably, innovations including tongue swabs, sputum pooling, and the use of non-sputum specimens such as stool and nasopharyngeal samples have improved bacteriological confirmation in children and other populations with difficulty producing sputum, while targeted next-generation sequencing has been endorsed for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level. Urine lipoarabinomannan assays offer diagnostic benefit in people with HIV and advanced disease, though performance limitations restrict wider application, and host blood transcriptomic and other biomarkers show promise for prognosis and triage but none yet meet WHO target product profile criteria for reliably distinguishing infection from disease at the point of care. The review concludes that substantial gaps in diagnostic performance, implementation, and equity persist, particularly for detecting subclinical tuberculosis, identifying priority areas for future research and development.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.summary: This narrative review examines how the diagnosis of tuberculosis in people with HIV has evolved from 1990 to the present. The paper describes the particular diagnostic challenges posed by HIV-associated tuberculosis, including lower bacillary loads in sputum, high rates of extrapulmonary and disseminated disease, and nonspecific clinical features that overlap with other opportunistic infections, all of which historically led to both underdiagnosis and overdiagnosis. The authors trace the transition from smear microscopy—which has reduced sensitivity in people with HIV—through the development of nucleic acid amplification tests and the urine lipoarabinomannan lateral flow assay, alongside the broader impact of antiretroviral therapy on reducing tuberculosis incidence and mortality. Despite these advances, the review concludes that no currently available rapid test achieves ideal sensitivity, and only urine lipoarabinomannan detection combines affordability with point-of-care suitability. The authors therefore argue that further development of accurate, affordable, and deployable point-of-care diagnostics remains an urgent priority.
items.venue: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
items.citation: Maartens G. The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.. South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde. 2026

items.title: Development and validation of a blood-based diagnostic model for pulmonary tuberculosis combining GBP5 expression and routine laboratory indicators.
items.summary: This study addressed the challenge of diagnosing active pulmonary tuberculosis, where conventional laboratory methods suffer from poor sensitivity and miss many cases. Using a retrospective case-control design, the researchers built a blood-based diagnostic model by combining expression levels of the guanylate-binding protein 5 gene with routine laboratory indicators—white blood cell count, platelet count, and prothrombin time—identified through logistic regression analysis. An AdaBoost machine learning algorithm was used to construct the model, which was trained and tested on a cohort of patients with active tuberculosis or other pulmonary diseases. The resulting model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve exceeding 0.80 in both training and test sets, outperforming conventional diagnostic methods such as smear microscopy, culture, Xpert MTB/RIF, and interferon-gamma release assay. The authors conclude that this non-sputum, blood-based AdaBoost model shows promise as a rapid clinical diagnostic tool for active tuberculosis, though validation in larger patient cohorts is needed before clinical implementation.
items.citation: Zhao M, Hu Q, Wang Q et al.. Development and validation of a blood-based diagnostic model for pulmonary tuberculosis combining GBP5 expression and routine laboratory indicators.. Medicine. 2026

items.title: Near-point-of-care Diagnosis of Tuberculosis With LyocartE MTB Assay: a Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
items.summary: The study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of the LyocartE assay, a near point-of-care tuberculosis test, using both sputum and tongue swab specimens across multiple clinical sites in China. In a prospective multicenter design, consecutive individuals with presumptive tuberculosis were enrolled and tested with LyocartE alongside established comparators including Xpert Ultra, smear microscopy, and culture. Against a composite microbiological reference standard, LyocartE on sputum achieved high sensitivity and specificity, performing comparably to Xpert Ultra. Tongue swab specimens, which offer a non-invasive alternative to sputum collection, also yielded strong diagnostic performance with notably high specificity, and LyocartE results correlated well with Xpert Ultra cycle threshold values across both specimen types. The authors conclude that LyocartE is a promising rapid diagnostic tool for tuberculosis, though further evaluation in asymptomatic and paucibacillary populations is needed.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Ma Z, Yu X, Yu Y et al.. Near-point-of-care Diagnosis of Tuberculosis With LyocartE MTB Assay: a Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of performing differential expression analysis on large-scale single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic datasets spanning hundreds of subjects and millions of cells. The authors developed an open-source R package called dreamlet, which employs a pseudobulk approach based on precision-weighted linear mixed models to identify differentially expressed genes associated with traits across cell clusters. The method is designed to handle complex statistical models while controlling false positive rates, and benchmarking showed it to be substantially faster and more memory-efficient than existing workflows. The package was validated on published datasets and applied to a novel large-scale dataset of over a million single nuclei from postmortem brain tissue of Alzheimer's disease cases and controls, demonstrating both its computational scalability and statistical utility for disease-focused transcriptomic studies.
items.citation: Gabriel E. Hoffman, Donghoon Lee, Jaroslav M. Bendl et al.. Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise affect the expression of Toll-like receptors (TLRs), immune cell receptors that trigger inflammatory signalling cascades and are implicated in chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary lifestyles and non-communicable diseases. The authors conducted a comprehensive search across multiple databases, ultimately including dozens of studies categorized by exercise type and duration, spanning acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined training modalities. They found that acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise showed less activating potential, with many responses being neutral or downregulatory, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined exercise programs predominantly resulted in unchanged or decreased TLR levels, whereas chronic aerobic exercise produced mixed but mostly neutral effects on TLR expression. The authors concluded that exercise modulates TLR signalling in a manner dependent on exercise characteristics, though substantial heterogeneity in study designs limits firm conclusions and calls for further standardized research to clarify underlying mechanisms and pathophysiological implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
items.summary: This paper investigated whether language models can effectively navigate large document networks by playing the Wikipedia Game, in which a player must travel from one article to a target article using only hyperlinks. The researchers tested sentence embedding models and large language models across multiple Wikipedia language editions and academic literature citation networks, constructing large local graphs using publicly available data to avoid dependence on external APIs. Model performance was benchmarked against both human players and a term-frequency baseline. No model significantly outperformed humans, though several top-performing models achieved comparable success rates. Performance and rankings varied considerably across languages and subject domains, with implications for how practitioners deploy these models in real-world information retrieval tasks.
items.citation: Alexander Hickey, Joanna Knight, James Bishop. Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Can machines reason non-verbally?
items.summary: The paper investigates whether machines can perform visual, non-verbal reasoning — a domain where even advanced language-capable systems struggle with tasks such as completing abstract patterns or delineating ambiguous regions of interest. The core challenge identified is that visual reasoning involves implicit intermediate steps that lack clear verification methods, unlike the explicit, checkable steps of verbal reasoning. To address this, the authors introduce GenVerOpt, a framework that integrates generation, verification, and iterative optimisation into a unified pipeline, enabling models to propose candidate solutions, assess their correctness, and refine them on a per-sample basis rather than relying purely on patterns learned during training. Tested across diverse domains, GenVerOpt surpasses human performance on abstract IQ puzzles, matches clinical experts in prostate cancer segmentation, and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in liver vessel reconstruction and tumour boundary alignment. The authors conclude that machine reasoning can be meaningfully extended beyond language, positioning visual non-verbal reasoning as a key component of more general and flexible artificial intelligence.
items.citation: Shaheer U. Saeed, Zion Tse, Gregory Slabaugh et al.. Can machines reason non-verbally?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale census of emission-line galaxies using JWST near-infrared slitless spectroscopy from the COSMOS-3D program, covering a contiguous area and targeting a wide redshift range from essentially the local universe out to the epoch of reionization. The researchers combined wide-field slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging to build a homogeneous sample of over twelve thousand spectroscopically confirmed objects, reaching very faint line-flux limits. To overcome the source confusion that is inherent to slitless spectroscopy, they developed a multi-step identification framework that incorporates convolutional neural networks and large language models to replicate and streamline the human identification process. The resulting catalog delivers spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties, with detections spanning numerous emission lines that enable continuous coverage of galaxy populations across cosmic time. By stacking spectra in redshift bins, the study also recovers faint features such as higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and iron lines that are undetectable in individual spectra, demonstrating the broad utility of wide-field slitless spectroscopy for studying galaxy evolution and AGN activity at scale.
items.citation: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al.. A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS. arXiv. 2026

items.title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
items.summary: This paper presents DyssomniaNN, a computational framework designed to model human sleep disorders and the disconnect between objective sleep duration and subjective restorative quality. The model integrates established theories of sleep-wake regulation, including homeostatic and circadian drive processes and hypothalamic flip-flop switching circuitry, with a recurrent corticothalamic spiking neural network to simulate sleep dynamics across multiple biological scales. Five clinical cohorts were simulated over a standardized multi-day period, encompassing healthy sleepers and individuals with delayed-phase circadian disorder, chronic insomnia, paradoxical insomnia, and narcolepsy type one. The synthetic neural activity generated by the model was validated against empirical human electroencephalography data, showing close spectral agreement, and a novel metric called the Well-Rested Index was introduced to quantify how restorative sleep actually is. Key findings demonstrate that total sleep time alone poorly predicts restoration, as paradoxical insomnia can yield normal sleep duration yet low restorative quality due to persistent cortical beta-band activity, while narcolepsy produces severe nocturnal fragmentation and abnormal rapid eye movement intrusions consistent with hypocretin deficiency.
items.citation: Daniel Szelogowski. DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates the role of sub-volume sampling strategies in self-supervised learning for three-dimensional medical images, arguing that the conventional practice of random cropping is a previously overlooked bottleneck. The authors first demonstrate through controlled experiments that crop quality directly influences downstream transfer performance, motivating a reframing of the problem as a "where-to-look" decision. They propose a plug-and-play framework that replaces random cropping with an offline, coarse-to-fine probe bank that selects sub-volumes guided by principles of anatomy-awareness, informativeness, and diversity. Two variants are introduced—a lightweight version relying on geometric and image-statistical cues, and a diagnostically richer version leveraging frozen visual features—to assess whether simple intrinsic priors are sufficient or whether semantic features provide additional benefit. Extensive experiments across multiple backbones and downstream tasks show that the lightweight variant consistently outperforms random sampling, with mechanistic analyses attributing the gains to more anatomically plausible observations, reduced spatial redundancy, improved learning dynamics, and more structured learned representations.
items.citation: Junkai Liu, Le Zhang. Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
items.summary: This paper introduces RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework designed to enable recursive self-improvement in AI systems by using predictive world models to guide both action selection and learning-data curation. The framework builds on JEPA-Anything and addresses the core challenges of costly external feedback and model reliability degradation by combining observed feedback with conditional world-model adaptation, alongside compatibility checks to govern when updated policy-model pairs should be retained. The approach was evaluated across a range of computational and scientific domains including code repair, graphical user interface navigation, laboratory planning, and chemical reaction optimization. Across these domains, RSI-Anything demonstrated consistent and substantial performance gains, such as more than doubling laboratory-planning scores across successive policy versions and outperforming Bayesian optimization in reaction yield under equivalent experimental budgets. The authors conclude that predictive world models combined with principled system update retention enable effective recursive improvement across diverse and heterogeneous environments.
items.citation: Taoyong Cui, Pinxian Zeng, Wanghan Xu et al.. RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A case for eliminating Widal testing for enteric fever, India.
items.venue: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
items.citation: Walia K, Gopalakrishnan R, Rupali P et al.. A case for eliminating Widal testing for enteric fever, India.. Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 2026

items.title: Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.
items.summary: This narrative review examined how emergency departments in the United States can improve the diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of bacterial sexually transmitted infections, specifically chlamydia, gonorrhea, and syphilis. The authors searched the published literature spanning several decades and identified a set of studies evaluating various intervention types in emergency department settings. They found that universal screening substantially increased testing and case detection, electronic health record prompts enhanced screening uptake, and point-of-care testing enabled same-day diagnosis and treatment while reducing unnecessary antibiotic use. Bundled interventions that addressed multiple steps in the care pathway appeared to have the greatest overall impact, though heterogeneity across studies made direct comparisons difficult. The authors conclude that future research should prioritize implementation feasibility, sustainability, health equity, and cost-effectiveness across diverse emergency department contexts.
items.citation: Andonian KS, Giri H, Goodman GR et al.. Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.. Sexually transmitted diseases. 2026

items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This pilot study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending a non-governmental organisation-led clinic on the outskirts of Beirut, while also assessing their knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to sexual health. Using a cross-sectional design over four months, researchers offered sexual health consultations alongside an anonymous questionnaire covering STI knowledge, condom use, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived HIV-related stigma. The cohort was predominantly young, educated Lebanese and Syrian men, among whom a notable proportion were living with HIV. Despite high levels of STI and HIV awareness, participants frequently reported condomless sex and recreational drug use, with perceived stigma identified as a key barrier to testing-seeking behaviour. The study concludes that integrating point-of-care testing into community sexual health services enables same-day diagnosis, counselling, and linkage to care, and underscores the need to address HIV-related stigma to reduce risky behaviours in this population.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.
items.summary: This study examined the costs of integrating point-of-care screening for three curable sexually transmitted infections into antenatal care in Zimbabwe, where such infections are associated with adverse birth outcomes but cost data have been lacking. Researchers implemented screening at two primary healthcare clinics in Harare and used a combination of study records, staff interviews, time-and-motion studies, and secondary sources to estimate economic costs from a health system perspective, comparing point-of-care testing against modelled syndromic management as the standard of care. Because high-volume implementation proved operationally infeasible during the study, a low-volume routine care scenario was modelled over a twelve-month period. The composite prevalence of the three infections was substantial, and the largest cost drivers were test kits and personnel, which together accounted for the majority of total intervention costs. The authors conclude that reducing the cost of point-of-care diagnostics will be essential for making such antenatal screening strategies economically viable.
items.citation: Martin K, Bath D, Nyamwanza R et al.. Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction
items.summary: This thesis examines cyberpunk fiction through the interlocking lenses of cybernetics, the Gothic, and theories of fiction, questioning the established claim that cyberpunk represents the supreme literary expression of postmodernism or late capitalism. Drawing on Baudrillard's theories of simulation and Deleuze-Guattari's materialist reworking of the Gothic — derived from Worringer's concept of nonorganic continuum rather than conventional supernatural literary traditions — the study develops a framework it terms "Gothic materialism" and "hypernaturalism." Key cyberpunk texts including Blade Runner, Videodrome, Neuromancer, and The Atrocity Exhibition are analysed through this framework, with the argument that these works are centrally preoccupied with the dissolution of boundaries between the animate and the inanimate. The thesis introduces the concept of the "flatline" — signifying simultaneously a state of undeath and a condition of radical immanence — as the point where cyberpunk converges Gothic and cybernetic concerns around catatonic states, bodies exceeding their own boundaries, and agency without subjectivity. Across four chapters addressing the flatlining of cybernetics, the body, reproduction, and fiction itself, the thesis argues that cyberpunk is better understood as "imploded science fiction" that destabilises both theory and fiction as distinct genres in the age of cybernetic simulation.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Mark Fisher. Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: Girls, gifts, and gender : an ethnography of the materiality of care in rural Mpumalanga, South Africa
items.summary: This ethnographic thesis examined social relations of care involving young people in rural South Africa during the AIDS epidemic and amid rising economic inequality, drawing on fieldwork conducted in the Agincourt area. The research focused on three forms of gift exchange: children's labour rendered in return for guardian care, girls' labour and sexual favours exchanged for material support from older males, and the local construction of "orphan" identities to attract charitable gifts from tourist-philanthropists. Data were gathered through work with non-profit organisations serving orphans and vulnerable children, participant households, and a range of stakeholders including government workers, faith-based leaders, and private game lodge operators running youth development initiatives. The thesis develops the concept of the "materiality of care" to argue that care practices must be understood through local perspectives and within the broader historical and political-economic context shaped by AIDS and poverty. The findings contribute to critiques of orphan-targeted interventions in sub-Saharan Africa, contending that such interventions fail to account for the familial contexts of parentless children or the shared hardships facing both orphaned and non-orphaned young people.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Annalise Weckesser. Girls, gifts, and gender : an ethnography of the materiality of care in rural Mpumalanga, South Africa. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: These clinical practice guidelines address the ongoing burden of chronic hepatitis B infection in the Asia Pacific region, where the disease continues to drive significant morbidity and mortality through complications such as acute-on-chronic liver failure, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma despite decades of scientific progress. The guidelines were developed by a dedicated Viral Elimination Taskforce comprising key opinion leaders from member countries and regions under the auspices of APASL, incorporating shifts in disease epidemiology, socioeconomic factors, and technological advances. The resulting recommendations span thirteen major areas encompassing screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance. The overarching aim is to provide healthcare professionals, policy-makers, and patients with practical, cost-effective guidance to support elimination of the disease burden caused by chronic hepatitis B infection across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: DSS Colitis Model: Traps, Tricks, and Reporting Recommendations
items.summary: This review examines the dextran sodium sulfate colitis model, the most widely used experimental system for studying inflammatory bowel disease, focusing on the sources of variability and inconsistency that undermine reproducibility across studies. The authors synthesize existing knowledge on both intrinsic factors inherent to the model itself—including gut-brain and gut-liver axis interactions whereby locally induced colonic inflammation affects distant organ systems and their metabolism—and extrinsic factors such as environmental, microbiological, and genetic variables that further complicate experimental outcomes and data interpretation. The review identifies inconsistent reporting practices as a major barrier to comparing findings across studies and translating results to human disease. To address these challenges, the authors provide practical guidance in the form of a "traps and tricks" subsection and a checklist designed to help researchers better design, execute, and interpret DSS colitis experiments. The overarching conclusion is that meticulous attention to methodological nuance and standardized reporting are essential for improving the scientific rigor and translational relevance of this widely employed model.
items.citation: Martina Perše. DSS Colitis Model: Traps, Tricks, and Reporting Recommendations. Biomedicines. 2026

items.title: Moment closure approximations in epidemiology
items.summary: This thesis investigates moment closure approximations as deterministic tools for capturing spatial and network structure in epidemiological models, extending well beyond the static regular lattice settings where such methods were originally developed. The work derives novel moment closure formulations for dynamic network models and continuous space models, enabling deterministic tracking of low-order correlations—such as the disease-status correlation between neighbouring individuals—that traditional mean-field approaches cannot represent. The thesis examines the accuracy of these approximations near critical points and during transient phases, explores their application to sexually transmitted disease models on dynamic networks, and develops a preliminary pair approximation for populations distributed in continuous two-dimensional space. Comparisons are drawn between disease dynamics on regular lattices, dynamic networks, and continuous space to illuminate how the choice of spatial representation affects epidemiological outcomes. The author concludes that moment closure approximations remain a productive area of research and that their extension to more realistic spatial and network structures is both feasible and informative.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Christopher Thomas Bauch. Moment closure approximations in epidemiology. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
items.summary: This paper investigated whether language models can effectively navigate large document networks by playing the Wikipedia Game, where players must traverse from one article to another using only hyperlinks. The researchers evaluated sentence embedding models and large language models across multiple Wikipedia language editions and academic literature citation networks, constructing large local graphs using OpenAlex to enable testing without dependence on third-party APIs. Models were benchmarked against human players and a TF-IDF baseline across diverse languages and domains. No model significantly outperformed humans, though several frontier reasoning and instruction-tuned models achieved comparable performance. Notably, model performance and relative rankings varied considerably depending on the language and topic domain, with practical implications for deploying such models in real-world information retrieval contexts.
items.citation: Alexander Hickey, Joanna Knight, James Bishop. Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An entangling Hubbard quasiparticle collider on a digital quantum processor
items.summary: This paper investigates quasiparticle scattering in the Fermi-Hubbard model as a means of probing strongly correlated quantum systems. The researchers implemented a scattering experiment on a digital quantum processor, encoding a half-filled chain of sites onto qubits and colliding a doublon (doubly occupied site) with a holon (empty site). They measured the transmission probability of these quasiparticles and found it agrees with predictions from the Bethe-ansatz scattering matrix without any free parameters. Beyond scattering probabilities, the collision was shown to generate entanglement through superposition of transmitted and reflected components, as evidenced by particle-number fluctuations, while a control experiment colliding two identical doublons showed neither interaction dependence nor number fluctuation, consistent with indistinguishable-particle physics. The work establishes digital quantum processors as a viable experimental platform for studying the entanglement structure arising from quasiparticle scattering in strongly correlated models.
items.citation: Chan Bin Bark, Hanbyul Kim, Yoonil Koo et al.. An entangling Hubbard quasiparticle collider on a digital quantum processor. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Can machines reason non-verbally?
items.summary: The paper investigates whether machines can perform visual, non-verbal reasoning — a domain where even advanced large language and multimodal systems remain significantly limited compared to their verbal reasoning capabilities. The core challenge identified is that visual reasoning involves implicit intermediate steps that lack clear verification methods, unlike the explicit, checkable steps in language-based reasoning. To address this, the authors introduce GenVerOpt, a framework that integrates generation, verification, and iterative optimisation into a unified pipeline, enabling models to produce candidate solutions, assess their correctness, and refine them on a per-sample basis rather than relying purely on patterns learned during training. Testing across multiple domains — including abstract IQ-style pattern completion and medical image analysis tasks such as prostate cancer segmentation, liver vessel reconstruction, and tumour boundary delineation — the framework surpassed human performance on abstract puzzles, matched clinical experts in segmentation, and outperformed state-of-the-art methods in boundary alignment. The authors conclude that non-verbal visual reasoning is an achievable and important frontier for machine intelligence, with GenVerOpt demonstrating that machines can reason beyond language in a flexible and generalisable way.
items.citation: Shaheer U. Saeed, Zion Tse, Gregory Slabaugh et al.. Can machines reason non-verbally?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
items.summary: This paper introduces RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework designed to enable recursive self-improvement in artificial agents by using predictive world models to guide both action selection and learning-data curation. The framework builds on a predictive architecture where observed feedback drives improvements to policies or workflows and triggers conditional adaptation of the world model, with compatibility checks determining whether updated policy-model pairs should be retained. The approach was evaluated across a range of computational and scientific tasks including code repair, graphical user interface navigation, laboratory planning, and chemical reaction optimization. Across these domains, RSI-Anything consistently outperformed baseline methods, achieving notable gains such as more than doubling laboratory-planning scores across successive policy versions and substantially exceeding Bayesian optimization in reaction yield under equivalent experimental budgets. The authors argue that combining predictive world models with principled retention of system updates enables robust recursive improvement across diverse and evolving environments.
items.citation: Taoyong Cui, Pinxian Zeng, Wanghan Xu et al.. RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
items.summary: Vision-Language Models are widely used for image reasoning tasks, but this paper investigates whether their internal representations actually encode structured spatial relationships faithfully. The researchers developed a new metric called EICS to measure whether representations consistently encode concepts under controlled interventions, alongside a benchmark of causally controlled spatial perturbations derived from scene graphs. Testing across multiple VLM architectures, they found that spatial relations are represented far less faithfully than lexical information, even in models that perform well above chance on standard compositional benchmarks. Further analysis revealed that while relational information is detectable at individual predicate tokens, it is systematically lost when the sentence is aggregated into a global representation via end-of-sequence tokens or mean pooling. This exposes a fundamental failure that output-based evaluations cannot detect: the relational information present in model inputs does not survive into the downstream representations these models actually use for reasoning.
items.citation: Shubh Garg, Chen Shani. When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Revisiting Tabular Deep Regression: Objectives and the Limits of Global Early Stopping
items.summary: This paper investigates the choice of objective functions for deep learning regression on tabular data, an area that has received less scrutiny than model architecture selection. The authors conducted a systematic re-evaluation of multiple proposed regression objectives across a broad collection of tabular datasets and several neural network backbones, enabling fair comparison under controlled conditions. They found that many alternative objectives offer limited or inconsistent improvements over a well-tuned Mean Squared Error baseline, though quantile loss showed consistent aggregate gains across backbones. The study also identified a novel limitation whereby regions of the input space with differing levels of target noise reach their optimal predictive performance at different training epochs, meaning a single global early-stopping criterion forces an unfavorable trade-off across uncertainty regions. To address this, the authors proposed a heteroskedasticity-aware extension of quantile loss that incorporates input-dependent label smoothing, which improved performance over standard quantile loss on several backbones.
items.citation: Danil Rudenko, Georgii Bulgakov, Nikolay Kartashev et al.. Revisiting Tabular Deep Regression: Objectives and the Limits of Global Early Stopping. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.
items.summary: This study examined whether molecular (NAAT-based) testing for sexually transmitted infections provides better diagnostic yield when paired with molecular rather than conventional diagnoses of bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis in women with symptomatic vaginitis. The researchers compared STI detection rates for four pathogens across a large cohort of women whose vaginitis was diagnosed by clinician assessment, conventional laboratory methods, or molecular methods. Women who tested positive for bacterial vaginosis by NAAT had significantly higher rates of co-detected STIs compared to those whose bacterial vaginosis was identified by conventional laboratory criteria or clinician assessment alone, and a positive bacterial vaginosis NAAT result conferred a significantly elevated relative risk for any STI. A similar trend toward higher STI detection with molecular vulvovaginal candidiasis diagnosis was observed, though it did not reach statistical significance. The authors conclude that an all-molecular approach combining vaginitis and STI testing on a single specimen improves STI case-finding and risk stratification compared to conventional diagnostic methods or empirical clinical assessment.
items.citation: Getman D, Seña AC, Nenninger A et al.. Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic affected pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) adherence, HIV incidence, and sexually transmitted infection rates among adult men who newly initiated PrEP. Using a retrospective cohort analysis of commercially insured patients from an administrative claims database spanning the pre- and pandemic periods, researchers applied group-based trajectory modeling and weighted regression methods to compare outcomes between those who started PrEP before versus during the pandemic. Men who initiated PrEP during the pandemic showed meaningfully worse adherence patterns, with a higher proportion falling into early discontinuation trajectories compared to prepandemic initiators. Initiating PrEP during the pandemic was associated with a substantially elevated risk of HIV acquisition, while rates of sexually transmitted infections did not differ significantly between the two groups. The authors conclude that public health emergencies can undermine HIV prevention continuity and call for targeted strategies to sustain PrEP access and adherence during such disruptions.
items.venue: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
items.citation: Unigwe IF, Jenjai C, Goodin AJ et al.. Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.. Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy. 2026
