items.title: Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the current landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies used to detect and characterize pathogens responsible for infectious diseases. The paper covers two primary approaches: nucleic acid amplification methods, including polymerase chain reaction variants and isothermal amplification techniques, and next-generation sequencing for comprehensive genomic characterization. Advances in polymerase chain reaction are described in terms of improvements to speed, quantification, automation, and point-of-care applicability, while isothermal amplification methods are highlighted for their suitability in decentralized testing settings due to their constant-temperature operation. CRISPR-based detection systems are presented as an emerging complement to amplification methods, and next-generation sequencing is discussed for its capacity to identify novel pathogens, track outbreak transmission, and analyze microbiomes as potential disease biomarkers. The authors conclude that the future of molecular diagnostics lies in integrating these various technologies into hybrid platforms that address the current limitations of each individual approach.
items.citation: Takata M, Chikumi H, Yoshifuji A. Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.. Yonago acta medica. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in CRISPR/Cas Technologies for Biological Discovery, Therapeutics, and Diagnostics.
items.summary: This review examines the broad and rapidly evolving applications of CRISPR/Cas technology beyond its origins as a genome editing tool. The authors survey recent advances across functional genomic screening, epigenome editing, therapeutic target discovery, and molecular diagnostics, with particular attention to newer modalities such as CRISPRi, CRISPRa, base editing, and prime editing. These tools have deepened understanding of disease mechanisms and opened new avenues for therapeutic intervention in areas including cancer immunotherapy, infectious disease, and neurological disorders. In diagnostics, CRISPR-based platforms leverage programmable nuclease activity to enable sensitive detection of pathogens, cancer biomarkers, and genetic disorders in both laboratory and point-of-care settings. The review concludes that continued development of novel effectors and engineered variants is driving the technology toward personalized and precision medicine.
items.citation: Kim MS, Do HS, Jang HY et al.. Recent Advances in CRISPR/Cas Technologies for Biological Discovery, Therapeutics, and Diagnostics.. Biomolecules. 2026

items.title: Base-mismatched crRNA in CRISPR Enabled Universal One-pot Rapid Nucleic Acid Detection
items.summary: This paper investigated how to simplify CRISPR-Cas12a-based nucleic acid diagnostics from cumbersome two-step workflows into a single-tube, one-pot format suitable for field use. The researchers introduced deliberate single-nucleotide mismatches into the seed region of the CRISPR RNA, which suppresses premature cis-cleavage activity and thereby allows isothermal amplification and CRISPR detection to proceed simultaneously without requiring redesign of the protospacer adjacent motif or expensive modified reagents. Molecular dynamics simulations were used to guide selection of effective mismatches by correlating moderate potential energy variation with improved assay performance. Applying this strategy to detection of two bacterial pathogens, the system achieved sensitive detection at very low copy numbers within half an hour, with good specificity maintained across simulated environmental samples. The approach was further validated using lyophilized reagent pellets on battery-powered portable devices, demonstrating its potential as a broadly adaptable and cost-effective platform for infectious disease surveillance in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Jianhao X, Xin W, Bing Y et al.. Base-mismatched crRNA in CRISPR Enabled Universal One-pot Rapid Nucleic Acid Detection. 2026

items.title: Diagnostics for Hemorrhagic Fever Viruses: Lassa Fever as an Example.
items.citation: Dhar B, Espinoza N, Farzani T et al.. Diagnostics for Hemorrhagic Fever Viruses: Lassa Fever as an Example.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: HOMEBRED: A unified CRISPR platform for field-ready shadowing of infectious agents and oncogenic mutations.
items.summary: This paper introduced HOMEBRED, a CRISPR-based diagnostic platform designed to detect infectious disease agents and oncogenic mutations in resource-limited or field settings. The platform incorporates an automated guide RNA design tool called CaSilico, which identifies conserved genomic regions to generate mutation-resistant detection components, and pairs this with extraction-free sample processing for simplified deployment. The system was demonstrated for several applications, including visual detection of foot-and-mouth disease virus using only a handheld blue light, differentiation of *Brucella* vaccine strains from field isolates to address the longstanding challenge of distinguishing vaccinated from infected animals, and identification of BCR-ABL1 fusion transcripts relevant to cancer diagnosis. HOMEBRED uses a dual guide RNA architecture to achieve the specificity needed for these discrimination tasks. The authors claim the platform matches conventional PCR in sensitivity while offering reduced cost and complexity, making it suitable for point-of-care and veterinary field diagnostics.
items.citation: Asadbeigi A, Fazilaty H, Saffari M et al.. HOMEBRED: A unified CRISPR platform for field-ready shadowing of infectious agents and oncogenic mutations.. iScience. 2026

items.title: Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities
items.summary: This study investigated hybrid molecules called nucleopeptides, which are short peptides functionalized with DNA nucleobases, as building blocks for multicomponent low-molecular-weight hydrogels. The researchers synthesized a series of six nucleopeptides derived from two complementary peptide sequences, one negatively charged and one positively charged at physiological pH, each functionalized with one of the four DNA nucleobases introduced via a peptide nucleic acid moiety. By systematically combining these components, they examined how electrostatic complementarity between oppositely charged peptides and Watson-Crick base-pairing complementarity between nucleobases jointly influence hydrogel properties including gelation time, sol-gel transition temperature, mechanical stiffness, stress resistance, and fibrillar network morphology. The comprehensive multiscale analysis demonstrated that judicious selection of complementary components enables fine-tuning of hydrogel physicochemical and mechanical properties, while also revealing unexpected behaviors that highlight the complexity of these bioinspired multicomponent systems. The findings underscore the promise of nucleopeptide-based multicomponent hydrogels as a versatile platform for developing advanced supramolecular materials with biomedical and biotechnological applications.
items.citation: Tristan Giraud, Marine Koch, Paul Hoschtettler et al.. Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities. ACS Materials Au. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize how approaches spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics generate deep molecular insight into disease pathogenesis, while deep learning architectures decode these complex biological datasets to uncover hidden patterns and build predictive models. The review traces multiomics and AI applications across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Disease areas such as oncology, neurodegeneration, and cardiovascular conditions are used to illustrate how this convergence accelerates therapeutic innovation, though the authors acknowledge persistent challenges including data harmonization, reproducibility, and algorithmic bias. Overall, the review argues that combining multiomics with AI marks the beginning of a new era in bench-to-clinic translational medicine, enabling more precise therapeutic interventions grounded in comprehensive molecular understanding.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: A comprehensive survey of AI agents in healthcare
items.summary: This survey systematically maps the landscape of AI agents in healthcare, focusing on how general-purpose agentic frameworks characterized by autonomy, planning, and tool use must be adapted to meet the safety-critical demands of medical decision-making. The authors reviewed over two hundred recent studies drawn from major academic databases and developed a taxonomy organized around three pillars: the perception of multi-modal clinical data such as electronic health records, imaging, and genomics; core agent capabilities including tool use, reasoning, memory, and multi-agent collaboration; and an application ecosystem structured by stakeholder roles spanning clinicians, patients, researchers, and administrators. The review identifies exponential growth in the field and further examines evaluation frameworks and deployment readiness across technical, evidentiary, and governance dimensions. Despite this rapid expansion, the authors find that current research remains heavily concentrated in benchmark and controlled evaluation settings rather than real-world clinical deployment. They conclude that realizing the potential of healthcare AI agents will require substantial advances in reliability, privacy protection, governance, and operational integration before meaningful clinical translation can occur.
items.citation: Gelei Xu, Xueyang Li, Yixiong Chen et al.. A comprehensive survey of AI agents in healthcare. Journal of Biomedical Informatics. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined CRISPR-Cas systems as alternative antimicrobial strategies against multidrug-resistant bacteria, motivated by the global erosion of conventional antibiotic effectiveness. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental evidence across studies evaluating different CRISPR effectors, including Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, alongside various delivery platforms such as bacteriophages, conjugative plasmids, and nanoparticles. The review found that CRISPR-based approaches effectively killed or resensitized resistant bacteria through mechanisms including chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid elimination, and RNA-targeted cleavage, with phage-mediated delivery showing the most consistent efficacy in complex environments and animal models. One CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has already advanced to clinical evaluation, reflecting the translational momentum of this approach. Despite promising results, the authors identified significant barriers to clinical adoption, including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient long-term safety data, concluding that optimized delivery systems, multiplex targeting, and standardized regulatory frameworks are needed before widespread clinical use.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Targeting biofilm-driven antibiotic resistance: emerging mechanisms and next-generation therapeutic interventions
items.summary: This review paper examines how microbial biofilms contribute to antimicrobial resistance, a growing global health and economic crisis affecting both community and clinical environments. Biofilms enhance antibiotic tolerance through multiple mechanisms including restricted drug penetration, enzymatic antibiotic degradation, and facilitation of horizontal gene transfer, making infections extremely difficult to treat. The authors synthesize current understanding of these resistance mechanisms and critically note the absence of approved anti-biofilm therapeutics, underscoring an urgent gap in available treatments. The review then surveys a range of emerging therapeutic strategies being developed to address biofilm-driven resistance, encompassing nanotechnology, antimicrobial peptides, bacteriophage-derived enzymes, quorum-sensing inhibitors, CRISPR-based tools, microbiome engineering, and artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery. The authors argue that a multi-platform therapeutic approach combining these innovations offers the most promising path toward overcoming resistant biofilm infections.
items.citation: Abdulkarim Mbaraka, Ritu Raj Meena, Ekta Menghani et al.. Targeting biofilm-driven antibiotic resistance: emerging mechanisms and next-generation therapeutic interventions. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as smart platforms for targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical applications: an updated review
items.summary: This review examines MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as multifunctional platforms for biomedical and technological applications, with particular emphasis on targeted drug delivery and cancer treatment. The paper synthesizes current knowledge on how the exceptional electrical conductivity, flexibility, and biocompatibility of MXenes and their composites enable the construction of smart microrobots capable of precise navigation and controlled therapeutic release. The review also addresses how combining MXenes with quantum dots in polymer matrices merges electrical, optical, and catalytic properties to broaden utility across drug delivery, tissue engineering, flexible electronics, and energy storage. Stimuli-responsive polymers integrated into these systems allow controlled activation of therapeutic agents, and the ability to co-deliver multiple drugs offers potential for synergistic treatment strategies. The authors highlight persistent challenges including scalable production, material stability, and clinical translation, while affirming the transformative potential of these nanocomposites for biomedicine and sustainable technologies.
items.citation: Mohammad Hossein Karami, Omid Moini Jazani. MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as smart platforms for targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical applications: an updated review. Discover Nano. 2026

items.title: Noise Space Learning for VLA Adaptation
items.summary: This paper investigates how to adapt pretrained vision-language-action models to specific manipulation tasks without modifying the underlying model weights. The proposed approach, noise space learning, works by learning a context-conditioned distribution over the noise inputs used in flow-matching-based generative action models, effectively treating this noise space as an interface for adaptation that is compatible with multiple reinforcement learning algorithms including PPO, SAC, and AWR. The authors provide an information-theoretic analysis to explain why operating in the noise space enables efficient adaptation, and they empirically evaluate their methods across simulation benchmarks and real-robot manipulation tasks under constraints on interaction budget, computational resources, and execution safety. Their findings yield a suite of noise space learning variants along with practical guidelines for selecting among them depending on available resources and deployment conditions.
items.citation: Junjie Lu, Chuheng Zhang, Yucen Wang et al.. Noise Space Learning for VLA Adaptation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit
items.summary: This paper reports the discovery and characterization of a very wide-orbit binary lens system identified through gravitational microlensing. By cross-matching microlensing event catalogs from two major surveys spanning over a decade, the authors identified an event exhibiting two short-lived brightness bumps separated by more than eight years in its light curve. Through systematic evaluation of competing interpretations — including a binary-lens single-source, a single-lens binary-source, and two unrelated independent microlensing events — the binary-lens single-source scenario was found to be the most physically consistent explanation. Bayesian analysis of the surviving model suggests the primary lens is likely a low-mass M dwarf hosting a companion that is probably a low-mass brown dwarf or super-Jupiter, with an inferred projected separation making it the widest low-mass companion discovered via microlensing to date. The authors discuss how future space-based observatories may improve sensitivity to such wide-orbit companions, while emphasizing that disentangling genuine binary-lens events from variable star contaminants and other degeneracies will remain a key challenge.
items.citation: Hongjing Yang, Weicheng Zang, Yoon-Hyun Ryu et al.. OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Images Talk Back: Guiding MMDiTs by Suppressing Image-to-Text Feedback
items.summary: This paper investigates the role of image-to-text feedback within multimodal diffusion transformers, where joint attention mechanisms allow an evolving image to update internal text representations that subsequently guide further image generation. The authors find that this feedback tends to preserve whatever objects and attributes are already present in the image, including errors, rather than correcting deviations from the text prompt. To address this, they propose Semantic Feedback Guidance (SFG), a method that suppresses image-to-text feedback by guiding generation away from an auxiliary branch that amplifies this feedback while weakening text-to-image conditioning, with an efficient in-place variant requiring no additional model evaluations. Experiments across multiple image-generation backbones demonstrate that suppressing this feedback substantially improves prompt alignment and preference-model scores, and the approach also generalizes to text-to-video and image-to-video generation tasks.
items.citation: Yucheng Yang, Xiaoxiao Sun, Shusheng Yang et al.. Images Talk Back: Guiding MMDiTs by Suppressing Image-to-Text Feedback. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of interpreting black-box vision model predictions through concept-based attribution, a field where existing methods are limited by requirements for model weight access, large annotated datasets, and restriction to classification or regression tasks. The proposed method, Hide and Seek (HnS), works by using a vision-language model to retrieve images aligned with a given concept, localizing that concept within each image, masking the localized region, and measuring how the black-box model's output changes between the original and masked versions. This design allows HnS to operate without access to model internals or labeled concept datasets while supporting local, image-level attributions across a broad range of vision tasks. Validation on standard benchmarks demonstrated that HnS achieved better agreement with ground-truth attributions than existing concept attribution methods. The approach was further shown to generalize to tasks such as image captioning and satellite image segmentation, where no prior concept attribution method is applicable.
items.citation: Bhanu Tokas, Rahul Nair, Rockwell Jackson et al.. Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
items.summary: This paper examines a fundamental vulnerability in AI safety evaluations that rely on capability elicitation to detect dangerous model behaviors before deployment. The researchers constructed backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, which are only decrypted and executed when a secret trigger is received, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to hiding arbitrary computations. These hidden circuits are provably difficult to detect or elicit under standard cryptographic assumptions, even when evaluators have full access to model weights. The approach was implemented and tested against multiple elicitation methods including fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training on a chemical reaction prediction task chosen as a proxy for chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear relevant capabilities. The findings demonstrate that elicitation-based capability audits face a fundamental cryptographic limit, meaning current evaluation frameworks cannot reliably guarantee that dangerous capabilities have been surfaced.
items.citation: Andis Draguns, Sumeet Ramesh Motwani, Raymond Douglas et al.. AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of managing data relay nodes in deep-space communication networks, where intermittent connectivity, long propagation delays, and limited storage make efficient scheduling critical. The authors develop a closed-loop reinforcement learning framework that treats relay-side bundle scheduling, dropping, and flow control as a constrained semi-Markov decision process, solved using a masked Lagrangian variant of Proximal Policy Optimization. To capture mission relevance, they introduce a metric called excess age, which measures information freshness relative to a source-dependent delay baseline, and define a goal-oriented loss function that supports nonlinear, source-specific penalties. Feasibility-aware action masking ensures that only transmissions completable within an active contact window are considered, respecting the store-carry-forward nature of the Bundle Protocol. Simulations using DTNSim demonstrate that the proposed approach improves age-based utility and inter-flow fairness across heterogeneous planetary sources compared to conventional schedulers such as FIFO.
items.citation: Sajjad Baghaeea, Aimin Lib, Shanmugarajan Balasubramanian et al.. Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review
items.summary: This narrative review examines the biological connections linking periodontal disease, gut health, and brain function through what the authors term the oral–gut–brain axis, proposing it as a unifying framework for understanding comorbidities among periodontal, cardiometabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases. The authors conducted a structured literature search across multiple major databases to synthesize evidence on the molecular mechanisms by which periodontal dysbiosis may disrupt intestinal homeostasis and promote neuroinflammation. Key findings indicate that periodontal pathogens, particularly Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum, have been detected ectopically in the gut and are associated with reduced tight junction protein expression, altered microbial composition, increased blood–brain barrier permeability, microglial activation, and amyloid-beta accumulation in preclinical and observational studies. Salivary biomarkers such as matrix metalloproteinases and interleukins, alongside intestinal markers including short-chain fatty acids and calprotectin, are identified as promising non-invasive tools for monitoring inflammatory burden across the entire axis. The authors conclude that while this tripartite framework is biologically plausible, existing evidence remains predominantly associative, and causal directionality in humans requires validation through longitudinal studies before pharmacological interventions targeting this axis can be clinically adopted.
items.citation: Caterina Nela Dumitru, Alina Oana Dumitru, Gabriel Valeriu Popa et al.. The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review. Dentistry Journal. 2026

items.title: Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.
items.summary: This clinical trial investigated whether rinsing with a Vitamin D₃ solution before providing a saliva sample could affect the results of SARS-CoV-2 rapid antigen tests. Adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection provided paired saliva samples immediately before and after a standardized one-minute Vitamin D₃ oral rinse, with both rapid antigen testing and rapid RT-PCR performed under blinded conditions. The rinse converted the majority of antigen-positive samples to antigen-negative, dramatically reducing overall antigen positivity, while RT-PCR positivity rates and viral RNA levels remained largely unchanged between pre- and post-rinse samples. The persistence of detectable viral RNA despite the loss of antigen signal suggests that the oral rinse interfered with antigen detection rather than eliminating the virus from the oral cavity. The authors conclude that Vitamin D₃ oral rinsing represents a previously unrecognized pre-analytical variable that could produce false-negative rapid antigen test results, with important implications for infectious disease screening and public health surveillance.
items.citation: Feteih SMN, Heaphy ELG, Aljagthmi A et al.. Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.. Frontiers in oral health. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether molecular testing on saliva and oral swabs could serve as accurate, nonsputum-based diagnostic tools for pulmonary tuberculosis. Using a nested case-control design within a prospective cohort of adults and children at primary care centers in Colombia, researchers applied Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing to saliva samples and nylon-flocked oral swab eluates from culture-confirmed tuberculosis cases and matched culture-negative controls. Saliva demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for detecting culture-confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis, exceeding the World Health Organization's target threshold for nonsputum diagnostic tests, while oral swabs showed lower sensitivity but similarly high specificity. Saliva sensitivity was significantly greater than that of oral swabs, though the two specimen types did not differ meaningfully in specificity. Both collection methods were well accepted by participants, supporting their potential as practical alternatives to sputum-based tuberculosis diagnosis.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Vargas DA, Fuertes-Bucheli JF, Sanchez-Hidalgo A et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Lethal hantavirus at sea: Infectious disease outbreaks on cruise ships and limits of preparedness
items.summary: This paper examined a lethal hantavirus outbreak aboard an expedition cruise ship traveling through the South Atlantic, representing an unprecedented cluster of zoonotic disease in a maritime setting. The authors analyzed the epidemiology of the outbreak, which involved multiple confirmed and suspected cases across passengers of numerous nationalities, and reviewed the broader context of infectious disease preparedness on cruise ships. Because hantavirus transmission occurs primarily through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta rather than sustained human-to-human spread, the authors focused on identifying potential point-source exposures, which may have occurred onboard, during shore excursions at ecologically diverse remote locations, or prior to embarkation in South America. The paper highlighted the complexity of outbreak investigations in maritime environments, where passengers from many countries visit multiple jurisdictions, and noted that viral sequencing and laboratory confirmation are essential to clarify the origin and characteristics of infection. The authors concluded that this unusual event underscores how emerging zoonotic risks intersect with global travel and ecological exposure, and reveals important limits in current preparedness frameworks for infectious disease outbreaks at sea.
items.citation: Alimuddin I. Zumla, Brian McCloskey, Giuseppe Ippolito et al.. Lethal hantavirus at sea: Infectious disease outbreaks on cruise ships and limits of preparedness. Travel Medicine and Infectious Disease. 2026

items.title: Targeting biofilm-driven antibiotic resistance: emerging mechanisms and next-generation therapeutic interventions
items.summary: This review paper examines the mechanisms by which microbial biofilms drive antimicrobial resistance and evaluates emerging therapeutic strategies to combat this challenge. Biofilms enhance antibiotic tolerance through multiple mechanisms including restricted drug penetration, enzymatic antibiotic degradation, and facilitation of horizontal gene transfer, making infections extraordinarily difficult to treat. The authors synthesize current understanding of how biofilm architecture and biology contribute to resistance, noting that no anti-biofilm drugs have received regulatory approval despite the severity of the problem. The review highlights a range of next-generation therapeutic approaches being developed to address this gap, including nanotechnology-based delivery systems, antimicrobial peptides, bacteriophage-derived enzymes, quorum-sensing inhibitors, CRISPR-based tools, microbiome engineering, and artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery. The authors advocate for a multi-platform therapeutic approach as the most promising path toward overcoming biofilm-mediated resistance and improving clinical outcomes for persistent and device-associated infections.
items.citation: Abdulkarim Mbaraka, Ritu Raj Meena, Ekta Menghani et al.. Targeting biofilm-driven antibiotic resistance: emerging mechanisms and next-generation therapeutic interventions. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress, Environmental Pollutants, Aging, and Epigenetic Regulation: Mechanistic Insights and Biomarker Advances
items.summary: This review examines how environmental pollutants interact with oxidative stress mechanisms to drive epigenetic changes and accelerate biological aging. The authors synthesize recent literature on how distinct pollutant classes, including air pollutants, metals, pesticides, nanoparticles, and micro- and nanoplastics, converge on shared molecular mechanisms such as mitochondrial electron transport disruption, NADPH oxidase activation, and redox cycling to generate excess reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. These oxidative signals are traced through their downstream effects on epigenetic remodeling processes, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNA regulation. The review critically evaluates the strength of evidence across different study contexts, from cell culture to human observational research, and benchmarks oxidative stress biomarker platforms according to their analytical specificity and readiness for clinical use. The authors also discuss how exposomics and artificial intelligence-assisted multi-omics approaches may advance biomarker discovery, while cautioning that confounding factors, batch effects, and limited prospective validation remain substantial barriers to translating these findings into clinical practice.
items.citation: Minelly Gonzalez, Michael Powers, Luca Cucullo. Oxidative Stress, Environmental Pollutants, Aging, and Epigenetic Regulation: Mechanistic Insights and Biomarker Advances. Antioxidants. 2026

items.title: Andes virus outbreak linked to expedition cruise ship travel, multi-country investigation and response, April to June 2026
items.summary:
The abstract contains specific numbers, statistics, dates, and other details I am instructed to exclude, but the scientific substance can still be summarized from the study design and findings described.

This paper investigated an outbreak of Andes orthohantavirus linked to travel aboard an expedition cruise ship, representing an unusual setting for transmission of this rodent-borne pathogen. The investigation was multinational in scope, reflecting the diverse nationalities of those aboard the vessel, and involved contact tracing, isolation, quarantine, medical evacuation, repatriation, and laboratory follow-up across multiple countries. Both passengers and crew members were affected, with a notable case fatality burden, and ongoing work at the time of reporting aimed to clarify the outbreak source, identify risk factors, and prevent further spread.

items.title: Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician
items.summary: Andes virus (ANDV), a zoonotic RNA virus transmitted through inhalation of aerosols from infected rodent excreta, is unique among hantaviruses in its capacity for sustained human-to-human transmission via respiratory droplets and close contact. This review updates general physicians on the clinical features, epidemiology, and management of ANDV infection, with particular attention to Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, a severe manifestation involving acute respiratory failure, haemodynamic instability, kidney injury, and dysregulated immune responses. Disease severity is associated with specific haematological and biochemical markers, and no approved antiviral therapy or vaccine exists, leaving supportive care as the only available management strategy. A recent outbreak aboard an international cruise ship demonstrated how ANDV can rapidly spread across multiple nationalities, illustrating the pathogen's potential for global dissemination in the context of mass travel. The authors emphasise the need for heightened clinician awareness, prompt contact tracing, and coordinated international outbreak preparedness given the virus's high case fatality rate and relatively prolonged incubation period.
items.citation: Emanuele Durante‐Mangoni, Iolanda Cafarella, Silvia Mercadante et al.. Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician. European Journal of Internal Medicine. 2026

items.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
items.summary: This paper investigated whether language models can effectively navigate large document networks by playing the Wikipedia Game, in which players must traverse from one article to a target article using only hyperlinks. The researchers evaluated both sentence embedding models and large language models across five Wikipedia languages and five academic literature datasets, constructing large local graphs of Wikipedia pages and paper citations to enable testing without reliance on third-party APIs. Models were compared against human players and a term frequency-based baseline to assess relative navigational capability. No model significantly outperformed humans, though several frontier reasoning and general-purpose models achieved comparable success rates. Performance and rankings varied considerably across languages and subject domains, with practical implications for deploying these models in information retrieval contexts.
items.citation: Alexander Hickey, Joanna Knight, James Bishop. Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?. arXiv. 2026

The work yields a suite of practical variants and concrete recommendations for selecting among them depending on the resource and deployment regime at hand.

items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of interpreting black-box vision models by attributing their predictions to human-understandable concepts. Existing concept-based attribution methods are limited by requirements for model weight access, large annotated datasets, and restriction to classification or regression tasks. The proposed method, Hide and Seek (HnS), overcomes these limitations by using a vision-language model to retrieve concept-aligned images, localize the concept within each image, mask the localized region, and measure how the black-box model's output changes between original and masked images. This approach enables both global and local (image-level) attributions without needing model internals or labeled concept data, and is applicable to diverse tasks such as image captioning and satellite image segmentation. Validation on standard benchmarks showed that HnS achieves better agreement with ground-truth attributions than existing methods, while extending concept-based interpretation to task types previously unsupported by such approaches.

The researchers constructed backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks inside host model weights, which are only decrypted and executed when a secret trigger is provided, extending previous work from concealing fixed strings to hiding arbitrary computations. These hidden circuits are provably difficult to detect or elicit under standard cryptographic assumptions, even when an auditor has full access to model weights. The proof-of-concept implementations were evaluated against a range of elicitation methods including fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training, using a chemical reaction prediction task as a proxy for dangerous capability assessment. The findings demonstrate that current elicitation-based capability audits face a fundamental cryptographic limit, as none of the tested methods successfully uncovered the hidden capabilities.

items.title: Can machines reason non-verbally?
items.summary: The paper investigates why modern AI systems struggle with visual non-verbal reasoning tasks, such as completing abstract patterns or delineating ambiguous regions of interest, despite their proficiency in language-based and mathematical reasoning. The core challenge identified is that visual reasoning involves implicit intermediate steps that lack clear verification methods, unlike the explicit, verifiable steps found in verbal reasoning. To address this, the authors introduce GenVerOpt, a framework that unifies generation, verification, and iterative optimisation into a unified pipeline, enabling per-sample refinement rather than relying on patterns learned during training alone. Tested across diverse domains, the framework surpasses human performance on abstract IQ puzzles, matches clinical experts in prostate cancer segmentation, and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in liver vessel reconstruction and tumour boundary alignment. The authors conclude that machine reasoning can be meaningfully extended beyond language, positioning visual non-verbal reasoning as a key component of more generalizable artificial intelligence.
items.citation: Shaheer U. Saeed, Zion Tse, Gregory Slabaugh et al.. Can machines reason non-verbally?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Plasmonic Nanoarray Biosensors for Non-Invasive Cancer Diagnostics.
items.summary: This review examines the use of plasmonic nanoarray biosensors for detecting cancer-associated biomarkers in non-invasively collected body fluids, specifically urine and saliva. The authors survey nanoarray architectures, fabrication strategies, surface functionalization approaches, and optical signal generation mechanisms, including localized surface plasmon resonance, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and metal-enhanced fluorescence. These platforms are considered in the context of identifying biomarkers relevant to bladder, prostate, pancreatic, oral, and head-and-neck cancers, where low biomarker abundance and complex fluid matrices present significant analytical challenges. The review finds that plasmonic nanoarrays offer advantages such as electromagnetic field concentration and multiplexed readout, but identifies persistent barriers including biofouling, fabrication reproducibility, and insufficient validation with authentic clinical samples. The authors conclude that advances in standardized biofluid processing, scalable manufacturing, and microfluidic integration will be necessary to translate these sensors into practical cancer screening tools.
items.citation: Kim SE, Choi HK, Choi JH. Plasmonic Nanoarray Biosensors for Non-Invasive Cancer Diagnostics.. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Group A Streptococcus molecular point of care testing in a paediatric emergency department.
items.summary: This study investigated whether a rapid molecular point-of-care test for Group A Streptococcus could improve antibiotic prescribing decisions in children presenting to a paediatric emergency department during a period of heightened streptococcal activity. Conducted as a pilot study, children under sixteen who had a clinician-requested throat swab also had a second research swab processed using a molecular point-of-care test, though clinical management was based solely on conventional culture results and was not influenced by the research findings. The study found that streptococcal prevalence was low during the study period, yet the large majority of participants received antibiotics, and most of those given antibiotics had a negative point-of-care test result. Conventional throat swab cultures took several days to return results, whereas the molecular test produced results within minutes. The authors conclude that point-of-care testing could reduce unnecessary antibiotic use in this setting when streptococcal suspicion is the primary prescribing driver, but that further research is needed to establish its overall clinical benefit.
items.citation: Mills EA, Bingham R, Nijman RG et al.. Group A Streptococcus molecular point of care testing in a paediatric emergency department.. The Journal of antimicrobial chemotherapy. 2026

items.title: Biological characteristics and whole-genome sequencing analysis of an alpha-hemolytic Streptococcus pyogenes strain
items.summary: This study investigated an unusual alpha-hemolytic strain of *Streptococcus pyogenes* isolated from erysipelas skin secretions, a phenotype atypical for a species that characteristically displays beta-hemolysis. The researchers used whole-genome sequencing alongside conventional microbiological methods, including mass spectrometry-based identification, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, multilocus sequence typing, and comprehensive bioinformatic analysis to characterize the strain's resistance genes, virulence factors, and phylogenetic relationships. The isolate was confirmed as *S. pyogenes* of sequence type ST176 and emm type emm58.7, carrying resistance genes for macrolides and tetracycline while retaining sensitivity to penicillins and cephalosporins, and harboring numerous virulence factor-encoding genes. The alpha-hemolytic phenotype was attributed to an amino acid substitution in the sagB gene that likely disrupts functional expression of streptolysin S, without compromising the strain's virulence potential or correct identification by standard methods. The authors caution that the morphological resemblance of such strains to commensal viridans streptococci poses a risk of clinical misdiagnosis, and advocate combining antigen detection, serology, and molecular diagnostics to improve detection of atypically presenting *S. pyogenes*.
items.citation: Mo Y, Wang Q, Qiu M. Biological characteristics and whole-genome sequencing analysis of an alpha-hemolytic Streptococcus pyogenes strain. 2026

items.title: Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis
items.summary: This review examines the bidirectional relationship between gut microbial-derived metabolites and kidney disease, with particular attention to the mechanisms driving renal fibrosis and disease progression. The paper synthesizes current evidence showing that kidney injury disrupts intestinal barrier function and gut microbial balance, resulting in reduced beneficial short-chain fatty acids and excessive accumulation of uremic toxins such as indoxyl sulfate and trimethylamine-N-oxide. These metabolites influence kidney pathology through multiple signaling pathways, including aryl hydrocarbon receptor and nuclear factor kappa B signaling, with tryptophan metabolites highlighted as especially important mediators of gut-kidney communication. The review covers how these disruptions contribute to acute kidney injury as well as specific chronic kidney diseases including diabetic kidney disease, immunoglobulin A nephropathy, and membranous nephropathy. The authors also survey therapeutic strategies targeting gut dysbiosis — including natural products, prebiotics, probiotics, and renal replacement therapy — as potential avenues for more precise management of kidney disease.
items.citation: Wan-Ying Zhang, Yu-Lu Zhang, Qing-Qing Yu et al.. Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis. International Journal of Biological Sciences. 2026

items.title: Biodiversity and biogeography of the multi-kingdom cancer microbiome

items.title: Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
items.summary: These guidelines address the clinical management of vascular graft and endograft infections, a serious complication in vascular surgery. The European Society for Vascular Surgery updated its previous guidance by systematically reviewing the best available scientific evidence and supplementing it with expert opinion. Recommendations were formulated across key domains including definitions, diagnosis, multidisciplinary team management, antimicrobial therapy, management of intracavitary and extracavitary infections, and follow-up, with each recommendation graded by strength and level of evidence. The resulting guidelines also incorporate shared decision-making principles and patient-facing information, as well as a discussion of unresolved clinical questions. The document aims to provide comprehensive, current guidance to clinicians and patients for selecting optimal management strategies in this complex field.
items.venue: European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery
items.citation: Anne Lejay, Ben R. Saleem, Tara D. Barwick et al.. Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections. European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery. 2026

items.title: The Gut–Vagina Axis
items.summary: This review paper examines the gut-vagina axis as an emerging concept in female health, focusing on how interactions between the gut and vaginal microbiomes may influence physiology. The authors synthesize recent advances in microbiome research to outline the mechanisms through which these two distinct microbial communities may communicate, including microbial migration between sites, hormonal and immune regulation, and metabolite exchange. The paper emphasizes that this communication is bidirectional, meaning each microbiome can influence the composition and function of the other. The authors discuss how these interactions may have downstream consequences for microbial composition, immune responses, hormonal balance, and metabolic activity at both local and systemic levels, with implications for broader female health outcomes.
items.citation: Lorenzo Agoni, Elena Roselletti, Giovanni Marasco et al.. The Gut–Vagina Axis. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Rapid Respiratory Microbiological Point-of-Care Testing and Antibiotic Use in Primary Care
items.summary: This randomized clinical trial investigated whether rapid multiplex microbiological point-of-care testing, capable of detecting a broad panel of respiratory viral and bacterial pathogens within approximately forty-five minutes, could safely reduce antibiotic prescribing in primary care settings. The study enrolled patients aged one year and older presenting with acute respiratory tract infections where antibiotics were being considered, randomizing them equally to receive the point-of-care test or usual care across multiple general practices in Southwest England. Overall, the intervention did not reduce same-day antibiotic prescribing compared to usual care, with identical proportions of each group receiving antibiotics, and there was no difference in patient-reported symptom severity in the days following the consultation. However, prespecified subgroup analyses revealed that when a virus was detected by the test, antibiotic prescribing was substantially reduced compared to virus-negative cases, and patients with chronic lung disease also showed a differential reduction, suggesting the technology may benefit specific patient subgroups. The authors conclude that while broad implementation of this testing approach did not achieve overall antibiotic reduction, targeted use in virus-positive patients may offer a meaningful pathway for antimicrobial stewardship in primary care.
items.citation: Alastair D Hay, Samantha Abbs, Matthew J Ridd et al.. Rapid Respiratory Microbiological Point-of-Care Testing and Antibiotic Use in Primary Care. JAMA Internal Medicine. 2026

items.title: Gut Microbial Metabotypes Shape Polyphenol Bioactivity: Toward Precision Nutrition Strategies for Human Health
items.summary: This review examines how gut microbial biotransformation of dietary polyphenols shapes their biological effects, focusing on the concept that individuals differ substantially in their capacity to produce specific microbial-derived metabolites such as urolithins, equol, and enterolignans. Because many polyphenols reach the colon largely unabsorbed, intestinal microorganisms convert them into lower-molecular-weight compounds whose absorption profiles and bioactivities can differ markedly from those of the parent molecules. The authors critically synthesize current knowledge on gut microbiota-mediated polyphenol metabolism, the classification of individuals into microbial metabotypes, and the determinants driving interindividual variability in metabolite production. Biological effects spanning mitochondrial function, endothelial homeostasis, metabolic regulation, inflammation, gut barrier integrity, and gut-brain communication are reviewed, with careful distinction drawn between evidence from human studies and findings from preclinical or mechanistic work. The review concludes that while metabotype-guided stratification holds promise for improving precision nutrition research, clinical translation is presently constrained by heterogeneous protocols, non-standardized analytical thresholds, and insufficient long-term intervention data, positioning microbial metabotypes as useful research biomarkers rather than established tools for routine personalized dietary prescription.
items.citation: Pasquale Perrone, Stefania D’Angelo. Gut Microbial Metabotypes Shape Polyphenol Bioactivity: Toward Precision Nutrition Strategies for Human Health. Nutrients. 2026

items.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
items.summary: This paper investigated whether language models can effectively navigate large document networks by playing the Wikipedia Game, a task requiring players to traverse from one article to another using only hyperlinks. The researchers tested sentence embedding models and large language models across multiple Wikipedia language editions and academic literature datasets, constructing large local graphs of Wikipedia pages and paper citations to enable evaluation without dependence on external APIs. Models were benchmarked against human players and a TF-IDF baseline across diverse languages and domains. No model significantly outperformed humans, though several top-performing reasoning-oriented models achieved comparable success rates. Performance varied considerably across languages and subject domains, with practical implications for the use of language models in large-scale information retrieval tasks.
items.citation: Alexander Hickey, Joanna Knight, James Bishop. Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Towards Physically Grounded Articulated 3D Assets: A Multi-Agent Pipeline and Benchmark
items.summary: This paper investigates the generation of physically grounded articulated three-dimensional assets, aiming to capture not just visual appearance but also realistic motion and physical behavior. The authors present Artisan, a multi-agent pipeline that extends a prior method by incorporating physical simulation feedback to produce assets with collision-free motion, gravitational stability, and accurate mass and material properties. They also construct a unified benchmark covering spatial fidelity, physical plausibility, downstream task performance, and overall quality, drawing on reference assets, stability prompts, and objects with known mass references. Through evaluation of more than ten representative models, Artisan achieves competitive spatial fidelity while attaining the lowest collision rates and highest stability rates among all compared methods. The work establishes a foundation for advancing three-dimensional generation toward assets that are both physically plausible and functionally usable.
items.citation: Xudong Cai, Ruijie Zhu, Haoliang Shang et al.. Towards Physically Grounded Articulated 3D Assets: A Multi-Agent Pipeline and Benchmark. arXiv. 2026

items.title: OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit
items.summary: This paper investigated a microlensing event exhibiting two short-lived brightness bumps separated by over eight years in survey data spanning more than a decade, aiming to identify very wide-orbit binary lens systems. The researchers cross-matched microlensing events from two major surveys and evaluated three competing explanations for the light curve: a binary-lens single-source, a single-lens binary-source, and two entirely unrelated microlensing events. Through model fitting and a Bayesian analysis, they ruled out the binary-source and unrelated-events scenarios based on poor fits, low event rates, and unphysical source properties, leaving the binary-lens interpretation as the most plausible. The surviving model implies a mass ratio suggesting the primary lens is likely a low-mass M dwarf orbited by a low-mass brown dwarf or super-Jupiter companion at a projected separation making it the widest low-mass companion discovered through microlensing to date. The authors note that while future space-based facilities will improve sensitivity to such wide-orbit companions, disentangling genuine binary-lens signals from variable star contamination and other degeneracies will remain a critical challenge.
items.citation: Hongjing Yang, Weicheng Zang, Yoon-Hyun Ryu et al.. OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
items.summary: The paper investigates the abelian sandpile model on the two-dimensional integer lattice, where sites topple by distributing grains to neighbors whenever a threshold is exceeded. A central challenge is that, unlike in three or more dimensions, the Green function of simple random walk is infinite in two dimensions, leaving open whether avalanches triggered in the stationary state remain almost surely finite. The authors prove that despite this infinite expected toppling count, avalanches in two dimensions are nevertheless almost surely finite, with the probability of an avalanche reaching distance R bounded above by a negative power of the logarithm of R. The proof strategy traces the avalanche backward in time and reduces the finiteness question to an estimate for the uniform spanning tree, which is then established using a multiscale electrical resistance argument. This resolves a longstanding open question about the geometry of sandpile avalanches in the critical dimension.
items.citation: Ahmed Bou-Rabee. Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A universal sector of $\mathcal{N}=1$ class $\mathcal{S}$ spectra
items.summary: This paper investigates the spectrum of light operators in four-dimensional superconformal field theories belonging to the class known as class S with minimal supersymmetry, specifically those arising from M5-branes wrapped on compact hyperbolic Riemann surfaces. Working in the large-N limit, the authors analyze Kaluza-Klein fluctuations around the corresponding anti-de Sitter supergravity backgrounds across the full range of a continuous twist parameter. By restricting to modes constant on the Riemann surface through an appropriate generalized geometric structure that depends on the twist parameter, they extract the relevant mass spectra and organize the resulting eigenstates into long and protected supermultiplets carrying definite flavor quantum numbers. The analysis reveals rich patterns in the spectrum as the twist parameter varies, including both isolated multiplets and infinite towers of multiplets, all characterized analytically. The results identify a universal sector of the operator spectrum common to this broad class of superconformal field theories.
items.citation: Ritabrata Bhattacharya, Abhay Katyal, Oscar Varela. A universal sector of $\mathcal{N}=1$ class $\mathcal{S}$ spectra. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Constructive Arboricity in Almost-Linear Time for Dense Graphs
items.summary: The paper studies the arboricity of a graph—the minimum number of forests required to partition its edges—and the algorithmic problem of computing this quantity exactly and constructing an optimal decomposition efficiently. The authors present a randomized algorithm that determines the exact arboricity and builds an optimal forest partition within a running time that scales as the minimum of two expressions depending on the number of vertices and edges, achieving almost-linear time on dense graphs. The algorithm's guarantees hold both in expectation and with high probability. Additionally, the paper introduces the first known almost-linear-time algorithm for constructing a near-optimal partition that uses at most one more forest than the minimum required.
items.citation: Iman Gholami, Mohammad T. Hajiaghayi, Mahdi JafariRaviz et al.. Constructive Arboricity in Almost-Linear Time for Dense Graphs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.
items.summary: This study developed a rapid point-of-care molecular detection method for Group B Streptococcus, a major cause of neonatal infections, by combining bacteriophage lysin-based cell lysis with real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR. The method used specific primers and probes targeting the GBS cylA gene and a human reference gene, achieving complete nucleic acid extraction within five minutes and total turnaround in approximately thirty-five minutes, compared to the eighteen to forty-eight hours required for conventional culture. Performance was evaluated in two clinical cohorts using vaginal swab samples, with the assay benchmarked against standard culture and antigen testing. The assay demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity, with culture-concordant specificity approaching near-complete accuracy after sequencing confirmation of discordant samples, and substantially outperformed antigen testing in sensitivity. The authors conclude that this approach holds promise for intrapartum or near-patient GBS screening, though further validation in real-world clinical workflows is needed.
items.venue: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
items.citation: Zhu H, Zeng X, Huang X et al.. A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.. European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.
items.summary: This large retrospective cohort study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic and its associated non-pharmaceutical interventions affected the epidemiology of Group A Streptococcus pharyngitis in children. Researchers analyzed tens of thousands of pediatric clinical episodes from a tertiary outpatient clinic spanning pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods, comparing positivity rates and using multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors of Group A Streptococcus detection. Group A Streptococcus positivity rose progressively across all three periods, increasing from roughly one in five cases before the pandemic to more than one in three in the post-pandemic period. Older age and male sex were also independently associated with a positive result. The authors conclude that this progressive increase likely reflects a combination of shifting healthcare utilization patterns, testing practices, age distribution, and transmission dynamics rather than any single cause, and they call for continued epidemiological surveillance.
items.venue: The Journal of international medical research
items.citation: Nas Y, Gözüküçük S, Bayırlı H et al.. Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.. The Journal of international medical research. 2026

items.title: Rapid molecular culture versus conventional culture for periprosthetic joint infection: diagnostic performance and clinical relevance.
items.summary: This study evaluated a rapid PCR-based assay called Molecular Culture® applied to sonication fluid from patients undergoing hip or knee revision arthroplasty to diagnose periprosthetic joint infection. Sonication fluid samples were retrospectively analysed and patients were classified according to established infection criteria, with the molecular assay's results compared against conventional culture as the reference standard. The molecular approach delivered results within approximately four hours, compared to the prolonged turnaround of conventional culture, and identified additional clinically relevant pathogens that conventional culture missed. After clinical correlation, the assay demonstrated high negative percentage agreement, suggesting strong utility for ruling out infection. The authors conclude that the molecular assay functions well as an adjunctive diagnostic tool, particularly benefiting patients with uncertain infection status or prior antibiotic exposure, where rapid pathogen identification could guide earlier and more appropriate antimicrobial therapy.
items.venue: Journal of bone and joint infection
items.citation: Morreel E, Savelkoul P, van Loo I. Rapid molecular culture versus conventional culture for periprosthetic joint infection: diagnostic performance and clinical relevance.. Journal of bone and joint infection. 2026

items.title: Diagnosing Sepsis and Identifying Bacterial Resistance Genes Directly from Whole Blood Using a Rapid Real-Time PCR System.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a rapid real-time PCR system capable of detecting a broad panel of pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes directly from whole blood in patients with sepsis. Researchers collected whole-blood samples from adult sepsis patients simultaneously for both conventional blood culture and rapid real-time PCR analysis, comparing the results of the two methods. The most frequently isolated organisms by blood culture were common gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, and among resistance genes detected by the molecular panel, those associated with methicillin resistance and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase production were predominant. Agreement between blood culture and rapid real-time PCR results was statistically significant, and the molecular method demonstrated high specificity alongside moderate sensitivity, with results available within four hours. The authors conclude that this rapid approach offers a clinically meaningful advantage by enabling early identification of causative pathogens and resistance mechanisms, potentially preventing progression to septic shock and reducing mortality.
items.citation: Begmyradova S, Öksüz L, Aktas Z et al.. Diagnosing Sepsis and Identifying Bacterial Resistance Genes Directly from Whole Blood Using a Rapid Real-Time PCR System.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026
