items.title: The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods
items.summary: This study examined the use of Raman spectroscopy to distinguish natural gemstones from their laboratory-grown synthetic counterparts, focusing on ruby, sapphire, emerald, and spinel, which are among the most commercially significant gems. The researchers evaluated both a laboratory-grade Raman spectrometer equipped with two different laser wavelengths and a portable Raman system, applying them to identify gems produced by various manufacturing methods and to determine geographic origin. The laboratory instrument proved capable of differentiating natural from synthetic gemstones and determining the origin of same-coloured stones, with the dual-laser capability being essential since emerald analysis required a specific laser wavelength. The portable system could distinguish between different stone types but lacked the sensitivity needed to discriminate between natural and synthetic specimens. Repeated measurements confirmed the reliability of Raman spectroscopy as a non-destructive, preparation-free analytical tool for gemological identification, with measured spectral bands consistently falling within accepted tolerances of reference values.
items.citation: Raabell Shah. The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods. Research Output (Edinburgh Napier University). 2026

items.title: Porous material engineering through synthesis for smart sensor systems
items.summary: This review examines porous materials as a platform for next-generation sensor systems, focusing on how their high surface areas, tunable pore structures, and chemical functionalization enable improved analyte detection. The authors systematically survey representative categories of porous materials—including metal oxides, polymers, and carbon-based systems—alongside their synthesis routes, which encompass sol-gel processes, template-assisted methods, three-dimensional printing, and light-material interactions. Fundamental sensing mechanisms are analyzed across electrical, electrochemical, and optical transduction pathways that porous architectures make possible. The review covers applications spanning environmental monitoring, biomedical diagnostics, and smart packaging, where porous material-based sensors are reported to show faster response times, better analyte discrimination, and greater operational stability. The authors draw together design principles and fabrication strategies intended to guide future development and practical deployment of advanced sensing technologies.
items.citation: Se Jin Choi, Sang Yoon Park, Kang Hyeon Kim et al.. Porous material engineering through synthesis for smart sensor systems. Microsystems & Nanoengineering. 2026

items.title: Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses
items.summary: This study developed a viral surveillance framework using Brazil's existing rabies passive surveillance program to detect bat-borne viruses with zoonotic potential. Researchers applied a selection algorithm to choose representative specimens from thousands of collected bats across São Paulo state, then subjected paired lung and intestine samples to nanopore metagenomic sequencing. The analysis revealed viral genetic sequences spanning multiple virus families of public health concern, including coronaviruses, arenaviruses, and paramyxoviruses, demonstrating substantial previously undetected viral diversity in urban synanthropic bats. Notably, the approach uncovered a previously unknown filovirus in bats from the Americas, highlighting the framework's capacity for identifying novel potential pathogens. The framework was validated by multisectoral One Health experts as a scalable and cost-effective model suitable for national expansion and adaptable to low- and middle-income country settings.
items.citation: Juliana Amorim Conselheiro, Filipe Romero Rebello Moreira, Gisely Toledo Barone et al.. Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses. One Health. 2026

items.title: Advances in low-cost electrochemical sensors for healthcare monitoring and diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines recent progress in the development of low-cost electrochemical sensors designed for healthcare diagnostics and point-of-care testing, particularly in resource-limited settings. The authors survey innovations in materials, design, and fabrication approaches, with emphasis on cost-reduction strategies such as the use of carbon-based compounds, conductive polymers, and plant-derived bioactive molecules, as well as scalable manufacturing techniques like screen printing and three-dimensional printing. The review covers applications of these sensors in monitoring and diagnosing chronic and infectious conditions including diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and infectious diseases, as well as their integration with digital platforms for real-time data collection. The authors also address outstanding challenges including sensor stability, specificity, and barriers to large-scale commercialization, alongside proposed solutions and future research directions. Overall, the review argues that affordable electrochemical sensors hold considerable potential to broaden access to diagnostics, lower healthcare costs, and improve patient outcomes.
items.venue: Advances in Industrial and Engineering Chemistry
items.citation: B. Anuthra, Jasmine Ratan, Priyanka Gupta et al.. Advances in low-cost electrochemical sensors for healthcare monitoring and diagnostics. Advances in Industrial and Engineering Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Tracing the Cosmic Origins: Machine Learning Reconstruction of the Primordial Density Field from EoR Observations
items.summary: This paper investigates whether the primordial density field of the Universe can be reconstructed from observations of large-scale structure during the Epoch of Reionization, aiming to recover cosmological information lost to non-linear gravitational evolution and astrophysical processes. The researchers used simulated 21-cm and CO line-intensity maps generated with a dedicated simulation framework, feeding these into a three-dimensional U-Net neural network trained to reconstruct the initial density field at very high redshift. The two emission lines were chosen because they trace complementary environments — 21-cm probing diffuse neutral gas and CO probing dense star-forming regions — and realistic instrumental effects mimicking next-generation survey telescopes were incorporated. In the idealized case, combining both tracers yielded high cross-correlation with the true initial conditions across a broad range of scales, and even under realistic observational noise the joint reconstruction maintained meaningful fidelity at large scales. Crucially, performing simulation-based inference on power-spectrum summaries derived from the reconstructed fields demonstrated that this approach roughly doubles the precision on key cosmological parameters such as the amplitude of matter fluctuations and the spectral index, confirming that joint multi-tracer reconstruction can recover otherwise inaccessible primordial information from future surveys.
items.citation: Anchal Saxena, P. Daniel Meerburg, Guochao Sun et al.. Tracing the Cosmic Origins: Machine Learning Reconstruction of the Primordial Density Field from EoR Observations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data
items.summary: This paper introduces WearableQA, a benchmark designed to evaluate whether AI systems can reason over longitudinal wearable health data from real users. The benchmark consists of thousands of multiple-choice questions derived from wearable time series, blood biomarkers, and demographic information spanning hundreds of days per user, preserving authentic signal characteristics such as device noise and inter-individual variability. Questions are organized across two reasoning axes—data versus health reasoning, and single- versus cross-signal reasoning—and are constructed using a dual-grounding framework that anchors questions in both published physiological literature and statistically validated population-level patterns. Evaluation of a diverse set of proprietary and open-source large language models reveals substantial performance variation, with most models falling well below ceiling performance, indicating that the benchmark effectively differentiates model capabilities. The authors conclude that WearableQA represents a realistic and diagnostically useful benchmark for assessing LLM reasoning over real-world wearable health data, with considerable room remaining for improvement.
items.citation: Ji Soo Lee, Xilun Chen, Pierce Chuang et al.. WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Parametric and feedback-controlled multiparameter quantum estimation in a double cavity optomechanics: steady and dynamical state
items.summary: This paper investigates the fundamental limits of simultaneously estimating multiple parameters in an open optomechanical system, where dissipation, thermal noise, and measurement incompatibility pose key challenges. The authors study a coupled-cavity platform featuring two mechanical modes interacting with driven optical cavities, two-mode squeezed vacuum, intracavity degenerate parametric amplification, and coherent optical feedback, using the continuous-variable Gaussian-state formalism to derive the linearized quantum Langevin dynamics and steady-state covariance matrix. Quantum Fisher information matrices for simultaneous estimation of the optomechanical coupling strength and cavity dissipation rate are evaluated using both symmetric and right logarithmic derivative frameworks. They find that intracavity parametric amplification substantially improves multiparameter estimation precision across a broad range of operating conditions, while coherent feedback produces a nonmonotonic effect on estimation precision that depends sensitively on feedback reflectivity, phase, squeezing strength, and thermal occupation. This nonmonotonic behavior reframes coherent feedback not as a simple enhancing or degrading tool but as a tunable resource for engineering quantum fluctuations and parameter-dependent correlations, with squeezing and parametric amplification together providing the greatest metrological gains in identifiable parameter regimes.
items.citation: Hamza Harraf, Mohamed Amazioug, Amjad Sohail et al.. Parametric and feedback-controlled multiparameter quantum estimation in a double cavity optomechanics: steady and dynamical state. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MEOX: Compact Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts for Earth Observation
items.summary: This paper introduces MEOX, a compact multimodal masked autoencoder designed for Earth observation that can handle heterogeneous remote sensing sensors and missing data without requiring a large architecture. The model uses sensor-specific adapters, sparse mixture-of-experts blocks with shared and private low-rank components, and metadata tokens to achieve flexible multimodal fusion while constraining parameter growth. It was pretrained on a large collection of multimodal Earth observation samples using modality-balanced masked reconstruction and structured sensor dropout, then evaluated through frozen and fine-tuned transfer on multiple benchmark tasks including land cover segmentation and scene classification. MEOX achieves competitive or superior performance compared to larger existing models on several benchmarks, including outperforming a previously reported mixture-of-experts baseline on cashew segmentation and EuroSAT classification tasks. Diagnostic analyses further characterize how experts specialize by modality, spatial region, and function, while probing experiments quantify the contribution of geographic metadata to representation quality.
items.citation: Mohanad Albughdadi. MEOX: Compact Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts for Earth Observation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Does Your Agent's Memory Survive a Model Upgrade? A Controlled Study of Memory Portability
items.summary: This paper investigates whether AI agent memory systems remain functional and accurate after a model upgrade, a scenario that is common in practice but rarely studied systematically. The researchers compared four memory storage strategies—verbatim long-context history, retrieval-augmented generation with chunked text, model-compressed natural-language notes, and a fixed-schema knowledge graph—by testing how well each format transfers when the underlying language model is swapped. Using synthetic agent histories with randomized answer codes and two open-weight small language models, they evaluated retrieval accuracy before and after model migration under controlled conditions. They found that fixed-schema knowledge graphs transfer with negligible accuracy loss, whereas compressed notes are highly coupled to the model that wrote them, showing asymmetric accuracy shifts depending on migration direction, and that partial embedding index migrations recover only a fraction of the performance gains achievable through full re-embedding. The study concludes that retaining original source histories is critical for memory repair after upgrades, and that migration testing must account for directionality, embedding space isolation, and the distinct failure modes of each memory format.
items.citation: Ankit Goyal, Jaideep Ray. Does Your Agent's Memory Survive a Model Upgrade? A Controlled Study of Memory Portability. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Log-Free $n^{1/5}$ Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
items.summary: The paper addresses Chowla's cosine problem, which asks how large the minimum negative value of a trigonometric sum over a finite set of positive integers must be. A recent result had established a lower bound of the form the set size to the power of one-fifth, but with a subpolynomial loss in the exponent. This work eliminates that loss entirely, proving a clean lower bound with an absolute positive constant and no logarithmic penalty. The key technical innovation is an exact averaging identity for the asymmetric boundaries of additive intersections, which replaces a multiplicative-amplification step in the prior argument that was responsible for the logarithmic degradation. The result thus achieves a log-free version of the bound while otherwise building on the structure of the earlier proof.
items.citation: Abhishek Shankar. A Log-Free $n^{1/5}$ Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Bedside identification of subphenotypes in acute respiratory failure (PHIND): a multicentre, observational cohort study
items.summary: This prospective multicentre observational study investigated whether inflammatory subphenotypes of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) could be identified rapidly at the bedside and whether they were associated with differing clinical outcomes. Using a near-patient immunoanalyser measuring plasma interleukin-6 and soluble TNF receptor-1, combined with plasma bicarbonate and a validated logistic regression model, patients with ARDS or acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure were classified within approximately one hour of sample collection as either hyperinflammatory or hypoinflammatory. The study enrolled several hundred patients across intensive care units in the UK and Ireland, finding that a minority were classified as hyperinflammatory while the majority were hypoinflammatory. Sixty-day mortality was substantially higher in the hyperinflammatory subphenotype, with adjusted analyses confirming significantly increased odds of death independent of other factors. The authors conclude that bedside subphenotyping of ARDS is feasible within a clinically actionable timeframe and that the findings support precision medicine approaches and the need for prospective, subphenotype-stratified interventional trials.
items.citation: Kiran Reddy, Pratik Sinha, David Antcliffe et al.. Bedside identification of subphenotypes in acute respiratory failure (PHIND): a multicentre, observational cohort study. The Lancet Respiratory Medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Immature Granulocyte Count for Early Sepsis Detection: A Comparative Evaluation With C-Reactive Protein and Procalcitonin.
items.summary: This study investigated whether immature granulocyte parameters, specifically immature granulocyte count and percentage derived from routine complete blood counts, could serve as early diagnostic biomarkers for sepsis in critically ill patients, comparing their accuracy against the established markers C-reactive protein and procalcitonin. In a retrospective observational design, critically ill intensive care unit patients were categorized into sepsis and non-sepsis groups based on clinical monitoring within the first day of admission, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Patients who developed sepsis showed significantly elevated immature granulocyte parameters alongside other inflammatory and organ dysfunction markers compared to those who did not. Immature granulocyte percentage demonstrated good diagnostic accuracy, outperforming C-reactive protein and performing comparably to procalcitonin, while the combination of immature granulocyte percentage with procalcitonin achieved the strongest overall discriminatory performance. The authors conclude that immature granulocyte parameters, being readily obtainable from standard hematological analyses, represent reliable early indicators of sepsis and could support timely clinical decision-making when incorporated into routine assessment.
items.citation: Taver R, Gupta V, Saxena P et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of Immature Granulocyte Count for Early Sepsis Detection: A Comparative Evaluation With C-Reactive Protein and Procalcitonin.. Cureus. 2026

items.title: Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review investigated the diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy, a serious form of acute brain dysfunction occurring in sepsis patients, by examining candidates spanning innate immune activation, blood-brain barrier disruption, glial response, and neuronal injury. The researchers conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis across multiple databases, pooling studies with extractable diagnostic data and characterizing heterogeneity according to how SAE was defined and when biomarkers were sampled relative to a clinical anchor event. Blood-brain barrier and glial markers such as GFAP and S100β generally demonstrated more balanced diagnostic discrimination than classic neuronal injury markers, while upstream immune and alarmin candidates ranked highly in Bayesian comparative analyses, though several top-ranked biomarkers were supported by only single studies. A key limitation identified was that few studies assessed whether biomarkers provide diagnostic information beyond established clinical predictors such as illness severity scores or sedation-related confounders, restricting immediate clinical applicability. The authors conclude that blood biomarkers for this condition reflect a biologically coherent immune-to-neuronal cascade but that prospective head-to-head validation under standardized phenotyping and sampling protocols is needed to establish their incremental diagnostic value.
items.citation: Zhang Q, Zhu R, Li Y et al.. Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.. Frontiers in molecular neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Plasma and urinary sTREM-1 as biomarkers of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in critically Ill children.
items.summary: This prospective observational cohort study investigated whether plasma and urinary levels of soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1 (sTREM-1) could serve as early biomarkers for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in critically ill children admitted to a pediatric intensive care unit. Researchers measured sTREM-1 levels at the time of sepsis diagnosis and again at the point of acute kidney injury diagnosis in those who developed the complication, using established pediatric scoring criteria to define both sepsis and kidney injury. Both plasma and urinary sTREM-1 concentrations were significantly elevated in children who subsequently developed sepsis-associated acute kidney injury compared to those who did not, and both biomarkers rose further following acute kidney injury onset. Receiver operating characteristic analyses demonstrated moderate discriminative ability for both plasma and urinary sTREM-1, with plasma levels showing somewhat better diagnostic performance. The authors conclude that sTREM-1 measured at sepsis diagnosis may support early risk stratification, and that urinary sTREM-1 additionally showed prognostic value for mortality in affected children.
items.citation: Magdy SM, El-Gawaad TA, Hussein FA et al.. Plasma and urinary sTREM-1 as biomarkers of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in critically Ill children.. European journal of pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic utility of cystatin C for early detection of acute kidney injury in patients with sepsis. Researchers systematically searched electronic databases for relevant studies, assessed their quality using the QUADAS-2 tool, and applied a random-effects meta-analysis alongside summary receiver operating characteristic curve analysis to pool diagnostic accuracy estimates. Across the included studies, cystatin C demonstrated good overall diagnostic performance for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, with subgroup analyses showing that studies applying Sepsis 3.0 diagnostic criteria yielded higher specificity and reduced heterogeneity. Combining cystatin C with other biomarkers further improved diagnostic accuracy. The authors conclude that cystatin C is a promising biomarker for early clinical identification of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, though heterogeneity among included studies warrants cautious interpretation.
items.citation: Cheng L, Zhang B, Hu X et al.. Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: This paper presents the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign international guidelines for the management of sepsis and septic shock in adults. The guidelines were developed by a large, geographically diverse, multidisciplinary committee using the GRADE methodology, incorporating evidence synthesis, patient and family input, and an Evidence to Decision framework to formulate recommendations across domains including screening, infection management, hemodynamics, respiratory support, adjunctive therapies, and goals of care. The guidelines address management across hospital, prehospital, and immediate post-hospital settings, with an emphasis on antimicrobial stewardship, early identification, and timely treatment. Recommendations range from strong to conditional depending on the certainty of evidence and balance of desirable versus undesirable effects, with particular attention to applicability in low- and middle-income country contexts. The guidelines aim to provide actionable, evidence-based guidance to support clinicians and health systems in improving outcomes for the tens of millions of patients affected by sepsis globally each year.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026
items.summary: The abstract provided is too thin to summarize meaningfully, as it contains only background epidemiological context and a general statement about early identification, without describing the specific guideline recommendations, methods used to develop them, or findings presented in the 2026 guidelines themselves.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzanic et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise affect the expression of Toll-like receptors (TLRs), a family of immune receptors involved in triggering inflammatory responses that have been implicated in chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary lifestyles and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple databases for human studies in which exercise was the sole intervention, ultimately including studies spanning acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined training modalities. Acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, whereas acute aerobic exercise generally produced neutral or downregulatory effects, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs were predominantly associated with unchanged or decreased TLR levels, while chronic aerobic exercise produced mixed results with most measurements showing no change in expression. The authors conclude that exercise does interact with TLR signalling in a manner dependent on exercise type and duration, but substantial heterogeneity across study designs limits firm conclusions and underscores the need for further standardized research.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Explainable AI in healthcare: a systematic review of XAI use cases in imaging, diagnostics, and rehabilitation
items.summary: This systematic review examined how explainable artificial intelligence methods are being applied across healthcare domains including medical imaging, diagnostics, and rehabilitation, with the goal of clarifying which XAI techniques are used, how they pair with different data types and models, and how they support clinical understanding. The authors followed established reporting guidelines to screen a large body of literature, ultimately analyzing several dozen studies identified through multiple academic databases. They found that a clear method-modality fit has emerged in practice, with saliency and heat-map approaches such as Grad-CAM favored for spatial interpretation in imaging tasks, while feature-attribution tools such as SHAP and LIME dominate in diagnostic and rehabilitation contexts where global and case-level explanations are needed. Many studies combined two or more XAI methods to cross-validate interpretations, reflecting a trend toward more robust explanatory frameworks. The authors conclude that while current healthcare XAI practice is maturing, trustworthy clinical deployment will require standardized reporting practices, rigorous evaluation of explanation faithfulness and stability, and external validation across diverse sites.
items.citation: Apoorva Aravindkumar, Marimuthu Ramadoss, Saqhibuddeen Ahmed Fakhruddin Ahmed et al.. Explainable AI in healthcare: a systematic review of XAI use cases in imaging, diagnostics, and rehabilitation. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence. 2026

items.title: UniMate: One Unified Model to Animate Diverse Skeletons
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of generating motion for diverse 3D animated characters, where existing methods are limited by their dependence on fixed skeleton topologies or require per-skeleton fine-tuning and reference motions at test time. The authors developed UniMate, a unified diffusion-based foundation model that takes a rigged 3D asset and a text prompt as input and synthesizes articulated motion for arbitrary skeleton structures without any test-time optimization or retraining. The model employs a topology-aware diffusion transformer that encodes skeletal structure through graph-aware attention biases derived from pairwise joint relations and geodesic distances, a spectral rotary position embedding adapted to arbitrary kinematic trees via the graph Laplacian, and a global topological conditioner derived from the rest-pose skeleton. To train the model, the authors curated a large dataset spanning a wide variety of creature types and articulated objects, with unified canonicalization and text descriptions paired to motion sequences. UniMate is reported to outperform state-of-the-art baselines in quality, generalization, and efficiency, while also enabling zero-shot cross-topology transfer, motion in-betweening, expansion, and text-guided editing.
items.citation: Linzhan Mou, Jiahui Lei, Zhiyang Dou et al.. UniMate: One Unified Model to Animate Diverse Skeletons. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Two extremely irradiated volatile-rich sub-Neptunes with companions in the TOI-426 and TOI-1839 systems: Insights into arrival and survival near the lower edge of the Neptunian desert
items.summary: This study investigates two highly irradiated sub-Neptune planets, TOI-426 b and TOI-1839 b, situated near the lower boundary of the Neptunian desert—a region of parameter space where close-in planets of intermediate size are rare. Using space-based photometry and ground-based radial velocity measurements, the researchers confirmed the planets' physical properties and detected additional companions in both systems, including a long-period giant planet around TOI-426 and a transiting sub-Neptune around TOI-1839. Despite receiving extreme stellar irradiation, the densities of all three transiting planets require substantial volatile content, and atmospheric escape modeling strongly favors water-dominated rather than hydrogen/helium envelopes, supporting a steam-world interpretation. Interior structure models show that hydrogen/helium envelopes would be lost on timescales far shorter than water-dominated ones, meaning the survival of these volatile-rich planets cannot be explained by photoevaporation of primordial atmospheres alone. A population-level analysis further reveals a statistically significant excess of outer giant companions around low-mass planets near the desert edge compared to those outside it, lending support to high-eccentricity tidal migration as an important mechanism in sculpting the lower boundary of the Neptunian desert.
items.citation: A. Castro-González, O. Barragán, D. J. Armstrong et al.. Two extremely irradiated volatile-rich sub-Neptunes with companions in the TOI-426 and TOI-1839 systems: Insights into arrival and survival near the lower edge of the Neptunian desert. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Tracing the Cosmic Origins: Machine Learning Reconstruction of the Primordial Density Field from EoR Observations
items.summary: This paper investigates whether machine learning can recover the primordial density field of the Universe from observations of the Epoch of Reionization, thereby retrieving cosmological information lost to non-linear structure formation. The researchers used simulated 21-cm and CO line-intensity maps at high redshift, generated with a dedicated simulation code, as inputs to a three-dimensional U-Net architecture trained to reconstruct initial conditions at a much earlier epoch. The two tracers were chosen deliberately for their complementarity, with 21-cm emission probing diffuse neutral gas and CO probing dense star-forming regions, and realistic instrumental effects mimicking next-generation radio and millimeter surveys were incorporated. In idealized conditions, combining both tracers yielded high-fidelity reconstruction across a broad range of spatial scales, and even under realistic noise the joint reconstruction maintained meaningful correlation with the true initial field on large scales. Crucially, performing simulation-based inference of cosmological parameters on power-spectrum summaries derived from reconstructed fields substantially tightened parameter constraints compared to using unreconstructed maps, demonstrating that such joint multi-tracer reconstruction can recover otherwise inaccessible cosmological information.
items.citation: Anchal Saxena, P. Daniel Meerburg, Guochao Sun et al.. Tracing the Cosmic Origins: Machine Learning Reconstruction of the Primordial Density Field from EoR Observations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data
items.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark designed to evaluate whether AI systems can reason over longitudinal wearable sensor data from real users, an area poorly covered by existing benchmarks. The authors constructed a large set of multiple-choice questions derived from wearable time series, blood biomarkers, and demographic information spanning hundreds of days per user, preserving realistic data characteristics such as device noise and individual variability. Questions were organized across two analytical axes distinguishing data computation from physiological interpretation and single-signal from multi-signal reasoning, and were generated using a dual-grounding framework combining established physiological literature with statistically validated population-level patterns. Evaluation of a broad set of proprietary and open-source large language models revealed substantial variation in performance, with most models falling well below ceiling accuracy and the overall range spanning from near-chance to roughly three-quarters correct. The benchmark thus demonstrates both its discriminative power and the considerable gap that remains before AI systems can reliably perform health reasoning over real-world wearable data.
items.citation: Ji Soo Lee, Xilun Chen, Pierce Chuang et al.. WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Necessary or Sufficient? Evaluating LLM Explanations With Behavioural Evidence
items.summary: This paper investigates whether the explanations produced by large language models alongside their decisions actually reflect the factors that behaviorally drive those decisions. The researchers tested two distinct interpretations of explanatory factors: necessity, asking whether changing a cited factor would alter the output, and sufficiency, asking whether retaining a cited factor while removing other information would preserve the output. Using controlled black-box interventions across two synthetic tasks—recommending advisors to clients and judging prompts for harmfulness—they measured necessity and sufficiency scores for factors across eight models from three major model families and compared these scores to the models' own cited rankings. They found only moderate correlations between the cited factor rankings and the behaviorally measured scores, and in a substantial proportion of cases an uncited factor outscored the lowest-ranked cited factor, indicating that model-provided explanations do not reliably identify the most influential factors. The authors conclude that while cited explanations carry some useful signal, they cannot be trusted as reliable guides for system monitoring or oversight, and they propose their framework as a practical black-box reliability check for explanations used in agentic contexts.
items.citation: Urja Pawar, Rajitha Ramanayake, Nabeel Kemal et al.. Necessary or Sufficient? Evaluating LLM Explanations With Behavioural Evidence. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Molecular Déjà Vu: Digit-Level Retrieval of Published Values in Frontier Language Models
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language models performing well on molecular property benchmarks are genuinely predicting properties or simply retrieving memorized published values. The authors audited a substantial set of frontier language models across numerous regression benchmarks, testing for verbatim digit-level retrieval of known results. They found that verbatim retrieval is widespread but benchmark-specific, with the majority of models showing retrieval on some datasets while other datasets remain largely unaffected. Notably, reasoning level strongly influences retrieval behavior, with higher reasoning settings flagging retrieval far more frequently than lower settings on identical inputs. The study also demonstrates that suppressing retrieval narrows performance differences between models, suggesting that memorization inflates apparent capability differences and that genuine predictive ability is not simply a function of how many values a model has memorized.
items.citation: Matthias Busch, Marius Tacke, Sviatlana V. Lamaka et al.. Molecular Déjà Vu: Digit-Level Retrieval of Published Values in Frontier Language Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: STARDaki: a consensus-based STARD extension for standardized reporting of diagnostic accuracy in acute kidney injury.
items.summary: This paper addressed the problem of heterogeneous and contradictory evidence surrounding biomarkers used to predict, diagnose, and prognosticate acute kidney injury (AKI). The researchers conducted a systematic literature review of diagnostic test accuracy studies on AKI biomarkers, evaluating their methodological quality and reporting completeness using established checklists (QUADAS-2 and STARD 2015), and then convened an international expert panel to develop consensus-based reporting standards through a modified Delphi process. The review found that the vast majority of identified studies were of insufficient quality or poorly reported, with compliance with existing STARD standards too low to permit meta-analysis. In response, the expert panel developed STARDaki, an extension of the STARD checklist tailored specifically to AKI biomarker studies, incorporating agreed criteria for patient selection, reference standards, and test-retest reliability reporting. The authors conclude that current AKI biomarker research is hampered by poor reporting practices, and that adoption of STARDaki should improve the quality, clinical applicability, and generalizability of future studies in this field.
items.citation: Yu H, Li Y, Mo GP et al.. STARDaki: a consensus-based STARD extension for standardized reporting of diagnostic accuracy in acute kidney injury.. Intensive care medicine. 2026

items.title: Biomarkers for Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
items.summary: This systematic review investigated the potential of biomarkers for diagnosing, predicting, and assessing prognosis in pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome, a severe and common complication in critically ill children where early recognition remains challenging. The authors conducted a comprehensive search across nine databases and assessed study quality using established tools, extracting data on biomarker characteristics, sampling methods, and outcome measures. Nine biomarkers were identified across four pathophysiological categories — epithelial injury, stress response, inflammatory response, and endothelial injury — with the majority demonstrating strong to moderate diagnostic and predictive performance based on area under the curve values. Despite this promise, the authors found that clinical utility was inconsistent across studies, and the overall evidence base was limited to a small number of moderate-to-high quality studies involving a relatively modest cohort of critically ill children. The review concludes that large-scale, multicenter prospective studies combined with advanced technologies are needed to validate existing biomarkers and identify new candidates to improve PARDS prediction, diagnosis, and management.
items.citation: Yang F, Zou J, Zheng L et al.. Biomarkers for Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Systematic Review.. Journal of inflammation research. 2026
